What if the Waukegan house is a rental?

According to the city's rental license page, every rental inside city limits needs a license before anyone moves in. Licenses expire each December 31, the fee is $60 per rented unit, and an application needs planning and zoning pre-approval plus a passed inspection by the Building and Code Department. A code officer reaches out within five business days to schedule it.

Where tenants occupy the house, keep the license current while it is listed and tell prospective buyers about the lease early. Ask the city's License Department how the license is handled when ownership changes.

Who records a Waukegan deed, and what goes on it?

Deeds for Waukegan homes are filed in the county building at 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, with the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office (phone 847-377-2575). Its fee schedule lists a $70 standard document fee and an $82 non-standard fee, and says the only other charges at recording are state and county transfer taxes.

The county's deed packet lists what must be on the document.

  • Signed and dated by the grantor, with a notary acknowledgment
  • The buyer's address, a full legal description and the preparer's name and address
  • A "mail to" address and the name and address for tax bills
  • A completed PTAX-203 declaration or a signed exemption statement

The state tax follows 35 ILCS 200/31-10, which prints the rate as 50¢ per $500 of the value stated in the declaration, counting any fraction of $500. The same packet names six Lake County municipalities that require a local stamp before recording. Waukegan is not on that list, though the closing letter described above applies.

Frequently asked questions

Must a Waukegan seller repair every item the inspector lists?

No. The city allows an as-is sale if the buyer signs a notarized affidavit accepting the listed items. The inspection still has to be done and the certificate issued, so apply as soon as the house is listed or under agreement.

What does the Waukegan closing letter process cost?

The city lists $300 at submittal, split into a $150 zoning certificate fee and a $150 closing letter fee. Any other invoiced amounts owed to the city, including the final water bill, are settled before the letter is issued.

Do foreclosure and tax-sale transfers in Waukegan skip the certificate?

No. The city's FAQ says its ordinance lists no exemptions for transfers such as foreclosure or tax sale, so those transfers also need the application, inspection and closing letter.

Who files the deed after a Waukegan closing?

The Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office takes it, at 18 N County Street in Waukegan. Bring it in or send it by mail; the office phone is 847-377-2575.

How soon can a Waukegan cash sale close?

The city's steps set the minimum: apply at listing, at least 30 days before closing, with an inspector calling within five business days. An as-is buyer can follow that schedule, and title work sets the rest.

What makes selling a house in Cicero different from selling in other Illinois towns?

Cicero requires two local steps on nearly every home sale: Real Estate Transfer Stamps and a Certificate of Compliance. The Town's Building Department explains both on its "Buying Or Selling A Home?" page, and they affect how fast a sale can close and who ends up paying for repairs.

Cicero is a town of about 5.87 square miles in Cook County, in the Chicago area. The Census Bureau estimated 81,858 residents on July 1, 2025, down 4.0 percent from the April 2020 base of 85,294. The 2020 count works out to 14,538 people per square mile.

A seller here usually has three paths: fix everything the Town flags and sell with a certificate in hand, sell as-is and let the buyer take on the compliance work, or complete a transfer that the Town classes as exempt. Each is described below with the paperwork it needs.

How does the Cicero Certificate of Compliance work?

A Town building inspector walks the property, hands the owner a list of everything out of line with the Town Code, and the property must meet that list before a certificate is issued. The Town describes the steps as an inspection, a compliance checklist and then bringing the property up to code.

The Town treats a "transfer" broadly. It covers a deed, articles of agreement for a deed, an assignment of the beneficial interest in a land trust, using real property as loan collateral and adding a present beneficiary to a land trust. Purchasing transfer stamps is mandatory for all transfers, including those that are otherwise exempt from the compliance step.

The three ways to transfer a home in Cicero
RouteWho handles complianceWhat the Town says
Sale with a current certificateSeller, before the saleThe property already meets Town Code, so the transfer is straightforward for the buyer
As-is saleBuyer, after the purchaseThe buyer assumes responsibility for bringing the property into compliance and obtaining the certificate
Exempt transactionNo certificate neededApplies to categories such as court-ordered or familial transfers and vacant land

Source: Town of Cicero Building Department. The Town advises owners to consult its compliance staff throughout the process and to allow ample time, because the review covers multiple parts of the property.

Which Cicero transfers are exempt from the compliance step?

The Town lists four exempt categories, and for those no inspection or certificate is required. Transfer stamps are still required for every one of them.

  • Court-ordered transfers: tax deeds, sheriff's deeds and transfers made under orders of local, county, state or federal courts.
  • Vacant land: transactions involving only vacant land.
  • No change in ownership interest: transfers that do not give a new party an ownership or beneficial interest.
  • Familial transfers: adding a spouse to a deed under Section 22-281 of the Town's Code of Ordinances, in effect since March 24, 2017.

If you inherited a Cicero home and are unsure which category applies, ask the Building Department before you list. The Town Hall is at 4949 West Cermak Road, open Monday through Friday from 8 AM to 6 PM, and the main line is (708) 656-3600.

What does the state and county paperwork look like for a Cicero sale?

Cicero deeds are recorded by the Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division, and the state transfer tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the declaration. That rate is set in 35 ILCS 200/31-10.

The Clerk's office records and maintains land records, lets the public search them by property index number or party name, and runs a Property Fraud Unit that helps owners investigate suspicious filings against their property. It is open 9 am to 5 pm and takes its last customer at 4:45 pm. The Town's page does not print a stamp amount, so ask the Building Department what the stamps cost and ask your title company which other charges appear on the closing statement.

On the disclosure side, Illinois law requires the seller of residential property to complete a report and give it to the buyer before the contract is signed. Section 20 of the Residential Real Property Disclosure Act sets that rule, and the report asks about basement leakage, roof and foundation defects, radon, lead paint and lead pipes, among other items. A house that needs work can still be sold in as-is condition, but the questions still have to be answered honestly.

What does the Cicero housing market look like in Census data?

Cicero is a town of renters and owners in nearly equal measure, and its homes are family-sized. Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024 put owner occupancy at 54.6 percent, the median value of an owner-occupied unit at $249,400 and median gross rent at $1,154.

The same tables count 24,432 households averaging 3.36 people, higher than in Chicago, Crystal Lake or Danville. Median household income is $70,842, 95.0 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 79.8 percent speak a language other than English at home. Hispanic or Latino residents are 87.5 percent of the population and 40.6 percent of residents are foreign-born.

Those numbers describe a long-tenured community with large households, which is the group most likely to be shopping for a family-sized house.

How did Cicero get its shape, schools and transit?

Cicero was incorporated on February 28, 1867, and it once covered far more ground. The original Cicero Township was about six times the size of today's town, until Oak Park and Berwyn were carved out and areas such as Austin were annexed by Chicago. The old Hawthorne Works factory employed more than 40,000 people at its peak, and the area long had a Czech and Bohemian character along what was then 22nd Street, now Cermak Road.

Cicero Elementary School District 99 operates 16 schools, which makes it one of the largest districts outside Chicago. High school students attend schools in J. Sterling Morton High School District 201, and Morton College is in town. Two private Catholic schools serve grades pre-K through 8.

For commuters, Cicero sits on two freight rail lines, the BNSF Railway and the Belt Railway of Chicago. The Metra BNSF Line stops near Cicero Avenue and 26th Street, the CTA Pink Line runs from its 54th/Cermak terminal to the Loop, and several Pace and CTA bus routes cross town.

Which Cook County tax items should a Cicero seller check?

Check whether the house has the Homeowner Exemption on its tax bill before closing. The Cook County Assessor says the exemption cuts the equalized assessed value by $10,000, renews automatically once granted, and requires that you own and live in the home as your principal residence.

  • Seniors 65 or older may also qualify for the Senior Exemption.
  • The Senior Freeze has an income limit of $65,000 or less for calendar year 2024 and must be filed each year.
  • Missing exemptions for tax years 2021 through 2025 can be redeemed with a Certificate of Error.

Taxes in Illinois are billed in installments, and the second installment bill shows the exemptions that were applied. At the closing table, ask the title company to show how the current year's bill is split between you and the buyer, and whether any installment is still unpaid.

What costs should a Cicero seller weigh in a cash offer?

The main question is whether a buyer who takes the house as-is leaves you with more or less than repairing it for the Town and listing it. A compliance checklist can include items you would never fix for your own use, so get the inspection list first, price the work with a contractor, and then compare it with the cash number.

  • Total of the repair bids needed to earn a certificate.
  • Months of mortgage, utility and tax payments while the house is listed.
  • Who buys the transfer stamps and who pays for the compliance inspection.
  • Whether the contract states plainly that the buyer will obtain the certificate after closing.

Put every figure side by side before deciding. A quick, certain closing is worth something, but only you can say how much.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a Certificate of Compliance to sell my Cicero house?

Usually yes, unless the transfer is exempt. The Town lets you sell with a current certificate or sell as-is, in which case the buyer takes on the work of obtaining it after the purchase.

Are transfer stamps required for every Cicero sale?

Yes. The Town says Real Estate Transfer Stamps are required for all real estate transfers, even those that are exempt from the compliance step.

Can I sell a Cicero house with code violations?

Yes, through an as-is sale. The buyer assumes responsibility for bringing the property into compliance, so the price usually reflects what the Town's checklist would require.

Who records the deed for a Cicero home?

The Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division records it. Your title company or attorney normally files the deed along with the state transfer declaration.

Is adding my spouse to the deed treated as a sale in Cicero?

It counts as a transfer, but the Town lists adding a spouse to a deed under Section 22-281 as an exempt familial transfer. No inspection or certificate is required, though the transfer stamps are.

Why is Bloomington a steady housing market compared with other Illinois cities?

Bloomington is the McLean County seat in central Illinois, laid out in 1831 after the county was created in December 1830. It grew from a settlement called Keg Grove, later Blooming Grove, and a fire in 1900 destroyed most of downtown, which was quickly rebuilt from local architects' designs. Insurance did the most to shape the modern city: State Farm was founded here in June 1922, and the city's 2018 financial report lists State Farm as its largest employer, followed by Illinois State University in neighboring Normal, Country Financial, McLean County Unit District No. 5, Carle Bromenn Medical Center and OSF St. Joseph Medical Center.

Bloomington covers 27.24 square miles, and its Census count rose from 76,610 in 2010 to 78,680 in 2020. Those employers draw buyers from the Bloomington-Normal area as a whole, so a listing here is read next to Normal houses too.

What do Census figures show about Bloomington homes?

The Census Bureau estimates 78,804 residents for July 1, 2025, up 0.1 percent from the April 2020 base of 78,688. Close to half of adults age 25 and over hold a bachelor's degree, and the average commute is short.

Households average 2.20 people and the typical commute is 16.8 minutes, so buyers shopping on location, school district and monthly cost will compare your house with others in both Bloomington and Normal.

Which school districts and amenities shape Bloomington buyer interest?

Two public districts cover the city. Bloomington Public Schools District 87 serves the interior with Bloomington High School, Bloomington Junior High and six elementary schools (Oakland, Washington, Bent, Irving, Sheridan and Stevenson) plus a preschool. Growth pushed the city well into McLean County Unit District No. 5, which runs Normal Community High School and Normal Community West High School and now enrolls most of its students from Bloomington itself. A small part of the city lies in Olympia Community Unit School District 16, and Central Catholic High School is a private option.

  • Parks: the Parks and Recreation Department maintains over 1,100 acres across 44 park sites and three golf courses, plus Miller Park Zoo.
  • Trails: the 24-mile Constitution Trail follows former railroad right-of-way through much of the city.
  • Colleges: Illinois Wesleyan University (founded 1850) is in the city, and Illinois State University is in Normal.
  • Culture: the Bloomington Center for the Performing Arts anchors the downtown Cultural District.

Because the school district can differ from one block to the next, confirm the district for your address before writing the listing description.

How do Interstates, rail and air access affect Bloomington sellers?

Interstates 39, 55 and 74 intersect at Bloomington, and US 51, US 150 and Illinois Route 9 also pass through. Historic US 66 once ran directly through downtown and later on a bypass to the east.

Amtrak serves the area from Uptown Station in neighboring Normal, with five trains in each direction daily between St. Louis and Chicago, and Greyhound and Burlington Trailways add bus links. Central Illinois Regional Airport on Route 9 has flights on Delta, American Eagle, Frontier and Allegiant. Connect Transit runs 13 fixed bus routes. These details matter when you market to out-of-town buyers or employees transferring in.

What must Bloomington owners know if the house is a rental?

Anyone who owns residential rental property inside the city limits must register it with the city and hold a Certificate of Inspection before renting or leasing a unit. This affects sellers because the city's rules shape what a buyer inherits.

  • Registration costs $65 per building, plus $5 per rental unit in buildings of three or more units, and each owned condo needs its own registration.
  • Registrations run until December 31 each year and cannot be transferred to new owners, so a buyer must register on their own.
  • The first inspection is included in the registration fee. Follow-up inspections are $100 each and a missed inspection costs $75.
  • Owners get at least 15 days' notice, and inspectors enforce the International Property Maintenance Code, the Fire Code and other city ordinances.
  • A building rated fair may be required to post a $5,000 letter of credit or pledged account until it receives a passing rating.
  • Violations not fixed by the reinspection date lead to a court appearance and possible court costs.

Owners who rent short term face a 6.0 percent city Short Term Rental Tax on stays under 30 days, with remittance due by the 25th of the following month and a 5 percent penalty for late payments. Those operators must also register the unit annually in the rental program. Sellers of a rental should settle any unpaid tax or inspection issue before closing. A cash buyer will often take on a tenant-occupied or violation-heavy property as-is, which can avoid a repair-and-reinspect cycle.

How are deeds recorded in McLean County?

The McLean County Clerk's office handles recording at 115 E. Washington Street, Bloomington, and its Predictable Recording Fee Schedule effective July 1, 2023 lists a standard document at $61.00. Documents exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee, such as government filings and powers of attorney, are $41.00, and a non-standard document is $75.00. A document counts as non-standard if it uses legal- or ledger-size paper or has six or more PIN or related-document references. Recorded documents must be originals or certified copies. Certified copies cost $18.00 and additional copies $1.00 per page.

The county's phone for recording is (309) 888-5170. The state transfer declaration and any transfer tax are separate from the recording fee. Your title company will collect them at closing, so ask for an itemized settlement statement.

How does McLean County handle assessment complaints and tax bills in Bloomington?

Taxpayers have 30 days from the publication date shown for their township to file an assessment complaint with the Board of Review, and a late complaint will not be heard. For 2026, the county table shows the Bloomington and City of Bloomington townships published on September 29, 2026 with a filing deadline of October 29, 2026, so that window has closed. The equalization factors for those townships were 1.0534 and 1.0385.

The county uses Form PTAX-230 for non-farm complaints. The assessment is based on the past three years' market value before January 1 of the assessment year, with a multiplier applied to bring the statutory assessment to 33.33 percent. The City of Bloomington Township Assessor keeps property record cards and a lookup tool, and the Board of Review office can be reached at (309) 888-5132. For future cycles, check the county's table for your township's publication and deadline dates, and ask the County Treasurer for installment dates and a payoff figure before closing.

Frequently asked questions

Can a new owner use the previous owner's Bloomington rental registration?

No. Bloomington's rental program says registrations cannot be transferred to new owners. A buyer who plans to rent must register the building, pay the registration fee and pass inspection.

What does it cost to record a deed in McLean County?

The county's schedule effective July 1, 2023 lists $61.00 for a standard document and $75.00 for a non-standard one. Fees can change, so confirm with the County Clerk before sending payment.

Did the 2026 Bloomington appeal window close?

Yes. McLean County's table shows a filing deadline of October 29, 2026 for the Bloomington and City of Bloomington townships, and late complaints are not heard. The same 30-days-from-publication rule applies in later years.

Is the short-term rental tax applied to every Bloomington short-term stay?

The city's FAQ applies a 6.0 percent tax to rentals of less than 30 days and lists no exemptions. Operators who use a listing site must still register each property and file monthly certification forms.

Does a cash sale remove the need to fix rental violations in Bloomington?

The city's rules still apply to whoever owns the building, but a cash buyer may agree to buy as-is and handle repairs and reinspection after closing. Settle fees or court matters tied to your ownership first, and get any sale terms in writing.

How can you sell a house quickly in Schaumburg?

Schaumburg homeowners can move fast by pricing a listing to sell, by selling privately, or by accepting a direct purchase from a buyer who closes with cash. The direct sale trims the most time, since it skips repairs, staging and the weeks a lender needs. What cannot be skipped is the village's transfer stamp, which gates the closing in Schaumburg.

What should a seller know about Schaumburg itself?

Schaumburg is a village in Cook and DuPage counties, about 26 miles northwest of downtown Chicago and 10 miles northwest of O'Hare International Airport. At the 2020 census it had 78,723 residents, which made it the most populous incorporated village in the United States. It covers about 19.5 square miles and was incorporated on March 7, 1956.

Growth came fast. The O'Hare opening in 1955 and the Northwest Tollway in 1956 improved access, then Alfred Campanelli began the Weathersfield subdivision in 1959 and eventually built more than 6,800 housing units. Woodfield Mall opened in 1971. Most of the village was built out between the 1960s and the 1990s, so many Schaumburg sellers are selling a house or unit with decades of wear on its roof, windows and mechanicals.

The Olde Schaumburg Centre Overlay District, set up in 1978, protects the historic area around Schaumburg and Roselle Roads.

What do Census numbers show for Schaumburg housing?

Schaumburg at 77,249 residents on July 1, 2025, with 31,655 households averaging 2.41 people from 2020 to 2024. Only 62.9% of housing units are owner-occupied, so renters make up a large share of the village.

How do jobs and commuting shape demand in Schaumburg?

Schaumburg is a job center in its own right. The village website lists Woodfield Mall as the top employer at 4,400 workers, followed by Zurich North America at 2,600, Motorola Solutions at 1,600 and OptumRx at 1,300, with IBM, Genworth Financial and Paylocity also on the list. Many Japanese companies have their U.S. headquarters in Schaumburg and nearby Hoffman Estates.

Census data shows a mean commute of 27.8 minutes. The Metra Milwaukee District West Line runs between Elgin and Chicago Union Station with a Schaumburg stop near Wintrust Field, and Pace buses meet at the Northwest Transportation Center near Woodfield Mall with service toward Rosemont and Elgin. The village also owns Schaumburg Regional Airport, a general aviation field on Irving Park Road. Buyers who work along the I-90 and Golf Road corridor tend to put proximity first.

Which schools serve Schaumburg homes?

Most of the village falls in Community Consolidated School District 54 for elementary and middle grades and in Township High School District 211, which runs five high schools: Schaumburg, Hoffman Estates, Conant, Fremd and Palatine. Schaumburg High School received about $20 million in renovation work completed in 2017.

Private options in the village include Schaumburg Christian School, St. Peter Lutheran School and St. Hubert Catholic School. Roosevelt University has a Schaumburg campus in the former Pure Oil headquarters building, and the Schaumburg Township District Library has its main branch here. Not every District 54 school sits inside the village, so check the attendance boundary for the address you are selling.

How does the climate affect houses in Schaumburg?

Schaumburg has four seasons with cold, snowy winters and warm, wet summers. Climate normals show about 39.6 inches of precipitation a year and 38.4 inches of snow, with the heaviest rain from April through August. January daily highs average near 32 degrees Fahrenheit and July highs near 84.

The village also sits at the headwaters of the West Branch DuPage River, with the east side draining through West Branch Salt Creek toward Busse Lake. In practice that means drainage and sump pump health deserve attention before listing, and the village's permit services publish a drain tile and drainage resource guide for homeowners who need work done.

What local rules apply before a Schaumburg house can close?

Schaumburg ties its transfer stamp to the condition of vacant homes. Since a 2015 ordinance change, every vacant single-family home is subject to an interior and exterior inspection before the real estate tax transfer stamp is released. The inspection fee is $100, paid when you schedule at the Community Development permit counter, and once the fee is in, the village says an inspection can usually be set within 3 business days.

If the inspection finds violations that are not corrected, the buyer must provide a notarized letter of intent before the stamp is released. Other holds on the stamp for the property must also be cleared first. Questions go to the Building Division at 847-923-4420.

Vacant homes must also be registered under Chapter 123.04 of the Village Code. There is no registration fee. Minimum upkeep includes cutting grass before it passes eight inches, removing dead shrubs, clearing accumulated mail and notices, replacing broken windows or doors, keeping sump pumps working and weatherizing the property. Code Enforcement can be reached at 847-923-3700.

What transfer taxes and recording steps apply in Schaumburg?

Illinois sets the state stamp at 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction under 35 ILCS 200/31-15, and a deed cannot be accepted for filing without the stamps under 35 ILCS 200/31-20. For the Cook County side of the village, the Cook County Clerk lists the state rate at $0.50 per $500 and the county rate at $0.25 per $500, with the seller as the liable party.

Part of Schaumburg lies in DuPage County, so the first task is to look up the parcel number and confirm which county records the deed. Ask the title company or the recording office for the exact stamp amount and any municipal charge, since the village's real estate tax transfer stamp is a separate item from the state and county stamps.

How do Schaumburg property tax bills work for a seller?

Cook County parcels are billed in two installments. The Cook County Treasurer lists the tax year 2025 first installment as due April 1, 2026 and the second as due October 1, 2026, and the earlier tax year 2024 installments as March 4, 2025 and December 15, 2025. Because those dates moved from earlier years, ask the Treasurer or your title company what is paid and what remains open on your parcel.

Two practical points apply to a quick sale. The title company prorates the year's bill between you and the buyer on the closing statement, and the Treasurer's exemption list includes the Homeowner Exemption and senior programs the buyer may need to claim. For a DuPage parcel, ask the DuPage County Treasurer for the matching schedule.

Does Schaumburg require an inspection to sell a house?

Only for vacant single-family homes. They need an interior and exterior inspection before the transfer stamp is released, and the fee is $100 paid when you schedule. Occupied homes are not covered by that rule on the village's page.

How long does the Schaumburg vacant home inspection take?

The village says it can usually be scheduled within 3 business days after the $100 fee is paid. Call the Building Division at 847-923-4420 to confirm timing before you set a closing date.

What happens if the inspection finds problems?

Uncorrected violations require a notarized letter of intent from the buyer before the tax stamp is released. Other holds on the property must also be corrected first.

Do I have to register a vacant house in Schaumburg?

Yes. Vacant buildings must be registered under Chapter 123.04 of the Village Code, and there is no fee. You return the Vacant Building Registration Form and keep the lawn, windows, sump pump and exterior in order.

Which county records a Schaumburg deed?

It depends on the parcel, because Schaumburg lies in both Cook and DuPage counties. Check the parcel number, then file with that county's recording office along with the required state and county stamps.

What are the realistic routes to a quick sale in Evanston, Illinois?

Three routes work in Evanston: put the house on the market, sell it without an agent, or hand it to a buyer who takes it as-is. Which one is quickest depends less on the buyer than on the city's paperwork, because every closing needs the city's transfer stamp before a deed can be recorded.

  • A full listing exposes the house to the widest pool of buyers and usually the best price, in exchange for showings, repair requests and lender timelines.
  • An owner-managed sale keeps the agent fee in your pocket while you handle pricing, the contract and disclosures.
  • An as-is purchase trims showings and repair negotiation, and the closing date is often something you can agree on directly.

Houses with tenants, deferred maintenance or an estate behind them tend to fit the as-is route. A tidy house with months of runway often does better on the open market.

What does the Evanston housing picture look like?

Evanston is a lakefront suburb that QuickFacts lists at 76,380 residents in mid-2025, a little below the 78,110 counted in 2020. It touches Chicago along Howard Street and sits roughly 12 miles north of the Loop on Lake Michigan, so the housing stock runs from older frame houses and brick two-flats to condominiums and high-rises near the water.

The 2020 to 2024 median home value for owner-occupied housing at $481,200. Owners live in 56.2 percent of the homes, which leaves a large renter share, and there are 31,705 households. Rent in the same estimate has a median of $1,762 a month, and the average commute is 27.5 minutes. A median is a citywide middle, so a bungalow far from the lake and a condo near the downtown stops can price very differently.

Northwestern University is the dominant employer. A 2015 employer list showed 9,471 jobs at the university, 3,727 at NorthShore University HealthSystem and 1,600 in District 65. Evanston has several shopping and dining strips, including downtown near Davis Street, Central Street, Dempster Street, Main Street and Howard Street, and both Metra and CTA stations serve parts of them.

How do Evanston's school districts figure into a sale?

Two public districts cover the entire city, and a buyer will want to know which elementary school serves your address. Evanston-Skokie School District 65 teaches pre-kindergarten through eighth grade, and Evanston Township High School, the only high school in District 202, teaches grades 9 through 12 to a little over 4,000 students.

District 65 operates ten elementary schools, three middle schools, two magnet schools, two special schools or centers and an early childhood school. The district office can tell you the attendance area for a given address. Montessori schools and a parish school with grades from pre-kindergarten to eighth also operate in the city.

Northwestern University sits inside the city limits, and the school district boundaries are separate from the campus area, so confirm your address with the district directly.

How much is the Evanston transfer tax, and how is the stamp issued?

Evanston's real estate transfer tax is usually paid by the seller, though the contract can say otherwise, and the stamp has to be issued before a deed is recorded. The tax dates to 1986 and feeds the city's General Fund.

Evanston transfer tax by sale price, from the City of Evanston finance page
Price bandCharge per $1,000
$1,500,000 or less$5
Above $1,500,000, through $5,000,000$7
Above $5,000,000$9

Stamps are electronic. The practical timeline looks like this:

  • File the stamp request through the city's online service portal or the 311 line. Counter requests are not taken.
  • Plan to file seven to ten business days ahead of closing. The city needs five business days to process, counted from the day after receipt, and it does not rush requests.
  • Complete the Evanston declaration form and add it, with any backup documents, to your service request.
  • A final water bill is created automatically with the request, except for condominiums and vacant land.
  • The stamp is released only once the paperwork checks out and everything you owe the city is paid.

A stamp for an exempt transaction costs $100. Payment rules tighten as the stamp amount grows. Between $5,000 and $50,000 the city will not accept personal or attorney checks, and at $50,000 or more only a cashier's check or wire works. The City Collector's office confirms the current rate and accepted payment types before you schedule a closing.

Do Evanston's rental registration and short-term rental rules change a sale?

They can, because a rental house carries registration and inspection duties that a buyer will ask about. Under Ordinance 141-O-18, long-term rentals of single-unit homes, condominiums, multi-unit buildings and accessory dwelling units are registered annually.

New registrations cost $200 plus $12 per unit, and annual renewals cost $12 per unit. Owner-occupied units, buildings registered as vacant, shared housing providers and units used only for short-term stays are exempt, although in a building with several units only the owner's own unit is covered by that exemption. Inspection frequency depends on the last result: within five years when no violations were found, within three when up to seven were found, and within one year when more than seven or an infestation turned up.

Stays under 30 consecutive days fall under the separate short-term rental license. New applicants pay $150 to apply and $250 a year, and the unit must pass a property maintenance inspection first. A buyer who wants to host guests should check this before making an offer, and a condo buyer may need a letter from the association confirming that its bylaws permit short stays. If you rent the house today, gather your registration confirmation and latest inspection report for the buyer.

How can permits and unfinished projects slow an Evanston closing?

Unpermitted work can surface in a buyer's inspection or a lender's review, so sort out permit status before you list. Building and Development Services handles permits, inspections and property maintenance enforcement for the city.

The city has adopted the 2021 international building, residential, existing building, property maintenance, mechanical, fuel gas and fire codes with local amendments, and it adopted the 2023 Illinois Stretch Energy Code. Permit applications received on or after October 1, 2025 must follow the Stretch Code, which matters if you are finishing a renovation to improve your sale price.

  • Collect permit records and final sign-offs for any addition, deck, finished basement or mechanical upgrade.
  • If something was built without a permit, ask the permit desk what the city will require before you list.
  • Resolve any cited maintenance violation before the closing date.

When repairs make no financial sense, an as-is buyer can take on the open items, as long as the purchase contract states clearly who is responsible.

How do Cook County assessments and appeals touch an Evanston seller?

Cook County, not the city, values Evanston homes and bills their property tax. For a residential property, the assessed value is generally 10 percent of the Assessor's estimated market value, and the Assessor does not set levies, rates or bills.

Appeals cost nothing and can be filed online in as little as 20 minutes. The usual window is 30 days after the reassessment notice, with the last day printed on the notice, and the appeal calendar by township is on the Assessor's website. The Assessor's guidance is that an appeal rarely changes the bill much when the listed characteristics are accurate and the estimated value is within 10 percent of what you believe the home is worth.

A fresh purchase price does not always match the Assessor's estimate, because the office values every property with the same method. Your closing agent or attorney prorates the tax bill at settlement. For payment status or refund questions, contact the Cook County Treasurer.

Frequently asked questions

Is it possible to close on an Evanston house in under a month?

Yes, an as-is purchase can close within a few weeks, though the city timeline sets a floor. File the transfer stamp request seven to ten business days before closing, and allow five business days for processing.

Which party covers the Evanston transfer tax?

The seller normally covers it, unless the contract assigns it elsewhere. The city prints $5 per $1,000 up to $1,500,000, then $7 through $5,000,000, then $9 beyond that.

Must a landlord register an Evanston rental before a sale?

Registration is an annual requirement for long-term rentals under Ordinance 141-O-18, so keep it current. Owner-occupied units, buildings registered as vacant and units used only for short-term stays are exempt.

Is an as-is sale possible for an Evanston house with open repairs?

Yes. The stamp still requires verified documents and payment of what you owe the city, including the final water bill, so settle those even if the buyer takes the repairs.

Which office should I ask about an Evanston tax bill?

Ask the Cook County Assessor about valuation and appeals, and the Cook County Treasurer about the bill itself. The City of Evanston does not set the amount.

What kind of place is Arlington Heights for a home seller?

Arlington Heights lies in Cook County roughly 25 miles northwest of the Loop, and a sliver of the village reaches into Lake County. Its 16.61 square miles are almost entirely developed, so a seller here competes with other established blocks.

The 2020 count was 77,676 people, the 15th largest municipality in the state. The July 2025 Census estimate of 76,216 sits 1.9% under that base, and one resident in five is 65 or older.

The village's history page calls the downtown Metra station the anchor of a walkable district of shops, restaurants and entertainment.

How did Arlington Heights grow, and why does that matter for an older house?

The settlement started as Dunton, a depot stop, and took the name Arlington Heights in 1874. Farms and greenhouses covered most of the ground into the postwar years.

Then came the 1950s and 1960s. Automobiles, the baby boom and a string of annexations lifted the count to 64,884 by 1970, by which time nearly all open land was gone. A house from those decades draws close attention from inspectors at the roof deck, the electrical panel, the supply piping and the basement walls.

  • Request the village permit file for your address.
  • Collect paperwork showing when the furnace, water heater and roof were replaced.
  • Find out whether a finished lower level or an addition went through permitting when it was built.

What do parks and local landmarks add to a listing?

The Arlington Heights Park District owns 456.53 acres and leases another 258.56 acres across 58 parks. Lake Arlington, a human-made 50-acre detention lake, sits inside a 93-acre park with a 1.8-mile path around the water, and the district also runs pools, courts, golf courses and a senior center.

Downtown has the Metropolis Performing Arts Centre, which opened in 1999, and the Arlington Heights Memorial Library, where 63.5 percent of residents held cards in 2014. Mitsuwa Marketplace, the largest Japanese supermarket in the Midwest, is in the village. Frontier Days at Recreation Park, held before Independence Day, draws a carnival and a parade.

Mention whatever is closest to your house, since a short walk to a park or the station is the kind of detail a buyer remembers.

What does the local economy look like?

The Census Bureau's 2022 figures put retail sales in Arlington Heights at $1.67 billion, health care and social assistance receipts at $1.57 billion, and accommodation and food service sales at $221 million. Retail works out to $22,237 per resident, well above the figure for Aurora or Batavia.

About two thirds of residents 16 and older are in the labor force, and 60.4% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. The share of residents born abroad is 21.5%, and 28.8% of residents speak a language other than English at home.

What is going on with the Arlington Park property?

The former racetrack at 3200 W. Euclid Ave. covers 326 acres, and the Chicago Bears Football Club bought it in February 2023. The village keeps a redevelopment page for it, and that page carries a statement that the team announced it would focus on a stadium opportunity in Indiana.

The village adds that it still regards the property as a highly viable redevelopment site because of its size, transportation access and place in the northwest suburbs. For a seller nearby, the future use of that land is unsettled. Buyers will ask what you know, so read the current village page and answer from it.

Which school districts serve Arlington Heights homes?

Elementary and middle students in most of the village attend Arlington Heights School District 25, and District 214 runs the high schools. Parts of the village belong instead to Districts 15, 21, 23, 57 or 59, which means two neighbors can have different schools.

  • South Middle School and Thomas Middle School are District 25 schools.
  • John Hersey High School is the only public high school inside village limits; some areas feed Buffalo Grove, Prospect, Rolling Meadows or Wheeling, and a few feed Palatine High School in District 211.

Verify the assignment for the exact street before writing it into a listing.

Can a buyer use the house as a short-term rental in Arlington Heights?

Not for stays under 30 consecutive days. The Village Board's March 2, 2026 ordinance set a 30-day minimum on all residential rentals, effective July 1, 2026, and it did not grandfather existing short-term rentals. Shorter stays count as nuisances, and the village acts on complaints.

Hotels, motels and lodging rooms are exempt. Sellers get a carve-out: if the rental agreement is signed along with the contract to sell, a seller may stay on after closing for fewer than 30 consecutive days. Ask the closing attorney to draft it that way.

What do permits and building codes mean when you sell?

Permits run through the Building & Life Safety Department and its online Civic Access Portal, where applicants can track a permit, book inspections and upload documents. The counter is open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays, with a 9:30 a.m. start on the first and third Wednesday, and the phone is 847-368-5560.

Work may take place between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. on weekdays and between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. on weekends. The village has adopted the 2024 International codes, replacing 2018 editions, with an effective date of January 1, 2027, and the department tells applicants to read the updated requirements before submitting.

How are the deed and transfer tax handled on an Arlington Heights sale?

State transfer tax is paid with revenue stamps bought through the county recorder. Both sides sign the PTAX-203 declaration, filed where the parcel is. Whether a county or home rule municipality adds a charge of its own is a question for the title company.

In Cook County, the Clerk's schedule prices a deed at $107, a total that bundles recording, GIS, storage, state housing and filer fees, and that schedule has applied since April 1, 2024. The Lake County slice of the village records with that county.

When does a cash sale make sense for an Arlington Heights house?

Cash works when the roof or kitchen is dated, when an estate or divorce sets the clock, or when months of showings and loan approvals are not an option. The trade is simple: speed and certainty in exchange for the price a fully updated listing might reach.

  • Line up any offer against what a listing would put in your pocket after agent fees and repairs.
  • Ask who covers the title search and recording, and get it in the contract.
  • Confirm the day of closing, plus what happens to utilities and your belongings that day.

A signed purchase agreement, a title commitment and a clear closing statement protect you on either route.

Frequently asked questions

How fast can an Arlington Heights cash sale close?

It can close on whatever date the contract names, since no lender has to approve anything. Recording in Cook County runs through the County Clerk, so give the title company time to prepare the deed.

Must I repair the house first?

No, but open permits deserve attention. Pull the record from Building & Life Safety and finalize anything unfinished. Cosmetic work is optional when you sell as-is.

Can I stay in the house after closing?

Yes, for a short time. The village lets a buyer and seller sign a rental agreement of under 30 consecutive days if it is executed together with the contract to sell. Without that paper, short stays at a residential rental are treated as nuisances.

Who writes the check for transfer taxes?

Whatever the contract says, so read that clause. Your title company can itemize each tax and name the party responsible.

Where does my deed get recorded?

At the recorder for the parcel's county. That is the Cook County Clerk for most of the village and Lake County for the small piece there. Look up your parcel number to be sure.

Three paths lead to a Bolingbrook closing: a listing, a sale you run yourself, or a direct purchase by an investor taking the property in its current condition. The route changes your timeline and net proceeds, yet the village's stamp office sits at the end of all three.

  • An agent listing draws the most showings, and you wait while a buyer's lender finishes underwriting.
  • A sale by owner keeps the commission in your pocket and hands you the contract, deed and village errands.
  • A direct purchase trims showings and repair negotiations, and the price usually reflects that convenience.

Get any offer in writing, with proof of funds or a loan approval attached, and find out who orders and pays for the title search before you sign.

How did Bolingbrook's neighborhoods come about?

Bolingbrook lies roughly 28 miles southwest of downtown Chicago, across Will County and DuPage County, and it incorporated on October 6, 1965. Nearly every home, church and business there went up after 1960, though the first settlement dates to 1831.

Westbury, west of Route 53, was the first subdivision, and Colonial Village followed on the far side of that road. Growth in the 1970s was dramatic: the 1970 census counted 7,651 people and 1980 counted 37,261, helped by mass annexation. The 2000 count was 56,321, the 2010 count 73,366 and the 2020 count 73,922. The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 74,803.

Houses from the 1970s through the 1990s are now old enough that roofs, furnaces and water heaters reach the end of their lives together. That cluster of repairs is the usual reason an owner here looks at an as-is sale.

What does QuickFacts say about Bolingbrook's homes?

Bolingbrook homeowners sitting on a typical home value of $314,700 for 2020 through 2024, with owners occupying 79.1 percent of housing units. The village counts 23,959 households averaging 3.08 people.

Which school districts reach Bolingbrook addresses?

Valley View Community Unit School District 365U covers most of Bolingbrook, but a handful of districts claim slices of it, so the exact address decides what a family hears. On the Will County side, parts belong to Indian Prairie CUSD 204, Plainfield CCSD 202 and Naperville CUSD 203. In DuPage County the portions fall under Woodridge School District 68 and Community High School District 99.

  • Bolingbrook High School belongs to Valley View.
  • Plainfield North and Plainfield East serve some addresses.
  • Neuqua Valley, Naperville Central and Downers Grove South serve others.

Fountaindale Public Library District covers most of the village. A listing that names the right district up front saves a buyer from checking boundary maps.

What do the highways and bus lines mean for a Bolingbrook buyer?

Interstate 55, the Stevenson Expressway, runs through the southern end, Interstate 355 hugs the east edge, and Route 53 (Bolingbrook Drive) divides the village north from south. Local streets such as Boughton Road, Veterans Parkway, Weber Road and Remington Boulevard carry the rest of the traffic.

Pace route 834 serves the village, and routes 755, 850 and 851 run express to Chicago using the I-55 shoulder with park-and-ride stops. The Metra Heritage Corridor stops in neighboring Romeoville with weekday rush-hour service. The average one-way commute is 30 minutes.

Employers add demand. Ulta Beauty and WeatherTech are headquartered in the village, and Wikipedia counts 24 corporate headquarters as of 2019.

What local landmarks can a Bolingbrook listing mention?

Valley View, the district serving most of the village, was the first school district in the United States to adopt the 45-15 plan, in which schools ran year-round with about three-quarters of students in session at a time. Bolingbrook's earliest school, North View on Briarcliff Road, is now closed.

Hubert H. Humphrey Middle School sits near The Promenade Bolingbrook shopping district, and Jane Addams Middle School is near the Bolingbrook Recreation and Aquatic Center. Tiny Boardman Cemetery, in the Heritage Creek subdivision, holds early residents from the 1830s farming settlement. Buyers who ask about the neighborhood respond well to specifics like these.

What does Bolingbrook require before issuing a transfer stamp?

The village sells its own stamp at $7.50 per $1,000 of price, with the cost split equally between buyer and seller, and it will not issue one until the property is clear of all village debts. The guideline words the base as "per $1,000.00 or fraction rounded to the next highest $500.00 of purchase price."

  • The original executed deed and a copy of the PTAX-203 transfer declaration.
  • A clearance letter listing any debts owed to the village.
  • The Residential Transfer Information and Disclosure form, signed by seller and buyer only, with a power of attorney if someone signs for either.
  • Payment by cash, credit card, check or money order, weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30.

Expect a turnaround of 24 to 48 hours, and note that the stamp is good for only five business days, so time the pickup near closing. Exempt transfers need the deed with the exemption wording, a village Certificate of Exemption and a $50 fee. The zoning office, (630) 226-8460, can answer questions about the disclosure form.

Where does a Bolingbrook deed get recorded?

Recording happens in the county where the parcel sits, Will or DuPage, so look at your tax bill to see which office to use. The Illinois Department of Revenue says buyer and seller complete the PTAX-203 and file it with that county, and that a county may charge its own transfer tax on top of the state's.

The state revenue stamp is priced at 50 cents per $500 of value under 35 ILCS 200/31-15. For the tax proration at closing, ask the county treasurer on your parcel for the installment dates and the latest bill.

How does Bolingbrook's weather show up in a home inspection?

Bolingbrook has a hot-summer humid continental climate, and NOAA data cited on Wikipedia show about 39.94 inches of precipitation a year, with January afternoons averaging 31.5 degrees and July afternoons 84.4. The village lies in the Gateway Wetlands, a stretch that runs from Downers Grove toward Joliet.

Inspectors for buyers therefore look hard at sump pumps, grading, gutters and basement walls. Servicing a sump pump or patching a roof before listing can keep a buyer's report short, while an as-is buyer simply prices whatever turns up.

How much does a Bolingbrook transfer stamp cost?

The village prints $7.50 per $1,000, with liability split equally between buyer and seller. Its guideline says the amount is figured per $1,000 or fraction rounded up to the next $500 of the purchase price.

Can a Bolingbrook closing proceed if the village is owed money?

No. The village requires the property to be clear of all debts before it issues a stamp, and the clearance letter shows what is owed, so those items need to be paid first.

Is Bolingbrook in Will County or DuPage County?

Both. The village straddles the two, and the county where your parcel lies records the deed and receives the PTAX-203.

Which school district serves my Bolingbrook house?

Most addresses are in Valley View 365U. Some are in Indian Prairie 204, Plainfield 202, Naperville 203, Woodridge 68 or Community High School District 99, so confirm the parcel with the district.

Would a cash offer suit a Bolingbrook house that needs repairs?

It can, when repair bills and carrying costs outweigh the gap in price. Weigh the net amount after repairs, months on the market and closing costs, and get the terms written down before you commit.

Selling in Decatur?

Which sales routes work for a Decatur homeowner?

Three routes are open: hire an agent, handle the sale yourself, or hand the keys to a cash buyer who accepts the house with its flaws. Your timeline and the condition of the roof, furnace and foundation usually settle which one fits.

  • An agent listing rewards a tidy house and a patient owner, because showings, an appraisal and a buyer's loan all take weeks.
  • A for-sale-by-owner deal saves the commission but puts pricing, paperwork and haggling on you.
  • A direct cash sale is common for estates, houses with renters, properties behind on payments, and homes needing work a lender would not finance.

Home values in Decatur sit well under those of the Chicago suburbs, so one big repair bill can swallow much of a seller's margin. In those cases an as-is sale can net about what a polished listing would.

What shapes the Decatur housing market?

Decatur serves as Macon County's seat, in the middle of Illinois, on the Sangamon River and Lake Decatur. Settlers founded it in 1829, and its economy has long revolved around processing corn, soybeans and heavy equipment.

Caterpillar, Archer Daniels Midland, Mueller and Primient all operate plants here. The Midwest Inland Port links the city to Canadian National and Norfolk Southern rail lines and to Decatur Airport. Drivers rely on Interstate 72, U.S. 51, U.S. 36 and Illinois Routes 48, 105 and 121. Millikin University and Richland Community College add students and staff to the local population.

Most addresses fall in Decatur Public Schools District 61, whose high schools are Eisenhower and MacArthur. Parts of the city spill into the Mount Zion, Maroa-Forsyth, Meridian and Warrensburg-Latham districts, so the district named on a parcel's tax bill is something a buyer with children will check.

Winters are cold and summers hot under a humid continental climate, so inspectors pay close attention to roofs, heating systems and damp basements. The town also has Lincoln history: he settled just west of it in 1830, and the 1860 Illinois Republican convention held in Decatur gave him his first endorsement for President.

Which Decatur landmarks and districts come up with buyers?

Buyers often ask where a house sits relative to downtown and the industrial belt. Lincoln Square, the old town square, holds the 1896 Transfer House, an octagonal former streetcar shelter designed by William W. Boyington that was moved to Central Park in 1962 when U.S. 51 traffic made it an obstacle. The Decatur Municipal Band, organized in 1857, is among the oldest nonmilitary bands still playing in the United States and Canada.

On the commercial side, the Midwest Inland Port, established in 2013, includes an Archer Daniels Midland intermodal ramp, five major roadways and a foreign trade zone, and the area is both an enterprise zone and a tax increment financing district. Business Facilities ranked Decatur third nationally as an emerging logistics center.

Decatur as the 17th most populous city in Illinois, and it has also been the fastest shrinking, which is a reminder to price from recent local sales and not from older figures.

How affordable are Decatur homes by the numbers?

Decatur shrinking from 71,399 residents in its 2020 base to 67,884 in mid-2025, a drop of 4.9 percent. Prices are modest, and nearly four in ten homes are rented.

Middle value of an owner-occupied home (2020-2024 estimates)$99,600

At roughly $100,000, a single new roof or furnace can equal a noticeable slice of a house's worth. That arithmetic explains why many owners here lean toward selling as-is.

Which Macon County offices touch a Decatur sale?

Three offices share the Macon County Office Building at 141 South Main Street. Each opens at 8:30 in the morning and closes at 4:30 in the afternoon on weekdays, except legal holidays.

  • Recorder, Room 201, (217) 424-1359. Files deeds and mortgages, maintains a tract index more than 150 years old, and takes electronic filings through vendors such as CSC and Simplifile.
  • Treasurer, Room 302, (217) 424-1426. Sends the annual tax bill and provides duplicates.
  • Supervisor of Assessments, Room 401, (217) 424-1364. Publishes assessments, applies exemptions and serves as clerk to the Board of Review.

The state transfer tax comes from 35 ILCS 200/31-10, which sets 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500. Whether Macon County adds a stamp of its own is a question for the Recorder's counter.

How are Decatur property taxes billed, and what if they go unpaid?

Macon County runs a year behind: the bill mailed in May covers the previous tax year. The first installment comes due 30 days after the mailing date, and the second falls on September 1, shifting to the next working day when that date is a weekend or Labor Day.

On a sale, the Treasurer's advice is to read the closing paperwork and ask the title company who owes the bill. Lateness is costly: 1.5 percent attaches for every month or part of a month. Once the second installment passes, a certified delinquency notice goes out with $10 added, and the unpaid amount is auctioned to tax buyers who open at 9 percent and bid downward. A house lived in by its owner generally gets 30 to 36 months to redeem.

A duplicate bill costs $1.00 with proof of ownership. New owners should send the Treasurer a change-of-address form by March 15.

Disputing a value has a short fuse: 30 days from the day your township's figures run in the local paper. Complaints are filed with the Board of Review, and the assessor's staff recommend attaching comparable sales, an appraisal or a settlement statement.

Which Decatur ordinances matter for vacant homes and rentals?

Two city chapters can follow a property into a sale.

  • At-risk property registry (Chapter 70.2). Lenders register a property within 15 days of starting foreclosure. Owners of a derelict vacant house register within 30 days. Residential registration is listed at $200, renewed every six months, with a late charge of 10 percent of the semi-annual fee per 30-day period. A buyer takes over the duty and must register or update the file within 15 days of the transfer.
  • Short-term rentals (Chapter 51.5). A yearly license is listed at $25 per unit, and an 8 percent tax applies to gross rental receipts, with monthly returns due by the 20th.

A registered vacant house costs money every six months it stays empty, which makes a prompt as-is sale attractive. Ask the city's building department about open permits or violations before you set a price.

What should a Decatur seller line up before closing?

Collect the paperwork first, then compare bids by the amount left after payoffs.

  1. Pull your parcel number and the latest bill from the Treasurer.
  2. Request your recorded deed and make sure the names match the signers.
  3. Check that no city registration charge or code fine is outstanding.
  4. Round up leases and renter contact information if anyone lives there.
  5. Obtain written payoff letters from each lender or lienholder.

Whichever route you pick, closing ends with a title search, a signed deed, the state declaration and county recording. A cash buyer may skip the appraisal, but clean title is still required.

Frequently asked questions

Will a buyer take a Decatur house with open code problems?

Often yes. Investors regularly buy houses with violations and fix them. Learn from the city what is open so your price reflects it, and settle any registration balance first.

Who covers Illinois transfer tax on a Decatur sale?

The state rate is 50 cents for each $500 of value, and your contract decides which side pays. Confirm with your closing agent, and ask the Recorder if a county stamp also applies.

What are the due dates for Macon County tax bills?

Mailing happens in May, the first installment is due 30 days later, and the second is due September 1 or the next working day. Late payments add 1.5 percent monthly.

Is a license required for a Decatur Airbnb?

Yes. Chapter 51.5 requires a yearly license for each short-term unit, listed at $25, plus an 8 percent tax on rental receipts filed monthly with the city's Finance Department.

I inherited a Decatur house with unpaid taxes. Where do I start?

Call the Macon County Treasurer at (217) 424-1426 with the parcel number to learn the balance. If the taxes were sold, redemption runs through the County Clerk and includes penalty, costs and interest.

What are the realistic ways to sell a house fast in Skokie?

A Skokie owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or sell directly to a buyer who pays cash. The direct route usually shortens the calendar the most, because there is no showing schedule and no lender appraisal to wait on. Whichever path you take, Skokie adds its own paperwork: a village transfer stamp, a final water reading, and in some cases a pre-sale inspection.

This page walks through the village, its housing numbers, and the steps that sit between a signed contract and a recorded deed. The aim is to help you decide how much time you need before closing.

  • List on the open market and accept showings, repairs requests and a longer timeline.
  • Sell by owner and handle the contract, disclosures and title work yourself.
  • Sell directly to a cash buyer, usually as-is, with a closing date you choose.

What kind of village is Skokie?

Skokie is a village in Cook County, in Niles Township, about 15 miles north of the Chicago Loop. It covers roughly 10 square miles and borders Evanston, Chicago, Lincolnwood, Niles, Morton Grove, Glenview and Wilmette. Its street grid continues Chicago's numbering, which is why house numbers here read like Chicago addresses.

The community was incorporated in 1888 as Niles Centre, and voters picked the name Skokie in a referendum on November 15, 1940. The 1920s brought subdivisions of two and three flats and the Chicago-style bungalow, and a second building wave followed in the 1940s and 1950s. That history explains why so many Skokie homes are brick bungalows and mid-century houses, a stock that tends to need updated kitchens, electrical panels and mechanicals.

Major east-west roads include Old Orchard Road, Golf Road, Dempster Street, Oakton Street and Touhy Avenue, with Skokie Boulevard, Crawford Avenue and McCormick Boulevard running north and south.

What do Census figures say about Skokie homes and owners?

Skokie's population at 66,544 as of July 1, 2025, a little below the 67,824 counted in 2020. For 2020 to 2024 it shows 24,382 households averaging 2.68 people, and an owner-occupancy rate of 74.7%. Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $387,200.

Who buys in Skokie and what draws them?

Skokie sits on the CTA Yellow Line, which ends at the Dempster Street station, and a second station at Oakton Street opened on April 30, 2012 to serve the downtown. Pace's Pulse Dempster Line has run through the village since 2023, linking O'Hare Airport and Evanston. Interstate 94 and US 41 are the main highways. Census data puts mean travel to work at 27.9 minutes.

Employment is anchored by health care. The village's 2018 financial report listed NorthShore University HealthSystem as the largest employer at 2,410 people, ahead of Federal-Mogul and Niles Township High School District 219. The Illinois Science and Technology Park occupies the former Pfizer laboratories downtown, and Westfield Old Orchard is one of the larger malls in Illinois. Buyers who work in those places, or commute by Yellow Line, are the people most likely to pay a premium for a renovated Skokie house.

Which school districts serve Skokie?

Several elementary districts serve the village, and Niles Township High School District 219 operates the public high schools. A portion of Skokie is served by Evanston/Skokie School District 65 and Evanston Township High School. Because the boundary depends on the street, confirm the district for a specific address before you advertise schools to a buyer.

The village also hosts Oakton College's Ray Hartstein Campus on Lincoln Avenue and Hebrew Theological College on Carpenter Road. Skokie has many religious day schools alongside the public districts, and the village's Jewish community has been part of its identity since the post-war decades.

What does the weather do to a Skokie house?

Skokie has a humid continental climate with four distinct seasons. NOAA climate normals for the Skokie area show about 38.4 inches of snow a year and roughly 40 inches of precipitation, with January daily highs near 32 degrees Fahrenheit. Spring storms can be severe, and tornadoes are possible.

  • Freeze and thaw cycles stress older brick, chimneys and flat roofs.
  • Heavy spring and summer rain puts basements and sump pumps to the test.
  • Hot, humid July weather (daily highs near 85) leaves cooling systems under load.

Buyers inspecting a Skokie bungalow commonly focus on the basement, roof and electrical service, so knowing their condition before you set a price saves surprises.

What does the Village of Skokie require before a sale closes?

Skokie requires a transfer stamp for any change in ownership within the village, and the Village Clerk's Office sells it at Village Hall, 5127 Oakton Street. The village prints its rate as $3 per $1,000 of property value, or any fraction thereof. The stamp cannot be issued while the property has liens, code violations or an unpaid balance owed to the village.

To process the stamp, submit the completed Real Estate Transfer Tax Form together with a Request for Final Water Reading. The request lists the closing date, a contact name, phone and email, the seller's forwarding address for the last water bill, and the buyer's phone and email. Documents can go to transfertax@skokie.org or by mail to the Clerk's Office. The clerk's phone is 847-933-8203.

There is one more step for rental property. The village will not issue a stamp for a multi-unit rental building, or for a single-family house, duplex or townhouse used as a rental unit, until the Property Standards Division has inspected it and any violations are corrected. Village ordinance says to schedule that inspection at least 28 days before closing, and last-minute slots may not exist.

Which state and county transfer taxes apply in Skokie?

The Cook County Clerk lists the state rate as $0.50 per $500 and the Cook County rate as $0.25 per $500, with the seller named as the liable party. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-15, county recorders sell the state stamps at 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction, and the statute moves the stamps to an electronic format after paper stamps were phased out at the end of 2025. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-20, a deed will not be accepted for filing unless the stamps have been purchased from the recorder of the county where it is filed.

Skokie's own tax is a third layer, so a sale in the village carries state, county and village charges. Ask your title company for a line-by-line estimate before you agree to a net number, because the contract decides who ultimately pays what.

How are Skokie property taxes billed, and what happens at closing?

Cook County bills Skokie parcels in two installments. The Cook County Treasurer's due dates page shows tax year 2025 first installment due April 1, 2026 and second installment due October 1, 2026, both now past. Tax year 2024 was due March 4, 2025 and December 15, 2025, and tax year 2023 was due March 1, 2024 and August 1, 2024. The schedule has shifted from year to year, so ask the Treasurer for the current installment dates and any payment already posted to your parcel.

At closing, the title company usually divides the year's tax between buyer and seller by closing date. Exemptions also matter: the Treasurer's site lists a Homeowner Exemption, a Senior Citizen Homestead Exemption and a Senior Citizen Assessment Freeze Exemption, and a buyer needs to apply for the ones they qualify for after the sale.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What are the steps to a quick sale in Skokie?

Work backward from the closing date, because the village timelines drive the schedule.

  • Pull the village's lien and violation status and clear any unpaid balance.
  • If the house is a rental, book the Property Standards inspection at least 28 days ahead.
  • Gather your forwarding address and the buyer's contact details for the final water reading request.
  • Order the state transfer declaration through the title company so the stamps and deed are ready together.
  • Record the deed with the Cook County Clerk's recording division after the stamps are affixed.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the Skokie transfer tax?

The village prints $3 per $1,000 of property value, or any fraction thereof. State tax of $0.50 per $500 and Cook County tax of $0.25 per $500 apply on top, according to the Cook County Clerk.

Does Skokie inspect houses before a sale?

Only rental property. The village will not issue a transfer stamp for a multi-unit rental building, or a single-family house, duplex or townhouse used as a rental, until an inspection is done and violations are fixed. Schedule it at least 28 days before closing.

Who arranges the final water reading in Skokie?

The seller submits a Request for Final Water Reading with the transfer tax paperwork. It lists the closing date, contacts and the seller's forwarding address for the last bill. The Clerk's Office takes the package at transfertax@skokie.org.

Can I sell a Skokie house with code violations?

You can sell it, but the village will not issue the transfer stamp while code violations or village balances remain open. Clear them first, or ask the Clerk's Office at 847-933-8203 how an open item affects your closing.

Which county records a Skokie deed?

Cook County. The Cook County Clerk's recording division collects the state and county stamps, and the deed needs the village stamp as well. Your title company normally handles the filing.

Why do people sell and buy houses in Palatine?

Palatine is a mostly residential village in the northwest Chicago suburbs. It sits mainly in Cook County, and a portion reaches into Lake County. The village covers about 14 square miles, and 67,908 people were counted on census day in 2020.

Growth came in waves. The village was founded in 1866 around a station on the Chicago and North Western Railway. After World War II the first suburb-style subdivision, Palanois Park, went up, and the population climbed from 11,504 in 1960 to 26,050 in 1970 and 65,479 by 2000. So much of the village's housing was built in the decades after 1950, and buyers of houses that age tend to ask about roofs, furnaces and basements first.

The Census Bureau estimated 65,842 residents for July 2025, about 3 percent below the 2020 base. The housing figures in the next section show a village where roughly two of every three homes are owner-occupied.

How do Palatine's numbers compare for owners and renters?

The figures below are five-year survey estimates covering 2020 through 2024.

Palatine village housing and income snapshot, Census Bureau QuickFacts

Owner-occupancy rate67.4%
Owner-occupied home value, median$355,600

With median rent at $1,549 and about a third of units not owner-occupied, some buyers are investors who lease houses out. An investor can price repairs into an offer, which is why an as-is sale can draw interest here.

Which commute routes and school districts help a Palatine listing?

Commuting is the village's selling point. The Palatine Metra station on the Union Pacific Northwest Line runs southeast to Ogilvie Transportation Center in Chicago and northwest toward Harvard and McHenry. Pace buses on Routes 604 and 697 connect to the Northwest Transportation Center in Schaumburg. The village has been rebuilding its downtown since December 1999, which added a new passenger station, a parking garage, condominiums and rowhouses near the tracks.

Public schools split by level:

  • Community Consolidated School District 15 for elementary and middle grades, with schools such as Lake Louise, Pleasant Hill, Willow Bend and Walter R. Sundling Middle School.
  • Township High School District 211 for high school, with Palatine High School and William Fremd High School both inside the village.
  • William Rainey Harper College, the community college for the area.

Private options include Saint Theresa, Saint Thomas of Villanova and Immanuel Lutheran, all preschool through grade 8. Buyers will want to know which attendance zone applies, so confirm the address with each district ahead of listing.

What does the weather and ground do to a Palatine house?

Palatine has a hot-summer humid continental climate with four distinct seasons. NOAA normals for 1990 to 2020 show about 37.6 inches of precipitation and 38.5 inches of snowfall annually, with January afternoons averaging 28.7 degrees and July afternoons 81.3. Spring brings thunderstorms and sometimes tornadoes.

The terrain adds a second factor. The village sits in wooded marshland where several streams begin. Most drain to Salt Creek, which rises at Wilke Marsh on the east side, while the northeast corner drains to Buffalo Creek and a small piece of the southeast to McDonald Creek. Wet basements, sump pumps and grading are therefore routine inspection topics. If your house has had water in the basement, a buyer will want to see repair records and any permit for drainage work.

Which repairs need a Palatine building permit before you sell?

The village issues two kinds of permit: Express for small, listed projects on detached single-family homes, with a stated goal of review within 5 business days, and Standard for larger work, with a goal of 10 to 15 business days. The Building and Inspection Services Division at 200 E. Wood Street answers questions at 847-359-9042.

According to the village, these projects need a permit:

  • Building or replacing a deck, shed, roof or fence.
  • Installing or replacing an air conditioner, furnace or water heater.
  • Finishing or remodeling a basement, kitchen or bathroom.
  • Adding or altering the electrical system, or replacing an electric stove with a gas model.
  • Drainage work, including regrading and connecting a downspout or sump pump to buried pipe.

Painting, installing flooring, replacing a faucet and swapping a window or door of the same size in the same opening usually do not. If a past owner did permit-required work without one, ask the division how to resolve it before a buyer's inspector finds it.

Does Palatine require a rental license when a house is leased?

Yes. Under Chapter 12 of the village code, every residential rental, including single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums, must be inspected and carry an annual Rental Dwelling License. The program dates to 1990.

An owner applies through the Citizen Self Service portal, pays the invoice, calls for an inspection, and attends a landlord seminar while adopting a Palatine lease addendum. The license expires one year after the application date and renews automatically unless the owner asks to close it. If a tenant lease runs past your closing date, tell buyers whether the license is current. If an investor buys it, the new owner starts the licensing steps for that address.
