What transfer taxes and recording steps apply in Palatine?

Palatine's finance FAQ answers no to a village-level transfer tax. The taxes that remain are the state and county ones, collected at recording.

Cook County Clerk's municipal list shows the state rate as 50 cents per $500 and the county rate as 25 cents per $500. Lake County's own pamphlet prints the same two rates, and notes that the Clerk collects only the state and county portions. A deed for a sale needs the state transfer declaration (PTAX-203), which is filed through the state's MyDec system.

One detail trips people up. The Clerk's list shows Rolling Meadows charging $3.00 per $1,000 and says its entry includes some Palatine mailing addresses. A Palatine address does not guarantee a Palatine location, so have the title company confirm the municipality from the parcel number. If your parcel sits in Lake County instead of Cook, you record with the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division.

What are the quickest ways to sell in Palatine?

Three routes exist: hire a listing agent, go for sale by owner, or take an offer from a cash buyer. Listing gives the widest exposure but means showings, buyer financing and repair requests after inspection. An investor paying cash will accept the property in its current condition and can set closing around your calendar, which suits a house with deferred maintenance, tenants in place, or a probate timeline.

  • Gather the deed, the last tax bill, any permit records and the rental license if the house was leased.
  • Ask the title company which county and municipality your parcel belongs to.
  • Compare any offer to what a listed sale would net after repairs, carrying costs and fees.

Frequently asked questions

Does Palatine charge a real estate transfer tax?

No. The village's finance FAQ rules it out. Illinois and the county still collect their own transfer taxes at recording, and the Cook County list shows 50 cents per $500 for the state and 25 cents per $500 for the county.

Which county records a Palatine deed?

Most of the village is in Cook County, so the Cook County Clerk's recording office handles those parcels. A portion lies in Lake County, and those parcels are recorded by the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division. Your title company can confirm which one applies from the parcel number.

Is a permit needed for a new roof or water heater in Palatine?

Yes. The village lists building or replacing a roof, and installing or replacing a water heater, furnace or air conditioner, among projects that need a permit. Express review is aimed at 5 business days. Call 847-359-9042 if you are unsure about a specific job.

Do I have to license a Palatine house I rent out before selling?

If it is rented, it needs an annual Rental Dwelling License under the village's Chapter 12 program. The license lasts one year from the application date and renews automatically unless you ask to close it. Ask the village how to close it once the sale is done.

Will anyone buy a Palatine house that needs work?

Yes. Many buyers, especially investors, purchase older Palatine houses as they are. Expect a buyer to price in roof, furnace, drainage and permit issues, so gather your permit records and any repair invoices before you ask for offers.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326

Selling in Des Plaines?

How can you sell a house in Des Plaines, IL?

An owner in Des Plaines can hire a broker, go it alone, or take cash from a purchaser who buys the house as it is. Repair needs, tenants in the unit and a firm closing date tend to decide which path fits.

  • A full listing can fetch strong prices where the middle home value is $335,600, but it brings showings, an appraisal and repair requests.
  • Selling alone skips the commission and makes the contract and disclosures your job.
  • A cash deal shortens the calendar and suits estates, rentals and houses with postponed maintenance.

Because Des Plaines sits beside O'Hare and two tollways, buyers range from commuters to investors who want rentals near the airport and the Metra line.

What makes Des Plaines distinct for a homeowner?

Des Plaines is a Cook County city that sits just north of O'Hare International Airport and takes its name from the river that runs along its east side. Its 14 square miles held 60,675 people in 2020.

French explorers named the river for the sycamores they thought resembled European plane trees. American settlers arrived after the 1833 Treaty of Chicago, followed by German immigrants. The Chicago, St. Paul and Fond du Lac Railroad built through in 1857, the stop took the Des Plaines name in 1859, and voters converted the village to a city in 1925. Postwar growth took off with O'Hare next door, lifting the census count from 14,994 in 1950 to 57,239 in 1970.

The road network includes Interstates 90 and 294, U.S. 12, 14 and 45, and Illinois 58, 72 and 83. Commuters board Union Pacific Northwest Line trains at the Des Plaines and Cumberland stations, and the Pace Pulse Dempster Line links Evanston with O'Hare. The city's 2021 annual financial report names these major employers: Rivers Casino, Universal Oil Products, Oakton College, Sysco, Juno Lighting, Holy Family Medical Center, Wheels Inc. and LSG Sky Chefs.

Younger students go to District 62, 59 or 63 schools, and high schoolers go to Maine West in District 207.

What does the census say about Des Plaines housing costs?

58,772 residents for mid-2025, 3.1 percent fewer than the 2020 base of 60,653. Owners live in most homes, and 34.2 percent of residents were born outside the United States.

Des Plaines housing figures, Census QuickFacts, 2020-2024 estimates
MeasureDes Plaines
Middle value of homes their owners occupy$335,600
Owner-occupied share of housing units78.3%
Median gross monthly rent$1,606
Number of households22,537
Average commute to work28.2 minutes

Because 92.3 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, few houses change hands, which leaves sellers with fewer recent nearby sales as price guides.

What local details come up with Des Plaines buyers?

The city uses ZIP codes 60016 through 60019 and area codes 847 and 224, at an elevation of 642 feet. Rivers Casino opened in July 2011 on roughly 21 acres next to the Tri-State Tollway at Devon Avenue and Des Plaines River Road, after the Illinois Gaming Board awarded the state's tenth casino license in 2008. It appears among the city's major employers.

Under parts of town lies the Des Plaines Disturbance, a zone of badly fractured rock that may mark an ancient meteorite crater 75 to 200 feet down, filled long ago by glacial activity. Nothing shows on the surface, and it rarely matters to a sale, but local lore makes it a conversation point.

Oakton College keeps a campus in the city, and Holy Family Medical Center also appears on the employer list.

Does a river, tornado history or flooding matter when selling a Des Plaines house?

Yes. A buyer or lender will ask about flooding. The McDonald's museum in town was torn down in 2018 after repeated flooding, and the river runs just east of downtown. Disclose any basement water or insurance claims and keep your repair receipts.

The earliest known Illinois tornado struck the site of modern Des Plaines on May 22, 1855, and spring storms here can still turn severe. The O'Hare station nearby averages 38.4 inches of snowfall, which is hard on roofs and gutters.

One more local quirk affects sellers: addresses inside city limits use the Des Plaines numbering system, while unincorporated parts of Maine Township with a Des Plaines mailing address follow Chicago's grid. Confirm with the city whether your parcel is incorporated, since that decides which city rules and which transfer tax apply.

How do Cook County recording and transfer taxes affect a Des Plaines sale?

A Des Plaines deed is recorded by the Cook County Clerk's recording division at 118 North Clark Street in Chicago. The clerk's schedule prices a deed at $107, a total that folds in the GIS, document storage and rental housing support fees, plus $5 per document for mail-back recording.

Three layers of transfer tax can apply, and the Clerk's list names the seller as the party liable on each:

  • State of Illinois: .50 per $500.00 of value, matching the rate in 35 ILCS 200/31-10.
  • Cook County: .25 per $500.00.
  • City of Des Plaines: 2.00 per $1,000.00, evidenced by a rubber stamp, with a $10.00 fee for exempt transfers.

The Clerk calls its municipal list a courtesy that is not legally binding, so phone the city's listed number, 847-391-5325, to confirm the stamp before closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Des Plaines houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How are Des Plaines property taxes billed and appealed?

Cook County splits the year's tax into two bills. Per the Treasurer's primer, the first equals 55 percent of last year's total and is typically due March 1, while homeowner and senior exemptions show up on the second. Interest on late payments runs 1.5 percent monthly.

Values come from the Cook County Assessor. Maine Township, which covers parts of Des Plaines, received new values on June 4, 2025, the latest turn in a three-year cycle. In 2026 the north suburbs are reassessed only where something changed, such as a permit. Maine's 2026 appeal window at the Assessor shut on July 21, and the Board of Review accepted appeals from August 31 through September 29, 2026.

Have the PIN ready when you talk to the Treasurer or Assessor, because Cook County identifies every parcel by a 14-digit number. Your closing agent will explain how the year's bill is divided at the table.

Which Des Plaines rules cover rentals and repairs before a sale?

Rental owners in Des Plaines need a rental license, and an ordinance passed on February 2, 2009 makes them complete Phase 1 of the Crime Free Multi-Housing Program. A first-time license applicant must attend the seminar beforehand.

Repair permits are filed online through the city's self-service portal, and express guides exist for sheds, decks, fences, driveways, roofs and non-structural kitchen or bath remodels. The city adopted the 2021 I-Codes, effective January 1, 2026, and its permit page lists construction hours of 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Saturday and 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Sunday. Inspections of rental dwellings or permitted work are booked at 847-391-5382 or permits@desplainesil.gov.

Closing out open permits before listing keeps unfinished work from surfacing late in a sale. Construction work in the city also needs a registered contractor, and contractor registration now runs through the same online portal, so a seller hiring out repairs should confirm the contractor is registered before the work starts.

If you plan to sell a rental, the city's rental dwelling inspection line is a useful first call, since it lets you learn what an inspector would flag before a buyer's inspector does.

Frequently asked questions

Who is liable for transfer tax on a Des Plaines sale?

The Cook County Clerk's list shows the seller as liable for the state, county and city taxes. Your contract can allocate it differently, so confirm with your closing agent.

Where is a Des Plaines deed filed?

With the Cook County Clerk's recording division at 118 North Clark Street in Chicago. Title companies can also submit deeds electronically.

Is a license needed to lease my Des Plaines house?

Yes. Rental property owners must obtain a license and complete the Crime Free Multi-Housing seminar before a new license is issued.

Does a Des Plaines mailing address mean I am in the city?

Not always. Some unincorporated Maine Township addresses carry a Des Plaines mailing address but follow Chicago's numbering. Ask the city to confirm that your parcel is within the limits.

Is the Maine Township appeal window still open?

The 2026 filing windows with the Assessor and the Board of Review have closed. Cook County sets new windows by township each year, so check the Assessor's assessment calendar for the next opening.

How can you sell a house fast in Orland Park, Illinois?

Orland Park sellers have three practical routes: a traditional listing, a sale without an agent, or a direct cash purchase. A cash buyer can close the fastest, while a listing often brings the highest price for a house in good order.

Orland Park is a village of about 22 square miles 25 miles southwest of Chicago, and most of it lies in Cook County with a small piece in Will County. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 57,954 residents, and 24.8% of them are 65 or older.

  • List with an agent when the roof, furnace and kitchen are in decent shape and you can wait through showings and a buyer's mortgage approval.
  • Sell it yourself when you are comfortable negotiating and coordinating with a title company and the village.
  • Take a cash offer when the house needs repairs, a probate is pending, or a tenant must be dealt with. Compare it against a listing price less commission, repairs and months of carrying costs.

How did Orland Park grow into the village it is today?

Orland Park began as a farming settlement called Orland in 1834 and grew into a large suburb mainly after 1960. The village was incorporated on May 31, 1892, after a Wabash Railroad line built in 1879 brought the town its first station, Sedgwick Station.

The population counts show how late the growth came: 788 in 1950, 2,592 in 1960, 23,045 in 1980, 51,077 in 2000 and 58,703 in 2020. Orland Square Mall opened in 1976, and shopping centers such as Orland Park Crossing followed. Most of the village's present population arrived after 1960.

The village likes to call itself the World's Golf Center. Village lore says someone counted 1,089 golf holes within 15 miles, and the slogan is painted on seven water towers. Wikipedia also notes planned downtown redevelopment at 143rd Street and LaGrange Road, the Main Street Triangle, with an estimated completion in fall 2027.

What roads and trains connect Orland Park to Chicago?

Interstate 80 forms the southern edge of the village, and Metra's SouthWest Service stops at 143rd Street, 153rd Street and 179th Street. Those three stations give commuters train service to Chicago Union Station on weekdays, with Pace buses on several routes.

The main corridors for drivers are La Grange Road (U.S. 45) north to south, 159th Street (U.S. 6) east to west, Harlem Avenue (Illinois 43) near the eastern border, Illinois 7, and 167th Street, which runs entirely inside the village. For 2020-2024 the Census Bureau reports a 33.8-minute average commute.

Orland Park's neighbors are Homer Glen to the west, Orland Hills and Mokena to the south, Tinley Park to the southeast, Oak Forest to the east, and Palos Park and Palos Heights to the north. Two bodies of water, Lake Sedgwick and McGinnis Slough, lie inside the village limits.

Which schools serve Orland Park addresses?

Most of the Cook County part of Orland Park is in Orland School District 135, and all of it feeds Consolidated High School District 230, whose Carl Sandburg High School serves most of the village. Addresses in the northern edge may instead be zoned to Stagg or Victor J. Andrew high schools, so confirm the exact school for your street.

Four elementary districts reach Orland Park in Cook County: District 135, Community Consolidated District 146, Palos District 118 and Kirby District 140. District 135 runs Century, Jerling and Orland junior highs. In Will County, Mokena School District 159 and Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210 cover homes in the village. St. Michael School is the Archdiocese of Chicago school in the village, and Moraine Valley Community College in nearby Palos Hills offers community college classes.

What local amenities do buyers ask about in Orland Park?

Buyers mostly ask about parks, shopping and the village's recreation facilities, and Orland Park has plenty of each. The village lists more than 60 parks, and Centennial Park holds the Aquatic Center with six water slides, Lake Sedgwick with boardwalks and pedal boats, and a free outdoor ice rink that runs from November to March.

The Sportsplex on 159th Street is the largest indoor recreation building, with three basketball courts, an indoor soccer field and a quarter-mile track. Shopping centers include Orland Square Mall and Orland Park Crossing, and healthcare, finance and retail make up much of the local employment base. The Taste of Orland Park food festival is held at the Village Center in early August, and the village hosts Independence Day fireworks in Centennial Park West.

Census data show a settled community: 90.3% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 25.9% of residents age five and older speak a language other than English at home. A listing that names the nearest park, Metra station and school boundary answers the questions buyers raise first.

Does Orland Park require anything from a seller or a landlord?

The village runs a rental registration program, and it applies to single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums as well as apartment buildings. The annual fee is $100 per unit for a detached or attached single-family residence and $100 plus $15 per additional unit for a multi-family building.

  • Inspections follow the village's tri-annual schedule, and a rental housing sticker is issued when the unit passes.
  • Landlords or their agents must attend one eight-hour Crime Free Housing seminar from the police department.
  • Every lease must carry the village's Crime Free Lease Addendum, signed by each tenant age 18 or older.

When a rental is part of the sale, tell the buyer whether the unit is registered and when the last inspection took place. Development Services answers registration questions at (708) 403-5300.

How do I handle water service and county taxes when selling in Orland Park?

Water is billed every two months by the village, and a high bill should be reviewed by calling 708-403-6175. Property owners are responsible for the private water line from the shut-off valve, usually in the parkway, to the house, plus any leaks inside.

Property tax comes from Cook County. Orland Township is in the 2023 and 2026 reassessment group, and the township assessor's office is at 14807 S. Ravinia Ave., phone (708) 403-4222. For tax year 2025 the Cook County Treasurer set the first installment due date at April 1, 2026 and the second at October 1, 2026, and both have passed. Ask the Treasurer for the next due date and ask your closing agent how the year's tax is prorated between you and the buyer.

A small part of Orland Park lies in Will County. If your house is in that part, ask the Will County treasurer for the schedule on your bill.

What do Census figures say about Orland Park housing?

The Census Bureau shows 85.8% of homes occupied by their owners and a typical owner-reported value of $367,200.

Orland Park village, U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts (housing and income are 2020-2024 estimates)
MeasureOrland Park
Estimated residents, mid-202557,954
Households23,256

Frequently asked questions

Does Orland Park charge a transfer tax when I sell?

Ask the village finance office and your title company which village charges apply to your closing, and get the figures in writing before the closing date.

Which county bills property tax in Orland Park?

Cook County, for almost all of the village. A small part sits in Will County and is billed there. Check the first digits and the county named on your tax bill.

Do I have to register a rental house in Orland Park before selling it?

If it is rented, yes, the village requires annual registration at $100 per unit for a single-family home, with inspections on a tri-annual schedule. Share the registration and inspection records with the buyer.

Where do I report a high final water bill in Orland Park?

Call the village water billing line at 708-403-6175. The village bills two months at a time, and owners are responsible for leaks on the private line and inside the house.

How is Orland Park's reassessment schedule set?

Cook County reassesses each township every three years. Orland Township is in the 2023 and 2026 group, so a new notice arrives in the reassessment year and the township assessor can answer questions.

What does selling a house in Oak Lawn, Illinois involve?

Oak Lawn has several local steps: a village transfer stamp, a point-of-sale sewer inspection for houses, and a stamp refund program for some sellers. Each step has its own form, so starting early protects the closing date.

The village borders Chicago on the southwest side and had 58,362 residents in the 2020 census. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 56,450, a 3.2% drop from the April 2020 base. It spans about 8.6 square miles with a density near 6,800 people per square mile, which means most homes sit on compact lots.

The sections below follow the order of a typical sale: the village stamp, the sewer inspection, Cook County recording, and property tax.

How did Oak Lawn develop?

The area was first called Black Oak Grove, after a road along today's 95th Street, and was settled in 1835. The Wabash Railroad brought a depot in 1880, and by 1882 the post office and station were simply Oak Lawn. The village incorporated in 1909. Growth jumped after World War II, and by 1960 nearly 20,000 people lived here.

On April 21, 1967, a tornado cut through the village, damaging or destroying roughly 900 buildings and killing more than 30 people. Rebuilding drove another round of growth, and the population peaked at about 63,500 in the mid-1970s. Since 2002 the downtown stretch of 95th Street has been redeveloped with condominium buildings, shops, a Metra station expansion and a parking garage.

  • Advocate Christ Medical Center is one of the largest hospitals and Level I trauma centers in the state.
  • Metra's SouthWest Service runs from the Oak Lawn station toward downtown Chicago.
  • Elementary schools include Kolb, Lieb, Harnew, Columbus Manor, Covington, Hannum, Hometown, Kolmar and Sward, with Simmons and Oak Lawn-Hometown as middle schools.
  • Oak Lawn Community High School and Harold L. Richards High School are the two public high schools.

What do Census figures show for Oak Lawn housing?

Over 82% of homes are owner-occupied, and the median household income is $83,911. The table collects the housing numbers a seller is most likely to compare against.

How does the Oak Lawn transfer stamp work?

The Cook County Clerk's October 2025 list shows an Oak Lawn tax of 5.00 per 1,000 of value, enacted January 1, 1982, with the seller liable and an exemption letter attached to the recording as proof. Exempt transfers pay no fee. The village adds that senior sellers of a primary residence are now exempt, with the rules in section 3 of its exemption list.

  • Request stamps or an exemption letter from the Finance Department. The village accepts only electronic fillable forms, and handwritten forms are rejected.
  • Questions go to 708-499-7775 or transferstamps@oaklawn-il.gov.
  • A Utility Billing Account Change form handles the water account.
  • The village's own address on the Clerk's list is 9446 S. Raymond St., phone 708.636.4400.

State and county taxes sit on top: 50 cents per $500 for the state under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, and 25 cents per $500 for Cook County.

What is the sewer inspection and how do I schedule it?

Oak Lawn requires a sewer inspection, called I&I, for single-family homes and qualifying townhomes before the transfer stamp. The village recommends scheduling well ahead of closing.

  1. Use the village's online permit portal, search the property address, choose Residential and the Transfer Stamp Sewer Inspection (I&I) permit type, and enter N/A for work details.
  2. The village reviews the request and emails either a record number with a scheduling link or a note that no inspection is needed.
  3. Pick a date for the I&I Sewer inspection. It happens between 10am and 2pm, and someone over 18 must be present with access to the interior.
  4. After the inspection, a payment link arrives by email for $100, and the results follow once payment is made.

Ask the village's Finance Department at 708-499-7775 whether your address needs the inspection, since the village screens each request first.

Can I get some transfer stamp money back?

Yes, in three cases under village ordinance 3-2-7, each requiring the seller to have owned and lived in the house as a principal residence without renting any part of it.

  • Reinvestment: buy or build a single-family home or condominium inside the village within one year of paying the tax, and live there.
  • Senior citizens: a one-time refund for a seller age 65 or older who owned and occupied the home for more than one year, with a rule for co-owners under 60.
  • Family sale: sell to a child, parent, grandparent, brother, sister or grandchild, step relatives included.

Refund requests are due within one year of the sale. Packets for each case are linked from the village's refund page, and the Finance Department's refund line is 708-499-7777.

How does Cook County assessment and recording apply?

Oak Lawn deeds are recorded with the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St. The Clerk lists the seller as liable for both the state and county stamps. A PTAX-203 declaration accompanies the deed.

For assessments, look up your 14-digit PIN on the Cook County Assessor's site to see your township. The south and west suburban townships follow a triennial cycle with reassessments in 2023 and 2026. Ask the Cook County Treasurer for installment status on the parcel, and expect the title company to prorate the year's bill at closing.

What do buyers see in Oak Lawn parks and daily life?

The village maintains 22 parks on more than 300 acres. Centennial Park alone covers 38 acres, and the park system includes outdoor pools, an indoor ice arena, two fitness centers, an indoor racquet center and an 18-hole golf course. Oak Lawn's public library began in 1934 with a collection of one hundred books.

Broadband subscriptions reach 91.3% of households in the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures, and the median owner cost with a mortgage is $2,000 a month. Those are useful points when a buyer weighs a house here against a rental.

Which sale route fits an Oak Lawn house?

An updated house near 95th Street or the Metra station usually does well in a listing. A house with sewer problems, an old rental history or an estate behind it often fits a direct as-is sale better, since the inspection and stamp steps still apply either way.

Yes. The Cook County Clerk's list shows a village rate of 5.00 per 1,000 of value, paid by the seller, with exempt transfers needing an exemption letter. Contact the Finance Department at 708-499-7775 for the stamp.

What does the Oak Lawn sewer inspection cost?

The village charges $100, paid by a link emailed after the inspection. It applies to single-family homes and qualifying townhomes and runs between 10am and 2pm.

Are seniors exempt from the transfer stamp?

The village states that seniors selling a primary residence are now exempt, with details in section 3 of its exemption list. A separate refund route exists for sellers 65 or older under ordinance 3-2-7.

How long do I have to ask for a stamp refund?

Refunds must be requested within one year of the date of sale. The village lists reinvestment, senior and immediate family cases, each with its own packet.

Where is an Oak Lawn deed recorded?

With the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St., phone 312.603.5050. The sale also needs the PTAX-203 declaration and stamped deed.

What changes when a Mount Prospect house goes on the market?

Mount Prospect is a Cook County village, so a sale here can carry transfer charges at three levels: state, county and village. The village stamp is its own step, apart from county recording, so schedule it early.

The village sits about 20 miles northwest of downtown Chicago and roughly 4 miles north of O'Hare Airport, partly in Elk Grove Township and partly in Wheeling Township. The Metra station and the closeness to O'Hare are the location points most listings lead with.

Owners here usually pick between an agent, an investor who pays cash, or a sale handled alone. The facts below apply to all three.

What do Census figures show about Mount Prospect homes?

Mount Prospect recorded 56,852 residents in 2020. The Bureau's mid-2025 estimate of 55,395 is 2.6 percent under its base figure. All of that fits within 10.72 square miles of land, or about 5,304 people for each one.

Census estimates for 2020 to 2024 put the midpoint home at $397,400 and midpoint rent at $1,502. Owner costs run $2,619 monthly with a loan and $1,046 without. Households number 21,600, averaging 2.56 people; 68.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the midpoint household brings in $101,720.

Nearly 30 percent of residents (29.6) were born abroad, and 43.1 percent of those age 5 and up use another language at home. A listing written in more than one language may reach more people. Among adults 25 and older, 48.6 percent hold a bachelor's degree or beyond.

Which school districts serve Mount Prospect houses?

Several elementary districts divide the village, and the district for your address often matters more to buyers than the village name. Confirm it before you advertise.

  • Central Mount Prospect: Mount Prospect School District 57.
  • North and somewhat east: River Trails School District 26.
  • South and somewhat west: Elk Grove Community Consolidated School District 59.
  • Small northern, north central and northwest pockets: Buffalo Grove-Wheeling CCSD 21, Arlington Heights District 25 and Prospect Heights District 23.

Township High School District 214 covers the whole village. Prospect High School is the only district 214 high school inside Mount Prospect, and some students attend Elk Grove High School or Buffalo Grove High School. Park services also vary by address, with the Mount Prospect, Arlington Heights, Des Plaines, Prospect Heights and River Trails park districts all serving parts of the village.

How do transit, jobs and shopping help a Mount Prospect sale?

Commuters board Metra's Union Pacific Northwest Line in the village: southeast to Ogilvie Transportation Center, northwest toward Harvard and McHenry. Pace buses cover local routes.

Employment is local too. The village's 2025 financial report lists CVS Caremark and Robert Bosch Tool Corporation as its largest employers, followed by the Village, Mount Prospect School District 57, Township High School District 214, Rauland-Borg, Costco, Walmart, School District 59 and TJX. Randhurst Village is the best-known retail address, and companies based in the village include Cummins Allison, NTN USA and Rauland-Borg.

The village counts as entirely urban. Its climate is humid continental, with muggy summers and snowy winters, in plant hardiness zone 5b, which is why inspectors look hard at roofs, sump pumps and furnaces.

What transfer taxes apply when a Mount Prospect house sells?

The Cook County Clerk's transfer fee listing starts with two charges: the State of Illinois at fifty cents for each $500, and Cook County at twenty-five cents for each $500. The seller is named as the liable party on both. The state figure matches 35 ILCS 200/31-15.

The village adds a real estate transfer tax of its own, paid by buying a stamp. Finance, on its Taxes and Service Fees page, offers an online stamp application and in-person stamps by appointment, along with a rebate form and an affidavit of no consideration for exempt transfers such as taking a person off a deed. Call Finance for the current village rate and the party responsible, since both come from the Village Code.

The Clerk's site also has a lookup that shows the transfer fee for each municipality in the county, handy for comparing neighboring towns. Put all three charges in your net sheet early.

How are Mount Prospect property taxes billed?

Cook County splits each year's property tax into two bills. The Treasurer's schedule lists April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026 for tax year 2025, and both have passed. Earlier years landed on other days, so rely on the date printed on your own bill.

The title company typically splits the year's tax between buyer and seller from the latest bill, so bring that bill and your parcel number. The Treasurer's site also describes homeowner, senior, senior freeze, disability and disabled veteran exemptions that a qualifying buyer may look into afterward.

Finance also describes a property tax relief grant for qualifying single-family owners, a rebate on part of the village share of the county bill. Call to learn whether it is open before counting on it.

Which disclosures and village rules apply to a seller?

Illinois puts the disclosure duty in 765 ILCS 77/20: report completed, report delivered, all before a contract is signed. Local buyers also ask about permit history on additions, finished basements and mechanical work.

The Village Code is posted online through the village's code library, and Community Development is the office for permit, inspection and code questions. For a rental, ask the village what license or inspection covers your address before you list.

  • Request permit records for work done during your ownership.
  • Resolve open code notices, since an unresolved notice can complicate the closing.
  • Confirm the water, sewer and refuse account status with the village before closing.

Any past basement water belongs on the report, with repair invoices on hand.

How do the three ways to sell compare in Mount Prospect?

Listing through an agent reaches the most people, with showings, inspections and a lender's schedule attached. Where household income at the median is $101,720, an updated house in a favored school zone may attract competing offers.

  • Agent: fits a house that shows well and an owner able to wait out a standard closing.
  • Owner sale: skips the listing fee but leaves the disclosure form, contract and stamp paperwork to you.
  • Cash purchaser: fewer conditions and a closing date you may help choose, at an offer reduced for needed repairs.

Whichever you pick, get the offer on paper and settle who pays each transfer charge.

Does Mount Prospect have its own transfer tax?

Yes. Finance sells the village's transfer stamps, online or in person by appointment. Ask it for the current rate and the responsible party, because the village sets this apart from the state and county charges.

How much is the Cook County transfer fee?

The Clerk lists twenty-five cents per $500 for Cook County and fifty cents per $500 for the state, with the seller liable for each.

Which school district is my Mount Prospect house in?

It depends on the address. Central areas are in District 57, north and east areas in River Trails District 26, south and west areas in District 59, and small northern pockets in Districts 21, 25 and 23. Township High School District 214 covers the whole village.

What if I need to remove someone from a Mount Prospect deed?

Finance links an affidavit declaring no consideration for exempt transfers like taking a person off a deed. Ask Finance whether your situation qualifies.

When are Cook County property taxes due?

The Treasurer's schedule gave April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026 for tax year 2025. Other years use different dates, so compare against your own bill.

Which selling routes make sense in Tinley Park?

A Tinley Park owner can list with a broker, market the house alone, or sell as-is to a buyer paying cash. The village straddles two counties, so the first job is to see which one your parcel belongs to.

Tinley Park is a southern suburb of Chicago covering about 16.2 square miles, with Cook County townships Bremen, Orland and Rich and Will County's Frankfort Township under one village government. The Census Bureau counted 56,703 residents in 2010 and 55,971 in 2020, and estimates 55,140 for July 1, 2025.

Does Cook County or Will County handle my Tinley Park house?

The county that holds your parcel number sends the tax bill, hears assessment appeals and records the deed, whatever the village line says. Part of the village lies in Will County, and that side includes the Brookside Marketplace shopping center.

The two counties run separate offices. Look at the latest tax bill, spot the county, and ask that county's treasurer where the account stands. Cook County's due dates change from year to year, as the table further down shows.

The village's four townships are Bremen, Orland and Rich on the Cook side and Frankfort on the Will side. The township matters when you look up an assessment or a past appeal, so note it from the parcel record before you call either county.

What do Tinley Park homes and households look like?

The Census Bureau's five-year survey results sketch a village of long-term owners, many of whom drive a long way to work.

  • Households that own: 86.9% of occupied homes
  • Middle value among owned homes: $299,900
  • Middle monthly rent, utilities included: $1,495
  • 22,320 households, about 2.45 people each
  • Household income at the midpoint: $105,189

Where does Tinley Park sit, and what is its housing stock?

The village borders Oak Forest to the northeast, Orland Park to the northwest, Orland Hills and Mokena to the west, Country Club Hills to the east, Matteson to the southeast and Frankfort to the southwest. Village government uses a council-manager structure.

Counting day in 2020 turned up 22,751 housing units, and 3.3% sat vacant. Within that, 1.1% of owner homes and 7.5% of rentals were empty. Residents had a median age of 43.0. Later survey work puts adult bachelor's attainment at 37.0% and the foreign-born share at 9.3%.

Shopping carries a lot of weight here: 2022 Census figures show about $1.81 billion in retail sales, roughly $33,380 for every resident, while health care and social services took in about $361 million.

How did Tinley Park grow?

Settlers arrived in the 1820s, and by the 1840s a large German community had formed, so the village took the name Bremen when it was founded in 1853. It was renamed Tinley Park in 1890 for the first station agent at the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific depot and incorporated on June 27, 1892.

The railroad drew a washing machine factory in 1905 and a cola bottling plant that ran into the 1950s. The big change came later: between 1970 and 1994, more than 11,000 housing units were built, mostly west and south of the original center. The village has since worked on its historic downtown, which follows the 1892 boundaries, and the outdoor amphitheater that opened in 1990 now holds about 28,000 people per event.

Which schools and commuter routes serve Tinley Park?

Four elementary districts cover the village: Kirby District 140, Community Consolidated District 146, Summit Hill District 161 and Elementary District 159. Victor J. Andrew High School in District 230 and Tinley Park High School in Bremen District 228 are both in the village, while small areas feed Lincoln-Way East and Rich Central. Residents are mostly in the Moraine Valley Community College district, with the rest in South Suburban College or Joliet Junior College territory.

Metra's Rock Island District has two stations here, Tinley Park on Oak Park Avenue and the 80th Avenue station. Pace runs routes 356, 364 and 386. The main roads are I-80 east to west, Harlem Avenue (IL 43) north to south, 159th Street (US 6) in the north and La Grange Road (US 45) at the western edge.

On the Will County side, the Treasurer explains that delinquent taxes become a lien that tax buyers purchase at an annual sale, and homeowners typically have one to three years to redeem before a buyer can start court action.

What does the Tinley Park Building Division require?

Most home improvements and additions call for building, electrical or plumbing permits, and the Building Division asks owners to call 708-444-5100 before starting if they are unsure. A homeowner may do work on their own property, with the exception that changing electric service needs a licensed electrical contractor. Any contractor the owner hires must be licensed and bonded with the village before work starts.

  • Apply with one copy of your plat of survey, normally provided at your closing, and any drawings or sketches.
  • Post the building permit placard at the site until the work is complete.
  • Starting without a permit can bring a fine.
  • The village's plan-review consultant does inspections on weekday mornings until noon.

The village notes that its comprehensive building code was revised and adopted on July 20, 2026, and lists the 2024 International codes among the current ones.

What if the Tinley Park mortgage is in default?

The Building Division page points to a Foreclosure Property Registration Program run through ProChamps, with a separate page for defaulted mortgage property registration. If a lender has started foreclosure on your home, ask the Building Division whether registration applies to you.

State law treats a few of these transfers differently. Under 765 ILCS 77/15, a borrower who hands the lender a deed in place of foreclosure, or who agrees to a consent judgment, is excused from the seller disclosure report. A regular sale still needs the report in the buyer's hands ahead of signing, as 765 ILCS 77/20 requires.

Investors who buy Tinley Park commercial space use a separate Change of Use/Owner application with a $50 fee, which does not apply to homes.

Which county does a Tinley Park address belong to?

Either one. The village covers parts of Cook and Will counties, and the county named on your bill decides which treasurer and which recording office you deal with.

They shift from year to year. The first installment fell on March 4 in 2025 and on April 1 in 2026, with the second on December 15, 2025 and October 1, 2026.

Most improvements and additions need a permit of some kind. Ring 708-444-5100 for the Building Division to confirm your project, and bring the plat of survey from your closing.

What if a Tinley Park owner gives the lender a deed in lieu?

The state exempts that kind of transfer from the seller disclosure report, though the deed itself still gets recorded at the county.

Title work, payoff letters and the agreed closing date set the pace. Without a mortgage there is no underwriting to wait on, and the county records the deed afterward.

What makes Berwyn different from other Chicago-area suburbs for sellers?

Berwyn is a dense inner-ring suburb in Cook County, packed into 3.90 square miles with Oak Park to the north, Cicero to the east, Stickney to the south, and Lyons, Riverside, North Riverside and Forest Park to the west. Its nickname is the City of Homes, and the housing reflects it: small bungalows on the north side around Roosevelt and Cermak roads, larger houses toward the south, and many duplexes and three-unit buildings scattered between.

The ground matters to anyone buying here. Before settlement the area was grassy marshland, with Mud Lake reaching nearly to today's southern border, and the south end flooded regularly in heavy rain during its early years. A sand and gravel beach ridge from ancient Lake Chicago runs along Riverside Drive. A buyer's inspector will look at basements and sewer laterals closely, so a seller with old flooding or backup history should gather repair records and any sewer scope reports before listing.

How dense and how costly is Berwyn housing?

Census Bureau estimates put Berwyn at 55,001 residents on July 1, 2025, down 3.9 percent from an April 2020 base of 57,235. Its density was 14,664.4 people per square mile in the 2020 count.

Households average 2.71 people, 62.8 percent of residents Hispanic or Latino and 25.0 percent foreign-born. Listings and disclosures that reach Spanish-speaking buyers and heirs are worth considering, since 53.5 percent of residents age five and older speak a language other than English at home.

What does the City of Berwyn require when a house changes hands?

Berwyn runs its own transfer paperwork through the Collections and Licensing office and the Compliance Department at City Hall, 6700 W. 26th Street. The city's checklist for quit claim transfers shows what the office looks at, and sellers on a regular sale should ask the same departments which items apply to them.

  • Building: a property inspection is required when all parties are coming off title, any fines or liens must be paid, and open permits must be closed out.
  • Police: parking tickets and fines must be paid in full.
  • Water: the water bill balance must be current.
  • Collector: bring the original deed that will be recorded with Cook County, the completed Berwyn Declaration form and a payment of $100.00, payable to the City of Berwyn by cash, check, money order or credit card.
  • Trusts and corporations: add the trust agreement or corporate papers only if the property is coming out of the trust or corporation, and add an Attorney's Certification form when someone is added to or removed from title.

City stamps are processed at the counter or by mail on four weekdays (Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday) between 9 a.m. and half past four, and on Tuesday until half past seven in the evening. Mailed packets need a return envelope with postage. The Compliance Department number is (708) 788-2660, extensions 6445 or 6449.

How does a Berwyn certificate of compliance and occupancy work?

Berwyn issues certificates of compliance and occupancy after a city inspection, and the fee depends on the type of property. For residential buildings the city's fee sheet lists $100.00 for a single-family house, $125.00 for two to three units, $175.00 for four to six units, and $70.00 for each unit over six.

Inspections are scheduled in person at the first-floor Compliance Department window in City Hall, with payment due when you schedule and no exceptions. Cash, check, money order and credit cards are accepted. An inspection report stays valid for six months from the inspection date, so time it close to your target closing rather than months ahead. The service window opens at 9 a.m. every weekday, closes at 5 p.m. on four of them, and stays open until 8 p.m. on Tuesdays.

Ask the Compliance Department whether your particular sale needs a certificate, because the answer can depend on the building type and who is on title. Buyers who plan to rehab a property often accept the inspection list as part of an as-is price.

What building permit rules should Berwyn sellers know?

The Building Permits Department says permits go out only until half past four on most weekdays and half past seven on Tuesdays. Applications can be submitted in person or emailed to buildingpermits@berwyn-il.gov, and incomplete applications are not sent for director review. Homeowners may do some non-commercial repairs themselves under the city's Work By Owner handout, but the city publishes guides on what needs a permit and on hiring contractors.

Codes the city lists as applicable include the 2024 International Residential Code, the 2012 International Property Maintenance Code, the Illinois State Plumbing Code 2014 and the 2021 Illinois Energy Conservation Code. If a prior owner finished a basement or added a bathroom without a permit, resolving it can take time, so ask for your address's permit file early.

What happens at the Cook County Clerk when a Berwyn deed is recorded?

Cook County deeds are recorded by the Clerk's Recording Division at 118 N. Clark Street, Room 120, in person or by mail. A deed needs the property index number (PIN), the full legal description, the property address, a mail-to address, the grantee's name and address, the name and address for future tax bills, and city, state and county transfer tax declarations and stamps or a stated exemption. The Clerk tells filers to check with the municipality for its own requirements, so Berwyn's own declaration and payment are a separate step before recording.

The Clerk's page prints the stamp history for Illinois: since September 15, 1989, stamps are $0.75 per $500.00, split into $0.50 for the state and $0.25 for the county. Only title companies may e-record deeds that carry consideration, while fully exempt deeds can be e-recorded by other filers. A document that misses the Clerk's format standards is charged an additional fee equal to the normal recording fee.

How do Cook County assessments and tax bills work for Berwyn homes?

Cook County reassesses one-third of the county each year, and a reassessment notice shows the PIN, characteristics, estimated market value and assessed value. The Assessor's page says residential assessed value equals 10 percent of fair market value, then a state equalizer and exemptions are applied. Appeals can be filed with the Assessor or the Cook County Board of Review.

The Cook County Treasurer mails two installments a year. The Treasurer's due-date page shows that tax year 2025 installments were due April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026, tax year 2024 installments were due March 4, 2025 and December 15, 2025, and tax year 2023 installments were due March 1, 2024 and August 1, 2024. The Assessor notes that the first installment is exactly 55 percent of the prior year's total. Because those dates move from year to year, read the Treasurer's page or your own bill before choosing a closing day. Exemptions listed by the Treasurer include homeowner, senior citizen, senior assessment freeze, persons with disabilities and home improvement.

Frequently asked questions

Does Berwyn require a city inspection to sell my house?

It depends on the transaction, so ask the Compliance Department at (708) 788-2660, extension 6445 or 6449. The city's quit claim checklist requires an inspection when all parties come off title, and its fee sheet lists certificates of compliance and occupancy at $100.00 for a single-family house.

How long is a Berwyn inspection report good for?

Six months from the inspection date. If closing slips past that window, plan on a new inspection and a new fee.

What is the transfer tax rate on a Cook County deed?

The Clerk's page prints $0.75 per $500.00 of value, made up of $0.50 for the state and $0.25 for the county. Berwyn adds its own declaration and a city payment, so ask the Collector's office what applies to your transaction.

Where do I pay water and parking fines before closing?

Contact the Water Department at (708) 788-2660, extension 6463 or 6466 for the balance, and the Police Department at (708) 795-5600 for parking tickets. The city's checklist says both must be current.

Can I sell a Berwyn house with open permits?

Open permits must be closed out for a transfer to be processed, according to the city's checklist. Ask the Building Department for the permit file, then decide whether to finish the work, credit the buyer or sell as-is to a buyer who will complete it.

What is different about selling a house in Wheaton?

Wheaton adds a city transfer stamp to every sale, and the buyer pays for it. The city also wants the seller's final utility bill settled before the stamp is issued, so the two sides of a closing depend on each other. Wheaton is the DuPage County seat and sits about 25 miles west of Chicago, in Milton and Winfield Townships.

The same rules apply whether the house is listed, sold privately or bought for cash as-is. What changes is who files the stamp application and how early the final water reading is booked.

How much is the Wheaton real estate transfer stamp?

The stamp costs $2.50 per $1,000 of full consideration, taken from line 11 of the Illinois MyDec PTAX-203 declaration, with the price rounded to the nearest thousand. The buyer, called the grantee, buys it. Illinois collects its own tax too, at half a dollar for each $500 of declared value (35 ILCS 200/31-10).

A buyer can get the stamp four ways, according to the city's Finance Department page:

  • Online through the transfer stamp portal, after creating an account.
  • By email to finance@wheaton.il.us.
  • By UPS or FedEx to the Finance Department at 303 W. Wesley St., Wheaton, IL 60187.
  • In person at City Hall, first floor.

Paper filings need a signed stamp application, a copy of the completed PTAX-203 or the deed, and a completed city utility account application form.

Which Wheaton transfers are exempt from the stamp tax?

Most Wheaton sales are non-exempt because they carry money. The city lists examples of exempt deeds, and the full list sits in City Code Chapter 66, Article VII, Section 66-190.

Common exemptions listed on the City of Wheaton transfer stamp page
Exempt situationNote
Transfer to or from a trustStill needs a $0 value stamp
Actual consideration under $100.00Same $0 stamp
Property acquired by or from a governmental bodyDocumentation required
Buyer sold a Wheaton primary home and is buying a new principal residence in WheatonExemption 13
Buyer is the natural or adopted child of a sellerExemption 14

An exempt stamp carries a $25 administrative fee and needs a signed, notarized deed. Since October 1, 2025 Wheaton no longer pays transfer tax refunds. Situations that once qualified for a refund are now handled as exemptions when the stamp is bought, so supporting documents must be ready on the closing timeline.

What must a Wheaton seller do before the stamp is issued?

The seller must call the city 5 to 7 days before closing to book a final water reading, at 630-260-2000 or waterbilling@wheaton.il.us. The final bill, or an estimate of it, then has to be paid in full. The city also checks for other unpaid charges.

  • Water, sanitary sewer and stormwater utility fees.
  • Inspection fees.
  • Building permit fees.
  • Property maintenance fines.

Because building permit fees and property maintenance fines are on the list, ask the city for a balance on your account a couple of weeks ahead and clear anything outstanding before the contract date.

What do Census numbers show for Wheaton housing?

The Census Bureau puts median home value at $455,700 for 2020 to 2024, with median gross rent of $1,799 and median household income of $120,008. Homeowners live in 71.7% of the housing, spread over 19,588 households averaging 2.54 people.

  • The July 2025 estimate is 54,065 residents, essentially level with the 2020 count of 53,970.

  • Around 86.4% of residents had the same address a year earlier.

How do property taxes work for a Wheaton seller?

Wheaton parcels are billed by DuPage County. Taxes arrive a year behind, so the bills mailed April 29, 2026 covered tax year 2025 and carried June 1 and September 1 installments, both now past. The general homestead and senior exemptions are each $8,000 on the county's current notice, and a seller should confirm both appear on the bill. For assessed value questions, the county treasurer points owners to the local assessor's number printed on the bill.

On the settlement statement the title company divides the unpaid tax for the year. State law also requires sellers of one to four residential units to hand over a completed disclosure report before a contract is signed (765 ILCS 77/20). For a rough house, that report is where known problems get written down.

What can slow down a Wheaton closing?

Most delays come from the utility step or from a missing exemption record. The city is firm that the transfer stamp cannot be issued until the final utility bill is paid, so a late call to the utility office can hold up the stamp and the recording that follows.

  • Booking the final water reading later than the 5 to 7 day window the city requests.
  • Forgetting that the buyer, not the seller, submits the PTAX-203 copy and the utility account application.
  • Claiming an exemption without a notarized deed or supporting documents.
  • Leaving building permit fees or property maintenance fines unpaid.
  • Counting on a refund after closing, which the city no longer issues.

Sellers who need to leave quickly, such as an estate heir or an owner relocating for work, should line up these items with the title company the week the contract is signed.

What shaped Wheaton and its neighborhoods?

The Wheaton brothers came from Connecticut, Warren laid claim to land in the center of town in 1837, and the place became a village on February 24, 1859, then a city on April 24, 1890. It won the county seat vote in 1867 by 1,686 to 1,635, and the 1887 courthouse is listed as a historic landmark at the federal level. The county moved its court complex about two miles west in 1990, and downtown has since added condominium and business projects.

Land area totals 11.32 square miles, and the city has been landlocked for decades. Most of it lies in Community Unit School District 200, feeding Wheaton North and Wheaton Warrenville South high schools, while the northeast corner is in Glen Ellyn District 41 and one elementary school in the southeast belongs to District 89. Wheaton College sits just east of downtown, and the city's 2025 financial report lists the DuPage County Government Center, District 200 and Wheaton College among its largest employers. The Union Pacific West Line runs through downtown, where the 758-unit Wheaton Center apartment complex with its two twenty-story towers is a recognizable landmark. The DuPage County Fairgrounds are in Wheaton as well, and the downtown business association runs seasonal events that bring foot traffic past listings in the center of town.

Frequently asked questions

Who pays the Wheaton transfer stamp, the buyer or the seller?

The buyer, also called the grantee, buys the stamp. The seller's job is to book the final water reading and pay the final utility bill, because the city will not issue the stamp until that bill is settled.

What is the Wheaton transfer stamp rate?

It is $2.50 per $1,000 of full consideration from line 11 of the PTAX-203, with the price rounded to the nearest thousand. Exempt deeds still need a $0 stamp and a $25 administrative fee.

How early should I schedule the final water reading in Wheaton?

Call 5 to 7 days before closing. The city's Finance Department takes requests at 630-260-2000 or waterbilling@wheaton.il.us, and the final bill must be paid before the stamp is issued.

Did Wheaton stop refunding transfer tax?

Yes, as of October 1, 2025. Buyers who would have qualified for a refund, such as a Wheaton homeowner moving to another Wheaton home or a child buying from a parent, now claim Exemption 13 or 14 when they apply for the stamp.

Which county handles property tax for Wheaton?

DuPage County. Its treasurer mails one bill with two installment coupons, and the 2025 bills were due June 1 and September 1, 2026. Both dates have passed, and the county bills a year in arrears.

Where is Normal and how did it get its name?

Normal is a town in McLean County, central Illinois, and it forms the Bloomington-Normal pair with its neighbor Bloomington. Its land area is about 18.3 square miles. The 2020 census counted 52,736 people, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 53,275.

The town was laid out on June 7, 1854 as North Bloomington. In 1865 it took the name Normal after Illinois State Normal University, the teacher-training school now called Illinois State University, and it was incorporated on February 25, 1867. Normal is the seventh largest Illinois community outside the Chicago metropolitan area.

Uptown Normal, built around a roundabout, holds the town hall, the Amtrak station, the Children's Discovery Museum, hotels and the restored Normal Theater. The original town was laid out mostly south of the rail lines, and the major retail center is on Veterans Parkway on the east side.

How much does Illinois State University shape the Normal housing market?

It is a major driver. Illinois State University, founded in 1857 as the first public university in the state, has a 350-acre campus in town, and Heartland Community College, founded in 1990, adds more students. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures show the effect:

MeasureNormal

Only about 55% of housing units are owner-occupied, and a quarter of residents moved within the past year. Rentals are a normal part of the market here, and Normal's rules for rental licenses and short-term stays come up in many sales.

Does Normal require a license for rental property?

Yes, for multi-family rentals. Section 11.8-1 of the Town code, as posted by the Town, says no one may operate an apartment, rooming house, multiple-use dwelling, hotel, motel, bed and breakfast or duplex (except the owner-occupied side) without a rental occupancy license issued by the Building Commissioner.

  • Licenses run January 1 through December 31 of a year.
  • A license belongs to one owner and one property and cannot be transferred without a transfer fee and a completed application from the new owner.
  • The code lists a change of owner as one reason a license may be revoked.
  • An inspection takes place before any license is issued, and the owner must give the Town access to the units. A tenant or owner who refuses can face a search warrant request.
  • Appeals of a refusal or revocation go to the Building Commissioner within 30 days.
  • Penalties run from $25 to $200 for a first offense and $50 to $500 for later ones, with each day counted as a separate offense.

An owner selling a duplex or small apartment building should tell the buyer that the license does not move with the deed. The Inspections Department is at 1 Uptown Circle, phone 309-454-9581.

What are Normal's short-term rental rules for a seller or buyer?

Short-term rentals in Normal need a Town business license. On June 16, 2025 the Town Council passed Ordinance 6028 on short-term rental licensing. The Town's business license page also says STRs are prohibited in R-1 and R-2 zoning unless the property is the owner-occupant's primary residence.

  • In R-1 zoning, no more than 2 unrelated people, or 1 family plus 1 unrelated person, may stay.
  • In R-2 and R-3 zoning, the limit is 4 unrelated people.
  • Parking is allowed only on hard surfaces, and street parking is capped at 24 hours unless a sign says otherwise.
  • Parties, meetings and other events are not allowed.
  • The Short-Term Rental Tax form and payment are due by the 25th of the month after collection.

The business license itself carries no fee, but the Town issues it only after taxes and debts owed to the Town are paid. If you are selling a house that has been used as an STR, ask the Town how the license and any tax account will be handled so the buyer does not inherit a balance.

How are deeds recorded in McLean County?

The McLean County Clerk's Recording Division records them, at 115 E. Washington Street, Room M104, in Bloomington. The phone is 309-888-5170 and the office is open Monday through Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm. Voters moved the old Recorder's duties into the County Clerk's office by referendum on November 6, 2012, effective December 31, 2013.

The county lists what every deed must include:

  • A statement of exemption or a transfer tax declaration.
  • The name of the person who prepared it.
  • Where future tax statements are to be sent.
  • A notary seal, date and signature, with original signatures; photocopies and digital signatures are not accepted.
  • A complete legal description with the permanent index number.
  • A complete return address.

The recorder's staff cannot give legal advice or legal descriptions, so have the deed prepared by an attorney or title company.

What does the Rivian plant mean for homes in Normal?

It has changed the local job picture. Diamond-Star Motors, a Mitsubishi and Chrysler venture, opened a manufacturing plant in Normal in 1986. Mitsubishi closed it on May 31, 2016, and Rivian bought it in January 2017. Rivian has built all-electric vehicles there since 2021, and the plant is the company's largest in the United States.

Interstates 55, 74 and 39 serve the town, and I-39 ends at Normal. U.S. 51, U.S. 150, Illinois Route 9 and historic Route 66 pass through. The Amtrak station at 11 Uptown Circle has four Lincoln Service trains a day in each direction between Chicago and St. Louis, and Connect Transit runs 16 fixed routes. Central Illinois Regional Airport is just over the line in Bloomington, about five miles from Uptown.

Which schools serve Normal addresses?

The town sits inside McLean County Unit District No. 5, which runs Normal Community High School, Normal Community West High School and Kingsley Junior High School. Illinois State University operates two schools of its own, University High School and Thomas Metcalf Elementary. Private options include Epiphany Catholic School, Calvary Christian Academy, Cornerstone Christian Academy and Bloom Community School.

Census data show that 97.6% of adults age 25 and older have a high school diploma and 52.9% hold a bachelor's degree or higher. The average trip to work takes 16.5 minutes.

How does Normal weather affect an older house?

The 1991 to 2020 NOAA normals show about 39.4 inches of precipitation a year, 20.1 inches of snow and 113 days with measurable precipitation. Summer highs average 86 degrees Fahrenheit in July, while January lows average about 16. The record high is 114 and the record low is minus 24.

That range is hard on roofs, gutters, window seals and furnaces. If your house is older, a recent roof receipt or a furnace service record answers some of the first questions a buyer's inspector will ask.

Can I sell a Normal rental property to another landlord?

Yes. The rental occupancy license is specific to one owner and one property, so the buyer applies in their own name, pays a transfer fee and passes an inspection. Ask the Inspections Department at 309-454-9581 how that will be handled before closing.

Where do I record a deed for a Normal house?

At the McLean County Clerk's Recording Division, 115 E. Washington Street, Room M104, Bloomington, phone 309-888-5170. The deed needs a transfer tax declaration or exemption statement, original notarized signatures and a full legal description with the permanent index number.

Are short-term rentals allowed in Normal?

They are allowed with a Town business license, but not in R-1 or R-2 zoning unless the property is the owner's primary residence. The Town adopted Ordinance 6028 on June 16, 2025, and guest limits depend on the zoning district.

What do Census figures say about home values in Normal?

The Census Bureau's median value of an owner-occupied home is $213,600 for 2020 to 2024. The town has a 54.8% owner-occupied rate, a $965 median gross rent and a median household income of $64,785.

How long is the commute from Normal to work?

The Census Bureau puts the mean travel time to work at 16.5 minutes for 2020 to 2024. Interstates 55, 74 and 39 serve the town, and Connect Transit runs 16 fixed routes.

What are the ways to sell a house in Oak Park, Illinois?

Oak Park owners choose between an agent listing, a sale they run themselves, and an offer from a buyer who pays cash and takes the building in its present condition. Which one fits depends mostly on the condition of the building and how soon the money is needed.

Oak Park is a village of 4.70 square miles that sits against the west edge of Chicago, so buyers here compare it with city neighborhoods as much as with other suburbs. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 52,823 residents, a drop from the 54,583 counted in 2020.

  • An agent listing suits a house that shows well, with updated systems and a seller who can stay out of the way during showings.
  • A sale handled by the owner suits someone who already knows the block, can price the house, and is comfortable reading a contract.
  • A cash sale suits a house with deferred work, a tenant in place, or an estate where heirs live elsewhere. Compare any figure with what a repaired and listed house would net after commission and carrying costs.

How does Oak Park's older housing stock affect a sale?

Most Oak Park houses date from before 1950, and some sit inside a historic district, which shapes both repairs and buyer interest. The village's historical society is quoted as saying that almost all of the housing stock went up between 1892 and 1950.

Oak Park separated from Cicero in 1902 after a referendum, and by 1930 the population stood near 64,000, above the 2025 Census estimate. Frank Lloyd Wright settled here in 1889 and built homes and Unity Temple before he left in 1911, so the village holds the largest collection of Wright-designed residences in the world. Hemingway was born here and spent his first six years at 339 N. Oak Park Ave., which is open for tours.

A preservation ordinance has been in force since 1972 and has been revised since. The village counts about 2,400 historic sites, mostly Queen Anne, Prairie School and Craftsman homes, and it recognizes three historic districts: Frank Lloyd Wright, Ridgeland-Oak Park, and Seward Gunderson. Ask the village's historic preservation staff whether your address falls inside a district before you plan exterior work, a window swap or a porch repair ahead of a sale. A buyer's inspector will also look closely at original wood windows, plaster, wiring and older masonry, so a seller should expect those items to come up in negotiation.

Where is Oak Park, and how do buyers get around from here?

Oak Park lies directly west of Chicago, bounded by Austin Boulevard on the east, North Avenue on the north, Roosevelt Road on the south and Harlem Avenue on the west. Its neighbors are Chicago, River Forest, Forest Park, Berwyn and Cicero.

Commuting is a large part of the pitch to buyers. Five CTA stations serve the village on the Green Line and Blue Line, there is a Metra Union Pacific West Line station downtown, and CTA and Pace buses fill in the rest. The Eisenhower Expressway runs along the south end and leads to O'Hare. Census data for 2020-2024 give an average commute of 31.6 minutes.

Oak Park also uses its own street-numbering system. East-west numbers begin at Austin Boulevard, and north-south numbers start at the elevated tracks just south of Lake Street. Border streets such as Austin and North Avenue match the Chicago grid, which is worth remembering when you check an address on a listing or a tax bill.

Which schools serve Oak Park houses?

Oak Park Elementary School District 97 serves the whole village, and Oak Park and River Forest High School, the single school in District 200, serves it. Fenwick High School is a Catholic college preparatory option run by the Dominicans.

District 97 runs eight primary schools, Lincoln, Mann, Longfellow, Beye, Irving, Holmes, Whittier and Hatch, plus Percy Julian Middle School and Gwendolyn Brooks Middle School. Because the school district boundary and the village boundary line up, buyers rarely need to ask which district applies. The high school district also draws on neighboring River Forest, so the tax bill for an Oak Park parcel includes several separate taxing bodies: the township, the high school district, the elementary district, the library district and the park district.

What does the Village of Oak Park require when a house is sold?

The seller must buy real estate transfer stamps from the Finance Department before the transfer can be completed. The village prices the stamps at $8 per thousand, or fraction thereof, of the full actual contract price, and the fee for an exempt transfer is $30.

The process runs in a set order, and skipping a step delays the closing.

  • Email the paperwork to waterbilling@oak-park.us for review before you go in to buy a stamp, including the completed Real Estate Transfer Tax Declaration Form.
  • An exempt stamp for a transfer with no sale needs the original signed and notarized deed plus the statement by grantor and grantee. Photocopies are refused.
  • For a condominium that shares a water meter billed to the association, file the Condominium Association Water and Sewer Charges Affidavit or a paid-assessment letter.
  • Order a final water reading by calling 708.358.5478 at least 72 hours before you plan to buy the stamps. No stamp is issued until every village utility charge is paid.

The village accepts a cashier's check, certified check, money order, MasterCard, Visa or Discover for utility charges. Personal checks are not taken. Your title company or attorney usually coordinates this, but confirm who is doing it so the stamp is not forgotten on closing day.

How do Cook County property taxes and reassessment affect an Oak Park sale?

Oak Park is in Cook County, which reassesses homes on a three-year cycle, and Oak Park Township is in the group reassessed in 2023 and 2026. The Cook County Assessor lists the Oak Park Township assessor at 105 S. Oak Park Ave., phone (708) 383-8005, for owners who want help reading a notice.

Tax bills come in two installments. For tax year 2025 the first installment was due April 1, 2026 and the second was due October 1, 2026, according to the Cook County Treasurer. Earlier years ran on different dates, for example March 4 and December 15 for tax year 2024, so the calendar can shift when bills are delayed. Ask the Treasurer for the current due date and for a copy of your bill, and ask your closing agent how the current year's tax will be split between you and the buyer.

What should an owner know about selling an Oak Park house with tenants?

Roughly half of Oak Park's approximately 26,000 residential addresses are in multifamily buildings, so a sale with renters in place is common here. The village's Community Relations Division publishes landlord and tenant guidance, and the leases already signed will matter to any buyer.

  • Apartments in buildings of four or more units need a written lease.
  • A landlord must hold at least one month's rent as a security deposit, and deposits in buildings with four or more apartments earn interest when held more than six months.
  • After a tenant moves out the deposit is due back within 45 days, or 60 days if a repair estimate is sent within 30 days.
  • For unpaid rent the landlord gives a written five-day notice before filing in court.

The village's guidance also sets minimum heat of 68 degrees from 6:30 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 65 degrees overnight. Call the Community Relations Division at 708.358.5405 with questions about local rules.

Census figures show 60.0% owner occupancy, which leaves a large renter share, and a typical owner-reported value of $465,500.

Who pays the transfer stamp when a house sells in Oak Park?

The seller buys the village stamps. Oak Park charges $8 per thousand, or fraction thereof, of the full actual contract price, and exempt transfers cost $30. The final water bill must be paid first.

Can I sell an Oak Park house that is inside a historic district?

Yes. A historic district does not stop a sale. It affects exterior changes, so ask the village's historic preservation staff before you plan repairs, and tell your buyer which of the three districts, if any, covers the property.

How soon should I order the final water reading?

Call 708.358.5478 at least 72 hours before you intend to purchase the transfer stamps. The final bill is prepared at that point, and the stamps are withheld until all utility charges are settled.

Does Oak Park reassess homes every year?

No. Cook County reassesses on a three-year cycle, and Oak Park Township falls in the 2023 and 2026 group. Between those years the assessment can still change through appeals or exemptions, so read each bill.

What if my Oak Park house has a tenant on a lease?

The lease and the security deposit stay important to the sale. Oak Park requires a written lease in buildings of four or more units and sets deposit return at 45 days after move-out, so gather those documents before you accept an offer.

Where is Hoffman Estates, Illinois, and where did the village come from?

Hoffman Estates is a village in the northwest suburbs, mostly in Cook County with a very small part in Kane County. Of its 21.07 square miles, nearly all is dry land, and mail is delivered under ZIP codes 60169, 60010 and 60192.

German settlers had farmed the area west of Roselle Road and north of Golf Road, then called Wildcat Grove. In 1954 Sam and Jack Hoffman, a father and son who ran a construction company, bought 160 acres and began building homes. Residents voted to incorporate, and the village was incorporated on September 23, 1959. Annexations north of the Northwest Tollway in the early 1960s more than doubled its land area.

The village had 22,238 people in 1970 and 52,530 in the 2020 census. The count rose from 8,296 in 1960 to 46,363 in 1990, so many houses are several decades old, and a buyer will ask how old the roof, furnace and windows are.

What do federal housing figures say about Hoffman Estates?

50,858 residents in mid-2025, which is 3.2 percent below the April 2020 base. The 2020 to 2024 survey counts 18,537 households of about 2.75 people each. Of the homes, 74.2 percent are owned, and those owners report a median value of $351,900. Renters pay a median gross rent of $1,734, and the middle household income is $106,806.

Two other numbers stand out: 35.4 percent of residents were born abroad, and 46.4 percent of people 5 and older use a non-English language at home. In the year before the survey, 90.5 percent stayed at one address.

  • Just over a quarter of homes have renters, so investor-owned and tenant-occupied houses come up in sales.
  • With so many languages spoken, translated showing instructions and listing documents can help.
  • The 2020 count listed 19,160 housing units, and 3.5 percent were vacant.

What jobs and businesses drive the local economy?

The Prairie Stone Business Park, a 750-acre planned district bounded by Illinois Route 59, Interstate 90, Illinois Route 72 and Beverly Road, anchors the village's employment. It took shape after Sears relocated its headquarters there in 1993, and it later added the 11,000-seat NOW Arena, a Marriott hotel and the Poplar Creek Crossing retail center. The Village took over the arena in 2011, and it is home to the Windy City Bulls of the NBA G League. The park also holds a Northern Illinois University branch, a health and wellness center and offices for companies such as Serta, Mary Kay and I-CAR.

A 2023 list of top local employers starts with St. Alexius Medical Center at 2,500 workers, then Siemens Medical Systems and Claire's at 400 each, the Village itself at 370, and FANUC America and Vistex at 350 each. Many Japanese companies also base their U.S. headquarters in Hoffman Estates and neighboring Schaumburg.

A transfer or job change can force a quick sale. Commutes average 28.5 minutes, and Woodfield Mall in neighboring Schaumburg, opened in 1971, turned the area into a major business center.
