Which county records a Hanover Park deed?

Hanover Park lies in both Cook and DuPage counties, so the recorder depends on where your parcel is. Your tax bill or title commitment shows the county and the parcel number.

For Cook County parcels, the Cook County Clerk's recordings office requires the preparer's and mail-to names and addresses, the common address, the Property Index Number and a legal description. A deed also needs grantor and grantee names and addresses, a completed MyDec declaration and any municipal transfer tax, which in Hanover Park is the stamp described above. An exemption statement is added where one applies.

For DuPage parcels, the DuPage County Recorder asks for a completed deed, the PTAX form or an exemption statement, municipal transfer stamps if applicable, the grantee's name and address for tax bills, the permanent parcel number, the legal description and the preparer's name and address. The DuPage office accepts PTAX-203 forms completed in MyDec and supports eRecording through several vendors. Title companies usually take care of these filings.

Where did Hanover Park come from?

Hanover Park is a Chicago suburb of about 6.5 square miles. Its oldest roots are in Ontarioville, where a stagecoach line ran along Lake Trail, later Lake Street, to Galena starting in 1836. In 1872 the Chicago & Pacific Railroad laid tracks on land Edwin Bartlett donated for a depot. He renamed his station Ontario in 1873 to avoid confusion with Luther Bartlett's station, and a post office opened that year.

Ontarioville was folded into the surrounding village of Hanover Park in 1982. Today the Ontarioville neighborhood sits south of U.S. Route 20, near County Farm Road and Ontarioville Road, and Metra's Hanover Park station on the Milwaukee District West Line runs alongside Ontarioville Road. The station is in fare zone 4, and Pace Route 554 reaches Elgin and Schaumburg.

What do the numbers say about Hanover Park housing?

The Census Bureau estimated 36,568 residents on July 1, 2025, down from the 37,470 counted in 2020. The village is dense, with 5,834.6 people per square mile in 2020, and it has large households.

The 2020 census found a median age of 35.0, and 43.3 percent of households had children under 18. Of the 11,732 housing units, 2.8 percent were vacant.

Census data also show that 37.5 percent of residents were born abroad and 57.8 percent speak a language other than English at home, so translated or plain-language paperwork helps many sellers. The village's labor force participation is 68.2 percent, the mean commute is 29.1 minutes, and the share of people without health insurance under 65 is 13.5 percent. About 91.5 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which points to long tenure in many homes.

Which school districts serve Hanover Park?

Several districts overlap here, and six different public high schools serve the village. Elgin Area School District U-46 is the largest, covering about 90 square miles across Cook, DuPage and Kane counties and nearly 40,000 students.

  • Schaumburg Township Elementary District 54
  • Township High School District 211
  • Community Consolidated School District 93
  • Glenbard Township High School District 87
  • Keeneyville School District 20
  • Lake Park High School District 108

Your address determines the district, and buyers who have children check this first. The Hanover Park Park District, created by voters in 1964, runs the parks, and library service comes from the Poplar Creek Public Library District or the Schaumburg Township District Library depending on the part of town.

What if the Hanover Park house is a rental?

The Village licenses all residential rental properties, and the Code Enforcement Unit inspects them. An owner needs to pass an inspection and attend a landlord training seminar before being licensed. The Crime Free Multi-Housing Program requires landlords to attend training and use a crime free lease addendum.

If you are selling a rented house, ask Code Enforcement at 630-823-5570 about the license and any open violations before you list. You can report a problem on the 24 hour hotline at 630-823-5572, and an officer usually investigates within 24 to 48 hours. Building permits for work on the property come from the Community Development Department, not Code Enforcement.

Frequently asked questions

Do I have to buy a transfer stamp to sell my Hanover Park house?

Yes. The Village requires all home sellers to buy a Transfer Tax Stamp before closing. Call Finance at 630-823-5790 at least three business days ahead.

What blocks the stamp in Hanover Park?

Unpaid money owed to the Village. Tickets, invoices, liens, judgments and the final water bill must all be paid before the stamp is issued.

Does a quitclaim deed need the stamp?

Yes. The Village says a quitclaim deed requires a stamp, and it asks for a copy of the signed, notarized deed with its transfer tax declaration form.

Which county records my Hanover Park deed?

Cook County or DuPage County, depending on where the parcel sits. The village spans both, so check your tax bill or title paperwork.

When are Hanover Park water bills due?

On or before the 21st of each month. A balance unpaid by then gets a 10 percent penalty, so clear it before you request the transfer stamp.

Which sale method makes sense for a Rock Island owner?

Owners here can hire an agent to list the house, market it themselves, or accept an offer from a buyer paying cash who is willing to take the property as it is. Repairs, timing and whether the building is a home or a rental drive the choice.

Rock Island is one of the Quad Cities, alongside Moline and East Moline in Illinois and Davenport and Bettendorf in Iowa, so the buyer pool crosses the river. A tidy house can do well on the open market. One that needs work, carries a tenant or sits on a rental-heavy block may be better matched to a direct sale. Weigh these points:

  • Putting the house on the market reaches the most shoppers, though repairs and open-house hours usually come with it.
  • Selling privately skips the agent's commission and leaves marketing, paperwork and negotiation to you.
  • A direct purchase for cash can close without a lender's appraisal, which keeps the schedule in your hands.
  • If the property is a rental, the city's rental license and inspection rules may come into play first.

Whichever way you go, have the price, closing date and cost split in writing before you commit.

What is the Rock Island housing picture in the Census data?

Home prices in Rock Island run modest. The five-year Census survey ending in 2024 puts the middle value of a house occupied by its owner at $125,900, and roughly 35 percent of occupied units are rented.

The 2010 census counted 39,018 residents, and the count has slipped since. In a market like this, many sellers are landlords or heirs and many buyers are local investors. A rental should be priced with area rents in mind, because an investor works backward from what tenants pay, and the middle gross rent is $842.

How do the rivers, the Arsenal and the neighborhoods shape a Rock Island sale?

The city sits where the Rock River meets the Mississippi, and Arsenal Island, the original Rock Island, lies in the Mississippi between Rock Island and Davenport. Rock Island Arsenal is the largest government-owned weapons manufacturing arsenal in the United States and employs about 6,000 people, so the base accounts for a large part of the local job market.

The city's older pockets each have their own character:

  • Downtown and the Broadway Historic District, with well-preserved late 1800s and early 1900s buildings.
  • Watch Hill and the southern part of the city, once the separate community of Searstown and annexed in 1915.
  • The blocks around Augustana College, which was founded in 1860.
  • Streets near the Mississippi riverfront, home to Schwiebert Riverfront Park and a casino.

Rock Island is also an old rail town. The Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad was founded here in 1851. Bridges cross to Davenport, including the Government Bridge, the Centennial Bridge and the Interstate 280 bridge, and Quad Cities MetroLINK buses use District Station downtown as a hub.

Which employers and schools matter to Rock Island buyers?

In its 2017 annual financial report the city ranked Rock Island Arsenal first with 6,301 employees, ahead of Trinity Rock Island with 1,848 and Rock Island-Milan School District 41 with 1,292. County government, Jumer's Casino and Hotel, Augustana College and Modern Woodmen of America each employ several hundred more.

District 41, Rock Island-Milan, covers the bulk of the city with 13 public schools, among them Rock Island High School. Some southwest addresses belong to Rockridge. Jordan Catholic Elementary School and Alleman Catholic High School serve private-school families.

An address close to a district line deserves a call to the district before you advertise it. Plenty of shoppers narrow their search by school district before they look at streets.

What is Rock Island's history, and how does it show in older houses?

The oldest part of the city was called Farnhamsburg, after homes built in 1826 by two trading partners. A plat was filed in 1835 under the name Stephenson, and the town took the name Rock Island in March 1841. The Rock Island Arsenal has produced equipment for the U.S. Army since the 1880s and was established in 1862, and it is a National Historic Landmark.

Two hotels, the Harper House and the Rock Island House, opened during the late 1800s. Chippiannock Cemetery dates to 1854, and the public library was established in 1872. A new Rock Island County courthouse was built from 2017 to 2018 at a cost of $28 million. These details matter to a seller mostly because they show how much of the city dates from the 1800s and early 1900s. Older houses can carry original wiring, plaster and stone foundations, and a buyer will want to know what has been updated.

What does Rock Island require for rental properties before a sale?

City ordinance calls for a rental license on every residential rental, and each unit has to pass an inspection against a minimum code standard before it is offered to tenants. Landlords apply through the city's self-service portal, and the Inspection Division sends an email to schedule the inspection after the rental fee is paid.

Inspections are scheduled with the owner or a designated agent, who must be present, and a cancellation fee of $50 applies if the owner does not appear or cancel 24 hours ahead. A Notice of Violation lists items that fail life safety requirements. The first re-inspection is free, and additional compliance inspections cost $50 each. The city can fine owners and revoke the license if repairs are not made in a reasonable time.

A license does not release the owner from fixing violations. Planning to sell a rental? Clear any open violations or tell the buyer about them, and ask the Inspection Division at 1528 Third Avenue where your license stands before you list.

How is a Rock Island deed recorded and which transfers are exempt from tax?

Deeds for Rock Island parcels are recorded with the Rock Island County Recorder. The office's fee schedule, set by county ordinance effective February 1, 2025, lists $83 for a conforming document with no page count, $64 for certain exempt document types, and $104 for a non-conforming document or one with more than five references. Any document with a legal description also needs the 10-digit PIN.

The state transfer tax statute exempts a list of transfers from the tax, and some of them still require the declaration to be filed. Section 31-45 of the Property Tax Code lists these among the exempt items: deeds where the actual consideration is less than $100, tax deeds, deeds of partition, deeds that only correct or confirm an earlier deed, deeds to or from government bodies and charities, and deeds given to a mortgage holder after foreclosure or as a substitute for it. A normal sale to a buyer does not fall in these categories.

Rock Island County offers a no-cost Property Fraud Alert subscription that sends a notice whenever a filing mentions you. Someone leaving a house empty for a while may want to enroll first.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a city rental license in order to sell a rented Rock Island house?

The license applies to renting a unit, so selling does not need one. Open inspection violations on a rented house can still slow a sale, so ask the Inspection Division where your file stands.

How much do Rock Island houses cost?

The survey figure for the middle owner-occupied home is $125,900. An individual house can land far above or below it, depending on size, condition and block.

Where is a Rock Island deed recorded?

Rock Island County. Its Recorder's Office lists conforming documents at $83 and non-conforming documents at $104 under a fee schedule effective February 1, 2025. Confirm the current figure before closing.

What school district is my Rock Island house in?

Rock Island-Milan School District 41 covers most addresses. A few in the southwest belong to Rockridge, so verify yours with the district.

How large is Rock Island?

About 36,225 people lived here in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate. Rock Island holds the county seat and counts among the Quad Cities.

Who lives in Addison, and what are the homes like?

Addison is a DuPage County village where most sales involve a suburban house or condo that must clear a short list of village steps before the deed can move. Census estimators counted 35,758 people on July 1, 2025, a hair above the 35,702 recorded in 2020, so the housing stock is stable and fully built out.

The village sits on Salt Creek, a tributary of the Des Plaines River, and covers roughly ten square miles. It was first called Dunkley's Grove and was incorporated in 1884. Most of the houses date from the stretch after 1960, when developers turned farmland into subdivisions and the population jumped from 6,741 in 1960 to 24,482 in 1970. Most sellers here are marketing a house from that postwar and later building era.

The economy leans on freight and distribution. Census figures show 2022 transportation and warehousing receipts of $508,509 thousand in Addison, far above the $112,946 thousand recorded for restaurants and lodging. The village describes its economy as logistics, manufacturing and food distribution close to the interstates and O'Hare.

  • Home value among owners, 2020 to 2024 survey: $341,300
  • Share of homes lived in by owners: 67.0%
  • Typical monthly gross rent: $1,245
  • Median household income: $90,431
  • Households: 12,832, with a mean commute of 25.6 minutes

Which village steps must be finished before an Addison sale can close?

Addison will not issue a real estate transfer stamp until the sewer, permit, water and paperwork items on the Community Development and Finance pages are cleared. The village page says the deed cannot be transferred before the stamp is issued, so a missed item can delay the closing date.

  • Sewer compliance: the certificate cannot be older than six months on closing day, and the village wants the inspection booked a fortnight early through Community Development at (630) 693-7530.
  • Permit release: confirms no open building permits or unpaid inspection fees. A release stays valid for two months only.
  • Water: the seller books a final meter reading, done 24 hours before closing, and pays the final bill by noon the business day before closing. The buyer pre-registers for the water and sewer account.
  • Paperwork: the seller's attorney sends the village a copy of the PTAX-203 or PTAX-203A and a copy of the drafted deed.

Condominiums skip the water account and the sewer or sump inspection. The only requirement for a condo is the permit release.

Addison transfer stamp amounts as printed on the village real estate transfers page
ItemAmount shown by the villageWho pays
Standard transfer stamp$2.50 for each $1,000 of purchase priceBuyer
Exempt transfer stamp (quitclaim, trust, foreclosure, sheriff sale)$50 administrative feeParty requesting the stamp
Transfer of beneficial interest$1.25 per $500 block, rounded upParty transferring

Source: Village of Addison, Real Estate Transfers.

Does a quitclaim deed or foreclosure transfer still need an Addison stamp?

Yes. The village issues a zero-dollar exempt stamp for quitclaim deeds, deeds into a trust, foreclosures and sheriff sales, and it still charges the $50 processing fee. A lost stamp has to be repurchased in full, so keep the original with the closing file.

The exempt stamp needs the same sewer inspection, permit release and final water bill as a sale. The village also asks for its own Certificate of Exemption form and a copy of the signed and notarized deed. When the owner name on the deed is changing, the new owner must open a water and sewer account with two forms of identification. When the name is not changing, the water balance simply has to be paid before the stamp is released.

Heirs deeding an inherited Addison house should plan on the same items, even though no sale tax is due. Starting the sewer appointment early is the best way to protect the closing date.

What rules apply to an Addison house that is rented out?

Every Addison dwelling that is not owner-occupied and charges rent needs an annual Residential Rental License. The license year runs May 1 to April 30, renewal notices go out by mail in March, and renewals are due by April 30.

The village counts more than 1,000 licensed rental properties and nearly 4,000 rental units, and it grades each property after an annual inspection. In a single-family house, condo or townhouse the inspector walks the interior. In a multi-family building the village inspects 20 percent of the units plus the common areas. Owners must also attend an 8-hour Crime Free Multi-Housing class within 90 days of getting a license.

Addison bans short-term rentals outright and classes them as a nuisance, which matters to a buyer planning to put the house on a booking site. A landlord selling a licensed rental can email Rentals@addison-il.org or call the Rental Housing Supervisor line at (630) 693-7544 to ask how an open license year is handled at closing.

How does DuPage County bill property tax on an Addison home?

DuPage County sends one bill with two installment coupons, and the tax covers the prior year. For 2025 taxes, bills went out on April 29, 2026, with payments due on the first of June and the first of September. The DuPage County Treasurer at 630-407-5900 can confirm the dates for the next cycle.

Addison spans Addison and Bloomingdale townships, so the township assessor named on the bill is the first contact for valuation questions. The treasurer's office says it does not set values. It also warns that a yellow box on the bill means a mortgage servicer is already paying, and a second payment would later have to be refunded.

  • The treasurer puts both the general homestead exemption and the senior exemption at $8,000.
  • Preliminary county figures for the 2025 levy showed assessed value up 8.2%, the average tax rate down 4.37% and the overall bill up 3.83%.
  • Individual bills differ by parcel because each one falls in a different mix of school, park and fire districts.

Because the bill arrives a year behind, ask the title officer how the current year's tax and any unpaid installment will be settled between buyer and seller.

Can an Addison owner appeal an assessment before listing?

An owner can file with the DuPage County Board of Review, but only inside the 30-day window that opens when the township roll is published. Section 16-55 of the Property Tax Code sets the deadline at 30 calendar days after publication, and the county says talking with the township assessor does not extend it.

DuPage asks for three or more comparable properties, with recent sales as the strongest evidence. Assessed values rest on the three prior years of sales, so the 2025 value drew on sales from 2022 through 2024. Written decisions usually arrive the following March. An owner who disagrees can go on to the state Property Tax Appeal Board or to court. An appeal challenges the assessed value only, and the tax rate stays with the local taxing districts.

What state transfer tax and declaration apply to an Addison sale?

Under Section 31-10 of the Property Tax Code the state levies 50 cents on every $500 block of value stated on the transfer declaration. When the deed says the property passes subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage balance is left out of the basis.

The declaration is filed on Form PTAX-203 or through the Department of Revenue's free MyDec system. Addison also wants its own copy of that form before it releases the village stamp, so the seller's attorney should send it to the water billing email listed on the village page.

What do Addison buyers look at beyond the house itself?

Buyers usually compare the school pattern, the commute and the age of the home. Addison Trail High School and Indian Trail Junior High anchor the public school map, and the elementary schools include Ardmore, Wesley, Lake Park, Fullerton, Army Trail, Lincoln and Stone. St. Philip the Apostle offers private Catholic schooling from pre-kindergarten through eighth grade.

Pace buses on Routes 711 and 715 connect Addison with Wheaton and other points. The average commute is 25.6 minutes, and 93.0% of residents had not moved in the previous year, which points to long ownership.

Addison owners can hire an agent, go it alone, or sell to a buyer who accepts the house in its current condition. A cash buyer still needs the same sewer certificate, permit release and final water bill, so the village timetable applies on every route. Owners with inherited, tenant-occupied or heavily worn houses often choose the as-is route because repairs would otherwise be negotiated after the buyer's inspection.

How far ahead should I book the Addison sewer inspection?

Call Community Development at (630) 693-7530 and set the appointment a minimum of two weeks ahead. The certificate it produces must carry a date within six months of closing.

Who pays the Addison real estate transfer stamp?

The buyer. The village page calls the purchase of the stamp the buyer's responsibility and prints the standard rate as $2.50 for each $1,000 of purchase price.

Do condos in Addison need a sewer inspection?

No. The village says condos do not schedule the water and sewer account or the sewer and sump pump inspection. A permit release is the only requirement.

Can a buyer run an Addison house as a short-term rental?

No. Addison prohibits short-term rentals and treats them as a nuisance. Long-term rentals need the annual Residential Rental License and an inspection.

What were the DuPage County property tax installment dates?

The 2025 taxes came due in two parts, on the first of June and the first of September 2026. The DuPage County Treasurer can confirm the dates on the next bill, and check whether a mortgage servicer already pays your taxes before sending money.

What should a Northbrook homeowner know before selling?

Northbrook is one of the simpler Cook County villages to sell in on paper, because it charges no municipal transfer tax and issues no transfer stamps. The one local step is closing out the water account with a final meter reading.

The village sits on the North Shore in Cook County, spreads over about 13 square miles, and borders Lake County to the north. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 34,744 residents. What is Northbrook like for sellers and buyers?

Northbrook began as Shermerville, named for the man who gave land for its first railroad station, and took its present name in 1923. It was incorporated in 1901. The population climbed from 3,319 in 1950 to 30,735 by 1980, and the last working farm closed in 1987. The village was also the first community without a Lake Michigan shoreline to filter lake water for public use.

  • Several elementary districts, numbered 27, 28, 30 and 31, serve the village, and High School District 225 feeds Glenbrook North High School. A small northwest corner falls in Wheeling's District 21, and a southeast sliver is in Sunset Ridge District 29.
  • Metra's Milwaukee District North Line stops at Northbrook station on Shermer Road downtown.
  • Shopping runs along Sanders Road, Skokie Boulevard and Lake Cook Road, and Northbrook Court opened in 1976.
  • Allstate is the largest employer, and Astellas and Barilla have North American headquarters in the village.
  • The Northbrook Park District runs Techny Prairie Park and Fields, a 113-acre park along the West Fork of the North Branch of the Chicago River.

Because the school district boundaries cross house by house, a listing should name the exact elementary and junior high district for the address. The village's Know Your Neighborhood tool shows zoning and school districts by property.

Northbrook Municipal Code Section 27-63 requires everyone in a property transaction to confirm with the village that a final meter reading was taken and that no unpaid water balance remains. Call the water billing office at 847-664-4171 to set that up.

Look up your parcel's township and 14-digit PIN on the Assessor's site. The township assessor for Northfield can answer questions about an appeal. For tax installment dates and the balance on a parcel, ask the Cook County Treasurer, because the sale closing statement usually prorates the bill.

For a seller, the practical point is access: Milwaukee District North Line trains, Lake Cook Road, Sanders Road and Skokie Boulevard all matter to buyers who commute, so name them in a listing or offer discussion.

Northbrook deeds are recorded through the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St., phone 312.603.5050, which also lists the state and county stamp amounts. The Clerk's list shows the seller as the party liable for the state and county tax, with a rubber stamp as proof of payment.

Because Northbrook has no municipal stamp, the closing package is lighter than in many neighboring suburbs. A seller still needs a signed deed, the PTAX-203 declaration, a clear title, and a final water read. If a trust or estate holds the title, the title company will tell you which exemption language applies.

North Chicago is a Lake County city of about 8 square miles on the Lake Michigan shore, directly south of Waukegan. The city's rules matter more than usual for a seller. A sale cannot close with a stamped deed until the city has checked for unpaid bills and, for any building, completed a sales inspection. Starting that process early keeps a closing date from slipping.

What shapes a sale in North Chicago?

The city grew around industry and the Navy. Land speculators moved in during the 1890s, a railroad depot opened in 1892, and the Washburn and Moen barbed wire plant became the first big employer. The settlement incorporated as a village in 1895 and as a city in 1909, and the Navy created its training area in 1911. A veterans hospital followed in 1926.

The population peaked in the 1970 census at 47,275 and fell to 30,759 by 2020. A few facts shape how a house here shows:

  • Two Metra stations, North Chicago and Great Lakes, serve the Union Pacific North Line, with trains south to Chicago and north to Kenosha. Pace buses link the city to Waukegan.
  • Main roads include Sheridan Road, Green Bay Road, Waukegan Road, Skokie Highway, Buckley Road and the Tri-State Tollway.
  • Foss Park Beach on the lakefront and the Greenbelt Cultural Center and Forest Preserve are the best-known green spaces.
  • Rosalind Franklin University of Medicine and Science, home of the Chicago Medical School, is among the city's larger institutions.

Most of the city drains toward the lake, while the western edge drains to the North Branch of the Chicago River. Ask the building department about any past drainage or basement water complaints on your street before you list.

  1. Call the Comptroller's Office at 847-596-8600 and the Department of Economic and Community Development at 847-596-8650 to request an outstanding payment and lien check.
  2. Pay anything the check turns up. The stamp is not issued until those payments are made.
  3. If the property has a building on it, schedule the sales inspection with Economic and Community Development.
  4. After the inspection, the buyers sign a Buyer's Acknowledgement form and give it to the Comptroller's office, which issues the stamp.
  5. The stamp goes on the deed, and the buyer or seller records the deed with the Lake County Recorder.

The department also recommends a Zoning Verification Letter before a sale. It states whether a use or structure is legal nonconforming, which can answer a buyer's questions about an old garage, an extra unit or a converted basement. The request form goes to the Economic and Community Development office at City Hall.

The building department phone is 847-596-8650, and permit questions go to permits@northchicago.org. Review times for permits are described as about 10 business days when volume is normal, so ask about timing if the inspection turns up work that needs a permit.

What do Illinois and Lake County charge on a deed?

Section 31-10 of 35 ILCS 200 sets the state tax at 50¢ for each $500 or fraction of $500. Lake County adds 25¢ per $500 on top, and its pamphlet notes that the county issues one stamp covering both. The Lake County Clerk collects the tax at recording, and the contract decides whether buyer or seller pays it.

North Chicago is one of the municipalities the county names as requiring its own stamp or exemption letter before the deed is submitted. You must get that from the city first.

  • A sale needs the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, form PTAX-203, completed through the Department of Revenue's MyDec site.
  • A deed with consideration of $100 or less carries a signed exemption statement instead of the declaration.
  • Only the stamped deed is recorded. The PTAX-203 goes to the county assessment office.
  • Recordings are filed at the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division, 18 N County St, 6th Floor, Waukegan. The office number is 847-377-2575.

The county's own pamphlet shows a $100,000 sale as an example of how the two rates combine, with a total tax of $150. Ask the Clerk's office for the figure that applies to your deed.

Do landlord and short-term rental rules affect a sale here?

Yes, if the house has ever been rented. Any dwelling not occupied by its owner falls under the landlord license rules in City Code Title 5, Chapter 14, whether or not rent is charged. The license runs January 1 to December 31, and inspections must be passed every two years for the certificate of compliance.

Other city rules that show up at closing time:

  • Short-term rentals need an endorsement on top of the landlord license, and only 25 endorsements are available per year, first come, first served.
  • Short-term rentals also owe the city's 9.5% hotel and motel tax, remitted monthly.
  • Rental properties with four or more units must have a Knox Box key box for Fire Department access under City Code Title 3, Chapter 2, Section 14.
  • Vacant and foreclosed properties must be registered through the HERA Property Registry, with a fee.
  • The city adopted the 2021 International Building, Residential, Mechanical, Fuel Gas, Fire, Property Maintenance and Existing Building codes on October 1, 2024, along with the 2020 National Electric Code.

An inherited house with a former tenant, or a house the owner has left empty, is the most common place these rules trip up a sale. Find out from the building department whether the address is registered, ideally before an offer arrives.

How are Lake County property taxes handled at closing?

Lake County sends one bill with two installment coupons. For the 2025 tax year, bills were mailed May 1, 2026, the first installment was due June 4 and the second September 4, with penalty interest added the day after each date. The county publishes a new calendar each year, and the Treasurer's office can tell you which installments are paid on your parcel.

At closing, the title company usually splits the year's tax between buyer and seller. Bring the latest bill to the closing table and phone the Lake County Treasurer if any installment shows as open. An unpaid installment stays attached to the parcel and becomes the next owner's problem unless it is settled in the closing statement.

Which way of selling suits a North Chicago house?

The choice depends on condition, timing and what the sales inspection might find. A public listing reaches the most buyers but adds showings, repair requests and a longer timeline. A direct cash sale moves faster and accepts the house with its flaws, and it still goes through the same stamp, inspection and recording steps.

  • Hire an agent and list publicly if the house shows well and you can wait for a financed buyer.
  • Sell as-is when repairs, a code violation, a former tenant or probate paperwork makes a normal listing hard.
  • Get the lien check and sales inspection started first in either case, because both can reveal debts or defects that change the price.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a city transfer stamp to sell in North Chicago?

Yes. The city requires a transfer stamp on any sale inside its limits, and it will not issue one until outstanding payments and liens are cleared and, for a building, the sales inspection is done. The stamp is attached to the deed before it is recorded.

Which office handles the sales inspection?

Call the Department of Economic and Community Development at 847-596-8650 or write to permits@northchicago.org. The Comptroller's Office at 847-596-8600 handles the lien and payment check and issues the stamp after the buyers sign the Buyer's Acknowledgement.

What is the Illinois and Lake County transfer tax rate?

Illinois takes 50¢ per $500 and Lake County takes 25¢ per $500, both collected by the Lake County Clerk when the deed is filed. The city stamp is separate, so confirm its amount with the Comptroller's Office.

Can I sell a North Chicago rental house with tenants in it?

Yes, but the unit must be covered by a landlord license, since any dwelling not occupied by its owner falls under City Code 5-14. Ask the building department for the certificate of compliance status, because a buyer or lender may want to see it.

Where does the deed get filed after closing?

Filing happens at the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division, 18 N County St, 6th Floor, Waukegan, phone 847-377-2575. The stamped deed is the document filed, while the PTAX-203 declaration is forwarded to the assessment office.

What is it like to sell a house in Woodridge, Illinois?

Woodridge is a DuPage County village southwest of Chicago, just north of where I-55 meets Illinois Route 53, with small pieces of the village reaching into Will and Cook counties. A seller here is usually dealing with a post-war suburban house, townhome or condo in a place that grew in a single burst. The village was incorporated on August 24, 1959 with fewer than 500 residents, and its name comes from a wooded rise locally called "The Ridge" above the East Branch of the DuPage River.

Growth after incorporation was fast. The 1960 census counted 542 people, the 1970 census 11,028, and the 2020 census 34,158. A developer founded the village, and most of its homes, businesses and churches went up after the 1950s, so many houses are now old enough to need a new roof, windows, furnace or a rebuilt basement. That is the main reason owners here look at selling as-is.

Whatever route you choose, the same local paperwork applies. The sections below cover the Woodridge-specific steps, starting with who your neighbors are and which schools serve your address.

What do the numbers say about Woodridge homeowners?

About 13,300 households live in Woodridge, and roughly two homes in three have an owner in residence. Here are the housing and income figures buyers and appraisers check first.

Woodridge village, Census Bureau QuickFacts (2020-2024 estimates unless noted)

Source: Census QuickFacts, Woodridge village. Few residents move in a given year: 89.8% were living at the same address a year earlier.

Which school district serves a Woodridge address?

It depends on the street. Woodridge has no high school of its own, and the village is split among several districts, so the district for your house can change the buyer pool. The village lists six districts on its school page: Center Cass 66, Community High School District 99, Lemont-Bromberek 113A, Lemont Township High School District 210, Naperville 203 and Woodridge School District 68.

  • Woodridge School District 68 runs six elementary schools (Edgewood, Willow Creek, Sipley, William F. Murphy, Meadowview and Goodrich) for grades K-6, plus Jefferson Junior High for grades 7 and 8.
  • Most high school students go to Downers Grove North or South in District 99.
  • Some southern Woodridge students are served by Lemont District 210 and attend Lemont High School.
  • Homes west of the DuPage River, in the Seven Bridges single-family area, attend Naperville District 203 schools.

Say the district name in your listing or when you talk to a cash buyer. It shapes price expectations more than a dated kitchen does.

What does a seller have to do at Woodridge Village Hall?

Anyone selling property in Woodridge has to buy a Real Estate Transfer Stamp from the village before the deed is recorded. The Finance Department page says stamps can take 60 minutes or longer to process and sometimes 24 hours or more, so allow time, or drop the paperwork off with a phone number and wait for a call.

Village Hall is at 5 Plaza Drive. The village does not accept stamp paperwork by email or fax, and original documents must be brought in or mailed with a self-addressed, postage-paid envelope. Questions go to 630-719-4909 or epay@woodridgeil.gov. Ask Village Hall for the current stamp amount before closing day, because it is a village charge and the closing agent will need the figure.

  • An exempt stamp is available when the transfer qualifies for an exemption under the state Transfer Tax Law.
  • A refund of the village transfer tax is available to someone who sold a primary residence in Woodridge and bought another residence in Woodridge.
  • Payment by check is converted to an electronic transfer, so the bank account can be debited the same day.
  • Mortgage lenders starting a foreclosure on a Woodridge home send a copy of the foreclosure notice to the Village Clerk at Village Hall.

Recording happens at the county, and a signed transfer declaration goes in with the deed or within three business days of the transfer, whichever is sooner (35 ILCS 200/31-25). Woodridge parcels can lie in DuPage, Will or Cook County, so confirm which recorder handles yours.

Do Woodridge permit and rental rules affect a sale?

Yes, in two ways: open work on the house and any rental use. Building permits are required for construction, alteration, repair, demolition or moving of any building in the village. The Community Development Department says it can issue some permits the same day, such as roofs, sewer repairs and water heaters. Other residential permits can take up to two weeks. Work must begin within three months and finish within one year of the permit.

If a house has an unfinished basement or addition, call Building Permits and Inspections at 630-719-4750 before you list, so a buyer does not inherit an open permit. Construction hours are limited: between September 1 and May 31 the village bars work after 7:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday, and on Sundays allows it only from 10:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. Summer evenings run later, to 9:00 p.m.

The village also runs a Residential Rental Program. Owners of three or more multi-family units need an annual license by January 1 and take part in a yearly inspection. Owners of single-family rentals, or two or fewer multi-family units, register at no fee. Both groups complete a four-hour crime free housing seminar once, and the certificate goes with the registration. An investor who buys your house to rent it will need to complete the same steps.

How do storms and flooding shape Woodridge houses?

Winters are cold and summers hot, with a 105-degree reading in July 2005 and minus 26 in January 1985 on the books. Inspectors and buyers look closely at roofs, basements and drainage. On June 20, 2021, an EF-3 tornado struck just after 11 p.m., damaged 225 homes in Woodridge and neighboring suburbs and injured eight people who were taken to hospitals.

Storm repairs are one reason a roof or siding permit shows up in a house history. Another is stormwater: the village enforces the 2019 DuPage County Countywide Stormwater and Floodplain Ordinance as part of its building codes. If a basement has had water, say so on the disclosure form and keep the repair records.

The village has been named a Tree City by the Arbor Day Foundation, and more than 8,000 trees were counted on public property in a 1996 study. Mature street trees are part of the curb appeal, though a large limb over the roof is a fair item for a buyer to raise.

How can a Woodridge owner sell without repairs?

Three routes exist: an agent listing, a sale by the owner, and a purchase by someone paying cash who takes the house as it sits. Each of the three ends with a village stamp, a recorded deed and a closing statement, so what changes is the timeline and who pays for repairs.

  • Agent listing: works when the house shows well and you can sit through showings, inspection demands and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Owner sale: avoids a commission, but disclosure forms, the contract and the village stamp become your job.
  • Cash purchase: no loan underwriting and no repair haggling, which helps with inherited houses, open permits, tenant trouble or a firm move date.

Compare what each route leaves in your pocket after repairs, carrying costs, the stamp and the months of waiting.

Who collects property tax on a Woodridge house?

The tax bill comes from the county where the parcel sits, so a Woodridge owner may deal with DuPage, Will or Cook County. Your bill lists the taxing districts, including the school district, park district and the fire protection district. Woodridge has no fire department of its own and is covered by the Lisle-Woodridge, Darien-Woodridge and Lemont fire districts, which each levy their own tax.

Before you sign a contract, ask the county treasurer where every installment on your parcel stands, and ask who is handling the proration at the table. The village website has a Property and Tax Information section with pages on buying or selling a home and on municipal taxes.

Frequently asked questions

Does the seller or the buyer deal with the Woodridge transfer stamp?

The seller needs to buy it, since the village states that anyone selling property in Woodridge must purchase a Real Estate Transfer Stamp. Your closing agent or attorney usually brings the paperwork to Village Hall at 5 Plaza Drive, because the village does not take stamp paperwork by email or fax.

Can I get my village transfer tax back if I stay in Woodridge?

Yes, in one situation. The village offers a refund when you sold your primary residence in Woodridge and then purchased another residence in Woodridge. Contact the Finance Department at 630-719-4909 to learn what documents it wants.

Which county records the deed for a Woodridge house?

Most of the village is in DuPage County, but small portions lie in Will and Cook counties. The county of your parcel decides which recorder takes the deed and which treasurer sends the tax bill, so check your parcel number with the closing agent.

Does a recent roof or water heater replacement need village paperwork?

Yes, both jobs need a village permit, and Community Development can issue permits for roofs and water heaters the same day. If the work is already done without one, call 630-719-4750 and ask how to close it out before the buyer's inspection.

Does Woodridge regulate rental houses that I might sell to an investor?

Yes. Single-family rental owners register at no fee, and owners of three or more multi-family units hold an annual license with village inspections. Every owner or manager attends a crime free housing seminar once, so an investor buyer should plan for that step.

How do homeowners in St. Charles usually sell?

Most use one of three paths: a listing through a broker, a sale they run themselves, or a purchase for cash with no repairs requested. The winner is set by repair needs and by how rigid your timeline is.

  • Broker listing: suits an updated house and an owner who can host showings for several weeks.
  • Owner-run sale: saves the agent's commission but puts pricing, marketing and negotiation on you.
  • Cash buyer: closes without loan approval, which helps with inherited houses, tenants in place or a pending relocation.

St. Charles homes tend to sell on location and condition. If yours has an open permit, an unfinished project or deferred maintenance, sort that out first, because the city's own permit page says open permits can hold up a sale.

Where is St. Charles and what shaped it?

St. Charles sits on the Fox River about 35 miles west of Chicago along Illinois Route 64. It lies in Kane and DuPage counties and forms a tri-city group with Geneva and Batavia. The river runs through downtown, and Pottawatomie Park along its bank is the city's largest park. The Census Bureau lists 14.40 square miles of land.

The first settlers staked claims in 1833 and the town was first called Charleston. The name St. Charles came in 1839 because another Illinois city already used the first one. Isolation held growth back for decades. The town had no railroad until a branch line from Geneva opened in 1871, and a direct Chicago connection arrived in the 1880s with the Chicago Great Western. A direct automobile route, later Route 64, was built in 1920.

Census counts trace the pattern: 4,046 residents in 1910, 9,269 in 1960, 22,501 in 1990 and 33,081 in 2020. A buyer touring a house near the river or the downtown grid is often comparing it with nearby Geneva and Batavia, so be ready to explain what sets your block apart.

Four state routes cross the city: 64, 38, 25 and 31. Randall Road on the west side and Kirk Road on the east side are the main county roads, and Pace buses on Routes 801 and 802 link the city with Elgin and Aurora.

What do Census numbers say about St. Charles homes?

Seven in ten homes are lived in by their owners, and the median home value is $377,400. The Census Bureau data for 2020 to 2024 is below.

Which schools and transit options serve St. Charles buyers?

St. Charles Community Unit School District 303 runs the public schools. It includes elementary schools such as Davis Primary and Richmond Intermediate, Thompson and Wredling middle schools, and two high schools, St. Charles East and St. Charles North. The city is part of Elgin Community College District 509.

  • Look up your attendance zone before you write a listing, since families ask about it early.
  • Pace Routes 801 and 802 cover the local bus connections.

Get the assignment for your exact address from the district, not from a neighbor.

What permits and rules matter before selling in St. Charles?

Take permit questions to the Building Division on the ground floor of City Hall, 2 E. Main Street, or call (630) 377-4406. The city says open permits can hold up the sale of a home, and that a disapproved final inspection means the work must be corrected before the sale.

  • A permit is required for a new fence or a replacement fence, and the plat of survey must show where it sits.
  • Patios, decks, pools, flatwork, air conditioners and water heaters each need a permit and inspection.
  • Electric service and panel work needs a permit plus an electric service application, because the city runs its own electric utility.
  • Painting, wallpaper, flooring, cabinets, countertops and appliance swaps with no electrical or plumbing change do not need one.

Work done without a permit can be charged double fees once you apply, and a citation with an adjudication hearing is possible if you wait too long. A plat of survey submitted with a permit application must be 11 by 17 inches. If you lost yours, the division can check its files.

One more check: many homes carry a St. Charles mailing address but sit outside city limits. The city says a letter in the numeric address, such as 12N123, signals unincorporated Kane County, where permits come from the county.

How are St. Charles property taxes assessed?

For a Kane County parcel, a township assessor sets the first value and the Supervisor of Assessments equalizes it. A DuPage County parcel in the city goes through DuPage offices instead, so confirm which county holds your parcel number.

Kane's assessment office explains why a bill can rise even when a value does not: your exemptions may be incomplete, neighbors may qualify for exemptions you lack, taxing bodies may have raised levies, or your value may have moved faster than the neighborhood average. The county also says the largest share of a bill goes to schools, and that it cannot set another government's levy.

  • Residential property supplies 75.7 percent of the county's tax base, ahead of commercial at 12.8 percent and industrial at 9.6 percent.
  • The Property Tax Extension Limitation Law applies in Kane, generally capping levy increases at 5 percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is lower.
  • New construction, bonded debt and voter-approved increases fall outside that cap.

Payment season for 2025 taxes closed on October 23, 2026, according to the treasurer's site. A parcel whose taxes were sold is redeemed at the County Clerk's tax extension office, 630-232-5964.

You may look at the township assessor's records for any parcel, including your own, to see how neighbors are valued. Your parcel number appears on your tax bill and your assessment notice, and the county also lists it through its online property search.

What is filed and taxed when a St. Charles sale closes?

Your deed is filed in whichever county contains the parcel, and the title company usually handles the filing. State law prices the transfer tax at 50 cents per $500 of value, paid for with revenue stamps from the recorder, with a MyDec report going to the Department of Revenue.

The county's own share, the recording fee and any city requirement are separate questions. Ask the Kane County Recorder, or the DuPage County Recorder for a DuPage parcel, and ask City Hall whether a water or utility final read is needed. The settlement statement will show every charge.

Frequently asked questions

Will an open permit delay my St. Charles closing?

It can. The city states that open permits can hold up the sale of a home, and unfinished or failed work must be corrected before the transfer.

Is my St. Charles address inside city limits?

Not always. If the numeric address contains a letter, such as 12N123, the city says the property is in unincorporated Kane County and permits come from the county.

Can I protest my St. Charles assessment after the tax bill arrives?

Generally no. Kane County says complaints for a given year must go to the Board of Review within 30 days of the township roll being published, and a bill that has already arrived is too late unless a complaint was filed.

Who handles electric service when a St. Charles house changes hands?

The city operates its own electric utility, which is why electrical permits include an electric service application. Ask the city about the account transfer for your address.

How many residents does St. Charles have?

The Census Bureau estimated 33,594 residents on July 1, 2025, compared with 33,081 counted in the April 2020 census.

What should a Mundelein owner know about selling?

Lake County is home to Mundelein, a village 33 miles from the Loop, and the recording for any sale goes through the county clerk's office in Waukegan. Owners generally compare an agent listing, a self-managed sale and a cash purchase of the house in its present state.

The village straddles Libertyville and Fremont townships and borders Grayslake, Ivanhoe, Diamond Lake, Libertyville, Hawthorn Woods and Vernon Hills. That mix matters for pricing. A tri-level near the old center and a newer two-story near the village edge attract different buyers, and the repair needs are different too.

What do the Census numbers say about Mundelein?

Mundelein held 31,560 people in 2020, and the mid-2025 Census estimate of 32,680 is 3.5 percent above its base. Land area is 9.59 square miles, which works out to about 3,293 people per square mile.

Figures for 2020 to 2024 show a midpoint home value of $309,700, midpoint rent of $1,566 and midpoint household income of $108,340. Owners live in 71.2 percent of homes, spread over 11,632 households of 2.72 people, and a typical commute lasts 27.9 minutes.

  • Growth is steady, with the Census estimate above the 2020 count.

How did Mundelein grow, and why does it matter to a seller?

The area was first settled by Europeans in 1835. The village went through several names: Mechanics Grove, Holcomb, Rockefeller and Area, before it adopted Mundelein in 1925 in honor of the Chicago cardinal. It was incorporated in 1909, after a spur line of the Chicago North Shore and Milwaukee Railroad reached the village.

The University of Saint Mary of the Lake opened in 1921 on the former Sheldon School estate, and in June 1926 the village hosted the closing events of the 28th International Eucharistic Congress. Ball Glass, a major employer, closed in the early 1980s, and the village added more than 10,000 residents between the 1980 and 1990 censuses.

A recent expansion is the 2022 annexation of more than 700 acres of land owned by the Wirtz family, where the plan was to build 1,200 houses and 600 townhomes. New construction near your house is competition to watch, so price against what buyers can find new as well as resale houses.

Which schools, roads and trains serve Mundelein?

Five elementary districts divide the village, so the one for your street varies. They are Diamond Lake School District 76, Fremont School District 79, Hawthorn Community Consolidated School District 73, Libertyville School District 70 and Mundelein Elementary School District 75. Mundelein High School serves the village, and Carmel High School and the University of Saint Mary of the Lake are private institutions in town.

  • Rail: Metra's North Central Service stops in Mundelein with weekday service between Antioch and Chicago Union Station. The station opened in 1996.
  • Bus: Pace Route 574 links Mundelein with Grayslake, Vernon Hills and other stops.
  • Streets: Lake Street, Illinois Route 60, Illinois Route 83, Maple Avenue, Midlothian Road and Hawley Street carry most traffic.
  • Interstate: Interstate 94 is five miles east.

The village hall opened in 2014 on a 10-acre site next to the Metra station, which puts the civic center and the train in the same place. Homes within walking distance of that area are easy to market on convenience.

Does Diamond Lake or the weather change how a Mundelein house sells?

Diamond Lake is a 153-acre glacial lake in south Mundelein, used for fishing, swimming and boating, and it drains to the Des Plaines River. Homes near it may appeal to buyers who want water access, and a lakefront or creekside lot should prompt you to confirm flood zone status before you list.

The village has a flood history. Floods in September 1936 and June 1937 damaged the main road and nearby businesses and neighborhoods. Disclose any water events at your own address on the seller report.

The Köppen label for Mundelein is humid continental, meaning warm to hot summers and cold winters. Since 1999 the extremes were 103 degrees in July 2012 and 26 below in January 2019. Swings that wide are why inspectors test the roof, furnace and sump pump.

What do Mundelein's building and permit offices require?

The Village of Mundelein posts a Permit Application for building and property work or new construction, plus a Homeowner Project Guide, and online fee payments. Contact customer service at 847-949-3283 or building@mundelein.org about a specific project. The main village line is 847-949-3200.

Gather permit records for any addition, deck, roof, furnace or finished basement before you list. An inspector will compare the house with that history, and a missing permit is simpler to fix before an offer than after one.

The village also provides water delivery and wastewater treatment, from a Lake Michigan supply. Ask the village about final water billing so the account closes at your sale date.

How is a deed recorded in Lake County, and are there extra transfer taxes?

Deeds are filed with the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk, on the sixth floor at 18 N County Street in Waukegan (847-377-2575). Its published fees are $70 for a standard document and $82 for a non-standard one, and the only extra charges at recording are the state and county transfer taxes.

State tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-15 is fifty cents for every $500 of value. On the eRecording page the clerk names six municipalities whose deeds need local stamps or a signed exemption certificate: Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. Mundelein does not appear. Most deeds qualify for eRecording, but a deed with a paper PTAX-203 cannot be submitted that way.

What should you prepare before accepting an offer in Mundelein?

The statutory disclosure report comes first: 765 ILCS 77/20 has the seller answer every item and deliver the report before a contract is signed.

After that, build the closing file with the parcel number, the latest tax bill, a loan payoff statement if applicable, permit records and the village water account details. Judge offers by the net amount and the number of contingencies, since a contingent deal can unravel late.

A cash purchaser may close within a short window and buy without repairs. A listing may bring more money but takes more time. Let your deadline choose.

Is there a Mundelein village transfer stamp?

The Lake County Clerk's list of six municipalities needing local stamps or an exemption certificate is Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago, and Mundelein is absent. The state tax of fifty cents per $500 still applies.

Which office takes a Mundelein deed for recording?

The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division, 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, Waukegan, in person or by eRecording through an approved vendor. Call 847-377-2575.

How much does Lake County charge to file a deed?

Its fee page gives $70 for a standard document and $82 for a non-standard one, with state and county transfer taxes as the only additions at recording.

Which elementary district covers my Mundelein street?

One of five: Diamond Lake 76, Fremont 79, Hawthorn CCSD 73, Libertyville 70 or Mundelein Elementary 75. Confirm by address, since Mundelein High School handles the older grades.

How do I start a building permit in Mundelein?

Use the Permit Application and Homeowner Project Guide posted by the Village, and call customer service at 847-949-3283 or email building@mundelein.org with questions.

Which selling routes are open to an O'Fallon, Illinois homeowner?

O'Fallon owners can go with an agent, run the sale themselves, or accept an offer from a company that buys for cash. The right pick turns on the house's condition, the lender's timeline and how much repair work the owner is willing to manage.

This O'Fallon sits in St. Clair County, east of St. Louis, and should not be mixed up with the O'Fallon in St. Charles County, Missouri. Both belong to the St. Louis metro area, which makes the pair unusual. The count in 2020 was 32,289 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 32,656.

  • An agent listing makes sense when the house is ready to occupy and similar sales nearby are easy to find.

How old are O'Fallon's houses, and where did the growth come from?

O'Fallon began as a railroad town in 1854, and suburban growth picked up in the 1980s and again after Interstate 64 was widened in the 1990s, so much of the housing stands in subdivisions from those decades. Lots were platted around a Baltimore and Ohio depot and sold at public auction on May 18, 1854, and German settlers came for the farmland.

It was incorporated as a village on January 27, 1874, and voters changed to a city form of government on March 14, 1905. Population rose from 7,268 in 1970 to 12,173 in 1980, 21,910 in 2000 and 32,289 in 2020. Subdivision names that come up in listings include Thornbury Hill, Nolin Creek Estates, Fairwood Hills, Deer Creek, Forest Hills and Fairwood East.

The city seal carries a pick and shovel for the coal mines that mattered to the local economy for more than a century, a locomotive for the railroad, and planes for Scott Air Force Base.

Where is O'Fallon, and why does Scott Air Force Base matter to sellers?

O'Fallon is about 5 miles from Scott Air Force Base and roughly 17 miles from downtown St. Louis, which puts a major employer within a short drive. The city center is around two miles east of where Interstate 64 meets U.S. Route 50.

The city flag credits the base as a workplace for many residents, both military and civil service. Sellers who deal with a buyer moving on orders should keep repair receipts, appliance manuals and a recent utility history ready. The Census Bureau lists 4,679 veterans in O'Fallon for 2020-2024.

McKendree University is about 10 miles away. The city covers 15.56 square miles of land (2020), with a density near 2,075 people per square mile.

Which school districts cover O'Fallon homes?

District 90 runs five elementary schools named Delores Moye, Estelle Kampmeyer, J. E. Hinchcliffe Sr., Laverna Evans and Marie Schaefer, and two junior highs, Amelia V. Carriel and Edward A. Fulton. The high school is O'Fallon Township High School, whose main campus is on South Smiley Street and which has a separate freshman campus called Milburn. Private options include Discovery School, St. Clare Catholic School and First Baptist Academy.

Is an occupancy permit needed in O'Fallon when ownership changes?

Yes. The city requires an occupancy permit when the ownership or occupancy of a home changes and no current permit is on file, and a residential permit costs $75 as of May 1, 2025 and stays valid for two years.

The city treats the permit as a property maintenance inspection. After you apply, the schedule runs like this:

  • Call to book the inspection appointment within 7 days of applying.
  • Plan on the inspection taking place inside a month of the application.
  • Any violations must be fixed, and the permit follows within a second 30-day window after that first inspection.
  • Water and electricity must be on during the inspection.

The house may be occupied before the inspection as long as no life safety problems exist. Ameren Illinois and the city's utility billing office ask for the occupancy permit number before they open service. The city offers a seller's and a buyer's "as is" letter, and you should ask your lender whether the permit is a condition of closing. You can apply online, by mail, through the white drop box in the parking lot, or at Community Development inside City Hall. Paying by card adds a 2.35% convenience fee. Landlords are also pointed to the city's Crime-Free Rental Housing Program.

How do I stop or transfer water service in O'Fallon?

Fill out the city's start or stop service request form, and call Utility Billing at 618-624-4500 extension 1 if you need help. The office is at 255 S Lincoln Avenue and keeps weekday hours, 7 a.m. to 5:15 p.m.

The city bills water and sewer for most O'Fallon addresses and for most of Fairview Heights. A new account is charged a $50 non-refundable new service fee on its first bill. Sewer charges follow an averaging rule: June, July and August sewer use is billed from the average of the October through April water consumption, with 10,000 gallons assumed for a new residence that has no history. A bill that looks too high can mean a leak, and the city will re-read a meter and run a leak check on request.

When are St. Clair County property taxes due?

Property tax in St. Clair County comes due twice a year, and the bills payable in 2026 had due dates of July 1 and September 1. That year's calendar also listed bill mailing on May 26, September 18 to stay out of newspaper publication, October 30 as the final payment day, and a tax sale on November 2, 2026. All of those dates are behind us.

The Treasurer's office opens at half past eight and closes at half past four, and the posted dates carry a tentative label. Contact the Treasurer about the next bill's schedule, and have your closing agent explain how the seller's portion of this year's tax is credited at closing.

Usually yes, because the city requires one when ownership changes and no current permit is on file. A residential permit costs $75 and lasts two years, and your lender can tell you if closing depends on it.

How long does the O'Fallon occupancy inspection take to schedule?

Contact the city within 7 days of applying, and the inspection must occur within 30 days of the application. The permit itself follows within another 30 days after the first inspection.

Can a buyer move in before the occupancy inspection is done?

Yes, provided there are no life safety issues. The city allows occupancy ahead of the inspection, but the inspection still has to happen and any violations still have to be corrected.

Which county collects property tax on an O'Fallon house?

St. Clair County. The Treasurer bills in two installments, and the bills payable in 2026 were due July 1 and September 1. Contact the Treasurer about the next bill.

No. They are separate cities in the same metro area. Illinois's O'Fallon is in St. Clair County, with 32,289 residents in the 2020 census, so make sure any records or tax searches use the Illinois city.

How do you sell a house fast in Glendale Heights, Illinois?

The first move for a fast Glendale Heights sale is the village's transfer inspection application, filed at least 21 days before closing, since that step sets the earliest realistic closing date for any buyer. After that, the choice is between listing, selling privately, or accepting an as-is cash purchase.

  • A private sale saves the commission and leaves the contract, disclosures and scheduling to you.
  • An as-is cash sale is common for houses with code problems, tenants or an estate, and the buyer can sign the village's guarantee of compliance for many checklist items.

Glendale Heights is a village in DuPage County and a far west suburb of Chicago. It is almost entirely residential, so most sales here are of single-family houses, townhouses, duplexes and condominiums, and the village's rules are written around those property types.

What is Glendale Heights like for home sellers?

Glendale Heights is a compact, diverse suburb. 32,655 residents in mid-2025, below the 33,176 counted in 2020, on roughly 5.4 square miles of land.

Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $261,700 in the 2020 to 2024 data, owners hold 64.4 percent of the housing, and the village has 11,196 households averaging 2.93 people. Median gross rent was $1,590, median household income was $86,545, and workers averaged 26.7 minutes to get to work. At home, 58.1 percent of residents age 5 and older speak a language other than English, and 37.9 percent were born outside the country.

The village grew out of farmland. Builders began putting up houses in 1958 on farms along Glen Ellyn Road north of North Avenue, and the village incorporated in 1959. It was first named Glendale because it sits between Glen Ellyn and Bloomingdale, and the word Heights was added in March 1960 for the roughly 100 foot rise created by the Valparaiso Moraine. Houses from the first building decades are now well past 50 years old, so roofs, furnaces and electrical panels deserve a look before you list.

Which employers and schools shape the Glendale Heights market?

Manufacturing and food production give the village a working base. The village's 2022 financial report listed Spraying Systems Co. as the largest employer at about 1,000 employees, followed by Cornelius at about 500 and Kronos Foods at about 400, with Super Target and Jewel-Osco among the retail employers.

Three K to 8 districts serve the village, and all feed into Glenbard Township High School District 87. Marquardt School District 15 covers the eastern part and feeds mainly into Glenbard East. Queen Bee District 16 sends students to Glenbard North and Glenbard West. Glen Ellyn School District 41 covers a portion of the village, and its students attend Abraham Lincoln School, then Hadley Junior High, and later Glenbard West.

The Glenside Public Library District serves the village, and Pace routes 711 and 715 connect it to Wheaton and other destinations. Because the district lines cut across the village, check the district for your street before you describe a school in a listing or offer letter.

What does Glendale Heights require before a house can transfer?

Glendale Heights requires a real estate transfer inspection for most sales, and the owner must file for a certificate of compliance at least 21 days before the proposed transfer, along with a plat of survey dated within one year. The inspection is visual only and does not replace a private home inspection.

Here is the sequence the village lays out for sellers:

  • Community Development inspects the property and gives you a report of items to correct. You can fix them and request a re-inspection, or the purchaser can sign a Guarantee of Compliance for items authorized on the checklist.
  • Pay any money you owe the village, such as unpaid building or code invoices, lien filing fees, parking tickets and rental fees.
  • Then go to Finance. There you pay the final water bill, hand in the stamp form with the deed copy and the state's PTAX-203 declaration, and pay the village's transfer tax of $3 on each $1,000 of value, rounding up any fraction.

The sample checklist gives a sense of the inspector's eye: ground-fault outlets near water, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, doors and windows that lock, a covered electrical panel, flues in good order, a sump pump that empties into the yard, and a self-closing fire-rated door from the garage into the house. A re-inspection can turn up items missed the first time, and the village may require an escrow to secure corrections. Call Community Development at 630-260-6030 and Finance at 630-260-6000 with questions.

Do Glendale Heights rental licensing rules affect a sale?

Yes. All residential rentals in the village must hold an annual license and be inspected each year, so a rental house or condo has an extra layer of paperwork at sale time. The transfer form asks whether the property was or will be used as a rental, and the checklist warns that a rental inspection is more stringent than the transfer inspection.

The village sets the license fee by property type: $200 for a single-family condominium, $300 for a single-family rental house, townhouse or duplex, and for apartment complexes $100 per building plus $50 per unit. Applications and fees are due by February 1 each year, and licenses expire January 31. A late renewal adds $25 per month, and a re-inspection fee of $75 can apply when an inspection is missed or cancelled late. Owners schedule inspections with their tenants by calling 630-260-6030.

If you own a rental here, clear any unpaid license or inspection fees before you apply for the transfer stamp, because the village will not issue it while rental fees remain owed.

How are DuPage County property taxes handled for Glendale Heights sellers?

DuPage County mailed the 2025 bills on April 29, 2026, with installments due June 1 and September 1, 2026. After a due date the county adds 1.5 percent a month, and it mailed delinquent notices on October 21, 2026 after a pre-delinquent bill on September 28.

The exemptions on the county's list include a homestead improvement exemption that shelters up to $25,000 of added assessment for four years, plus senior, disability and veterans programs. The assessor for your township, named on the tax bill, handles valuation questions and the residential exemption, and appeals go to the county Board of Review within 30 days after the township roll is published, supported by three or more comparable properties.

Selling or refinancing sometimes leads to a double payment, because a title company or lender and the owner each pay the same bill. The county refunds a duplicate payment only to the person who made it, using a notarized affidavit and proof of payment, so tell your lender and title company which of you is paying. For bills, call the Treasurer at 630-407-5900. For exemptions, call the Supervisor of Assessments at 630-407-5858.

At least 21 days before the proposed closing. The village requires the application and a plat of survey dated within one year, and the application fee for a single-family home is $100.

Who pays the Glendale Heights transfer stamp?

The village's instructions are addressed to the seller, who completes the stamp steps at the Finance Department. The tax is $3 for every $1,000 of value or fraction thereof, and the deed, PTAX-203 and final water bill are part of the packet.

What happens if the inspection finds problems?

You receive a report of items to correct, and you may fix them and ask for a re-inspection. A purchaser may instead sign a Guarantee of Compliance for authorized checklist items, and the village may require an escrow.

Does a rented Glendale Heights house need its license before I sell?

A rental house needs its annual license while it is rented, with renewals due February 1. Resolve unpaid rental fees first, since outstanding amounts owed to the village must be paid before the stamp.

What must be ready before a fast Elk Grove Village closing?

The village requires a transfer stamp, a settled water account and a few forms before a sale can close, so a fast sale in Elk Grove Village depends on lining up those items early. The Census Bureau estimates 31,885 residents for July 1, 2025, living in a village that sits next to O'Hare International Airport and handles its own transfer tax.

Elk Grove Village lies in both Cook and DuPage counties, and the county of your parcel decides where the deed is recorded. A title company or attorney usually files the paperwork, yet you should know what they will ask you for.

  • Your parcel number and the county on your tax bill.
  • The names on the deed, spelled exactly as recorded, including middle initials and trust numbers.
  • A final water meter reading booked ahead of closing.
  • A mortgage payoff statement and a list of any liens.

How does the Elk Grove Village transfer stamp work?

Elk Grove Village levies its own tax when title to local real estate changes hands: $3 for every $1,000 of value, counting any fraction, with the seller carrying primary liability. To buy the stamp you submit a village Real Estate Tax Declaration Form with two signatures, a copy of the new deed, a water and sewer affidavit, and either the state PTAX-203 or an EZ Dec form. An unsigned copy of the deed is accepted for purchase, but a copy of the signed deed must reach the Finance Department within 10 days after closing.

Acceptable payment is cash, a cashier's check, a money order, or an attorney's or title company's check made out to Elk Grove Village. It does not accept credit cards or personal and company checks. The finance counter in the Municipal Building, 901 Wellington Avenue, sells stamps on weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30, and finished forms can be emailed to fc@elkgrove.org. Mailed requests take about one week, so leave extra time if your closing is close.

The Finance Department's number is (847) 439-3900.

What water bill steps come before closing in Elk Grove Village?

The village requires the final water bill to be paid when you buy the transfer stamp, and it asks that a final meter reading be scheduled at least two days before the closing date. All other utility bills and debts owed to the village must also be settled before the stamp is issued. The water and sewer affidavit asks for the top three lines, the seller's forwarding address and the buyer's name.

Because the stamp, the final reading and the payoff all need to land near the closing date, put the reading on the calendar as soon as the closing is set. A seller who forgets the reading can delay the stamp, and a delayed stamp can delay the closing. Ask your title company to confirm that the village has the reading scheduled.

What fuel tank disclosure applies in Elk Grove Village?

The village requires a Real Estate Disclosure Form for underground fuel heating storage tanks on all properties located north of Elk Grove Boulevard. Sellers must give it to the buyers, and it covers the possible presence of those tanks. The village directs questions about underground heating fuel tanks to the Fire Department at (847) 734-8020.

This requirement is easy to overlook because it applies by location inside the village. Check where your street sits relative to Elk Grove Boulevard, and fill the form out before the contract date rather than at the closing table. A house with a known tank history can still sell, but the buyer should receive the information up front.

Are there exemptions or refunds on the Elk Grove Village transfer tax?

Certain transfers are exempt. The village points sellers to Village Code 3-2-5-F and the back of the declaration form for the complete list, and anyone claiming an exemption must supply proof of every fact needed to establish it. The exempt stamp carries a $10 handling fee, and all utility bills and village debts must be paid before it is issued.

Some taxpayers can claim a refund on a portion of the tax. Applications for re-investment or senior refunds must reach the village within one year of payment, so keep your receipt and closing documents. The village's Real Estate Transfer Stamp Refund and Exemption pages describe who qualifies. If you are transferring a house into a trust or between family members, ask the Finance Department whether the exempt route fits before you purchase a regular stamp.

  • Exemption claims need proof of each fact behind the exemption.
  • The exempt stamp carries a $10 handling fee.
  • Re-investment and senior refund requests must arrive within one year of payment.

What is it like to sell in Elk Grove Village, and what do the Census numbers say?

Elk Grove Village was incorporated on July 17, 1956 as a planned suburb about 22 miles northwest of Chicago. Centex built most of the early houses, and the village kept residential areas separate from a large industrial park on its eastern edge. That park covers 5.9 square miles, holds nearly 3,600 businesses and employs nearly 100,000 people, which makes it the largest consolidated business park in North America. Alexian Brothers Medical Center is the largest single employer, with more than 2,200 workers.
