How do storms and temperature swings affect an Edwardsville house?

Madison County has real storm exposure. The tornado outbreak of December 10 and 11, 2021 struck Edwardsville, where an EF3 tornado collapsed an Amazon warehouse. Lenders and insurers often ask about roof age, window condition and earlier storm repairs, so save receipts and permit records.

Temperature ranges are wide. Typical readings span roughly 19 degrees Fahrenheit in January to 90 in July. The extremes are minus 27 in January 1977 and 114 in July 2012. The city sits in Climate Zone 4A under the International Energy Conservation Code, so heating and cooling equipment gets used hard. An old unit or a stained ceiling will show up on any inspection report.

Some owners skip the roof repair and sell to a buyer who accepts the damage.

Which city rental rules touch an Edwardsville landlord who sells?

Edwardsville operates a Rental Registration and Inspection Program, and each rental must be registered annually. The 2026 form sets $40 for a single-family or mobile home building, $60 for a duplex and $25 per unit in buildings of three or more. Registrations received after January 31 pay a $75 late fee, a first re-inspection is free, and later ones cost $75.

The sale itself triggers paperwork. The form says an ownership change requires deregistration, with Property Sold as one of the listed reasons, and a purchaser has 30 days from taking title to register. The city also refuses registration to any owner with unpaid fees or fines. Contact rentalregistration@cityofedwardsville.com or 618-307-1501 with questions.

  • File the deregistration once the sale closes so city records name the right owner.
  • Pay any fees or fines owed to the city before the closing date.
  • Tell the buyer which units have tenants, because inspections are requested before occupancy.
  • Smoke detectors are required in each sleeping room, within 15 feet of sleeping rooms and on every level, and carbon monoxide detectors within 15 feet of sleeping rooms.

How does the Madison County Recorder process an Edwardsville deed?

The Madison County Recorder handles deeds for Edwardsville. Its page lists the state charge at $.50 per $500 of taxable consideration, or part thereof, and the county charge at $.25 per $500, or part thereof. A PTAX declaration or a statement of exemption has to accompany the deed, and the exemptions sit in 35 ILCS 200/31-45.

The office has a few rules that catch do-it-yourself sellers. Every deed needs the buyer's name and mailing address for tax billing. A notarized Plat Act affidavit travels with it, and the permanent parcel number belongs on the document. If you pay by check, write the recording fee and the transfer tax on different checks. The Recorder's documents page prints no dollar amount for the recording fee, so ask the office for the current figure.

A closing agent can take over this paperwork, and you should read the transfer tax line on the settlement statement before signing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Edwardsville houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

When does Madison County bill property tax, and who pays at closing?

The Treasurer bills real estate tax in four installments. Bills for 2025 taxes came due in 2026 on July 9, September 9, October 9 and December 9. A late installment gains a 1.5 percent penalty for each 30 days it stays unpaid. Under 35 ILCS 200/20-15, a missing bill does not cancel the debt.

Illinois tax is paid after the year it covers, since taxes on one year's assessments are paid the next year. At closing, the settlement statement divides the bill, so ask for that split in writing. If taxes go unpaid they are sold at the annual tax sale, and redemption can run two to three years. A lien of that kind complicates any sale, so clear it first.

Assessment appeals go to the Madison County Board of Review, which accepts filings up to 30 days after assessments are published. The Treasurer's FAQ names general homestead, senior homestead, disabled veterans, returning veterans, disabled persons and senior freeze relief. Phone the Chief County Assessment Office to learn which apply to your parcel.

Should I gather permit records before selling in Edwardsville?

Yes, because buyers and their lenders ask about work done to the house. Edwardsville's building permit application covers new construction, remodels, garages, roofs, and electrical, plumbing and mechanical work, and it includes a line asking whether the property is a rental. The roofing section asks for an Illinois roofing license number.

An open permit or an unpermitted addition can stall a closing. Collect records for decks, finished basements, water heaters and furnaces before you list. Ask the city whether anything on your address remains open, and finish it before you sign a purchase contract.

Frequently asked questions

What if tenants live in my Edwardsville house?

A sale is still possible. The city requires owners to register rentals each year and to deregister when the property sells, so file the Property Sold deregistration after closing. The buyer registers within 30 days of taking ownership. Review the lease and deposit terms with your closing agent.

How much transfer tax will an Edwardsville seller see on the settlement statement?

The Recorder prints $.50 per $500 for the state and $.25 per $500 for Madison County, each on taxable consideration or part thereof. The PTAX declaration fixes the taxable amount, and your closing agent turns that into dollars for the statement.

Who records the deed on an Edwardsville home?

The Madison County Recorder. The deed arrives with a PTAX declaration or exemption statement, a notarized Plat Act affidavit, the parcel number and the grantee's tax billing address. Title companies usually submit the package.

How many times a year does Madison County bill property tax?

Four times. The Treasurer's schedule for 2026 ran from July through December, with a 1.5 percent monthly penalty on late installments. Its website shows what has been paid on your parcel.

Will a cash sale close faster than a listing in Edwardsville?

Often yes, since there is no marketing period, mortgage approval or repair haggling. County paperwork, payoff and title review still apply, so a clean title sets the real pace. Get a written payoff and a lien check before accepting any offer.

Why do people sell houses in Woodstock, Illinois?

Woodstock is the McHenry County seat, about 51 miles northwest of Chicago, and most owners who sell are moving closer to work, downsizing, settling an estate or leaving a rental behind. The city has a long memory for a town this far out. It began as Centerville, named for its position at the geographic center of the county, and was chosen as county seat on September 4, 1843. Settlers renamed it Woodstock in 1845 after a Vermont hometown, it became a village in 1852 and a city in 1873.

The town square, the Opera House and the old county courthouse anchor the historic district, which the National Trust for Historic Preservation named one of its Dozen Distinctive Destinations in 2007. In the early 1900s the city was known as Typewriter City, and workers here built more than half the world's typewriters by 1922. The old typewriter factory ran until 1970 and was later converted into lofts. Film fans know the square from Groundhog Day, shot in 1993.

That mix of older homes near downtown and newer subdivisions on the edges means two very different sales. A century-old house near the square may call for a roof or rewiring, while a newer one farther out tends to sell on location and school boundaries.

What do Woodstock's housing and income figures look like?

Woodstock has about 10,650 households, and nearly three in ten of them rent. The table gives the headline housing and income figures.

Which schools and commuter options help a Woodstock listing?

Woodstock Community Unit School District 200 serves the city and was formed in 1969. For many buyers, the school buildings and the train station matter as much as the house.

  • District 200 runs an early learning center (Verda Dierzen) and six elementary schools: Dean Street, Greenwood, Mary Endres, Olson, Prairiewood and Westwood.
  • Two middle schools, Northwood and Creekside, feed Woodstock High School and Woodstock North High School.
  • St. Mary Catholic grade school covers kindergarten through eighth grade in town, and many students go on to Marian Central Catholic High School.
  • Woodstock station is on Metra's Union Pacific Northwest Line, the second to last stop before Harvard, with 14 weekday trains to Chicago.

Name the train line and the school district in any listing. Cash buyers weigh the same things, plus the repair list.

What happens at the McHenry County Recorder when a Woodstock home sells?

The deed is recorded with the McHenry County Recorder, and a transfer declaration (PTAX-203 or the online MyDec) has to accompany it. The Recorder's office says a document that meets state requirements and comes with the right fee is recorded the same day it is received, and that it usually returns documents within about two working days. Call 815-334-4110 for fee questions.

One point helps sellers here: the Recorder states that no municipality in McHenry County charges a separate transfer tax. So the Woodstock closing does not add a city stamp like those in some other Illinois towns. The state still expects a signed declaration to travel with every deed (35 ILCS 200/31-25).

Before closing, search for liens. The Recorder will help you look for liens and foreclosures filed against a property, and the County Treasurer (815-334-4072) and County Clerk (815-334-4242) handle questions on property sold for back taxes. The Assessor's office at 815-334-4290 can confirm who owns a parcel.

Do Woodstock's building permit rules matter before a sale?

Yes, because open or missing permits show up in a buyer's inspection. Woodstock's Building and Planning staff issue permits for work such as roofs, furnaces, water heaters, decks, fences, garages, sheds, solar panels, plumbing and electrical work, and for windows or doors when the opening changes size. Driveways and aprons need zoning approval only.

  • Express permits are generally issued in 3 to 5 business days, and typical review for other projects is 10 to 15 business days.
  • Most building permits last 120 days, while a permit for a new principal building or an addition lasts 12 months, with a written extension possible for good cause.
  • A final inspection is required before a building is used or occupied, and inspections need at least 48 hours' notice at 815-338-4305.

Did an earlier owner finish the basement or add a deck without a permit? Speak with Building and Planning before you list. A cash purchaser may overlook it, but a lender's appraiser might not.

Does Woodstock regulate rental houses?

Yes. Title 4, Chapter 13 of the Woodstock City Code sets up a performance-based Property Management Program. An owner who is found liable for two or more code violations in one rental unit within six months must register every unit they own, at no fee, and return the form within 30 days. An owner found liable for four or more violations in a single unit within 12 months needs a city permit to keep renting.

That permit depends on interior and exterior inspections. The unit that triggered it is inspected, and so are all of an owner's units if they own eight or fewer in the city. For larger owners the city inspects the original unit plus up to 25% of the rest. The first inspection and re-inspection are free, and a third and later ones cost $40 each. The requirement ends after twelve months without another finding of liability.

If you are selling a rental, ask Building and Planning whether the property is under the program. An investor who buys it will want to know before offering.

What are the options for selling a Woodstock house fast?

A quick sale is realistic when the house is priced to match the repairs it needs and the paperwork is clean. You have three paths, and the right one depends on condition and timing.

  • Agent listing: you wait on showings, an appraisal and the buyer's financing. It suits a sound house near the Square.
  • Owner sale: no commission, though the contract, disclosure and showings land on you.
  • Cash purchase: no financing step and few repair requests. It fits estate houses, tenant-occupied homes and houses with code violations.

Get any offer in writing and compare the net after repairs, taxes and carrying cost.

Does the City of Woodstock charge its own transfer tax?

No. The McHenry County Recorder states that no municipality in the county charges a separate transfer tax. You still file a transfer declaration (PTAX-203 or MyDec) with the deed, and the recorder's fees apply.

Which office records a Woodstock deed?

Record it with the McHenry County Recorder. Call 815-334-4110 with fee questions. Documents that meet state requirements and have the correct fee are recorded the same day they are received.

Is a permit needed for a new roof or furnace in Woodstock?

Yes. The city's permit list includes roofs, furnace installs or replacements, water heaters, fences, decks and sheds. Express permits generally take 3 to 5 business days, so apply early if you want the work finished before listing.

What if my Woodstock rental has had code violations?

Registration becomes mandatory after two or more violations in one unit within six months, and a permit with inspections is required after four or more within 12 months. Registration is free, and the first inspection and re-inspection carry no charge.

Who can tell me whether property taxes are owed on a Woodstock parcel?

Ask the McHenry County Treasurer at 815-334-4072 about unpaid tax and the County Clerk at 815-334-4242 about property sold for back taxes. The Recorder's office points sellers to those two offices for tax sale questions.

How can a South Elgin owner sell a house?

Three routes lead to a closing: an agent listing, a private sale, or an as-is cash purchase. Each one finishes with a recorded Kane County deed, and the real contrast is the calendar and the repair bill you accept along the way.

  • Agent listing: staging, photos and showings come first, and the closing date follows the buyer's lender.
  • Private sale: you price the house, field the calls and negotiate, usually with an attorney reading the contract.

Cash fits a house that needs a roof or furnace, an inherited property nobody lives in, or a move with a hard date. A listing may bring a stronger price on a tidy home, at the cost of weeks of preparation.

Where is South Elgin, and how fast did it grow?

South Elgin is a Kane County village in the Fox River Valley, built along both banks of the river. Elgin borders it on the north and Bartlett on the east. The village covers about 7.26 square miles, and its ZIP code is 60177.

Early settlers called the place Clintonville, after James Clinton. The name South Elgin took over in 1897. The decennial counts tell the rest: 7,474 people in 1990, 16,100 in 2000, 21,985 in 2010 and 23,865 in 2020. The Bureau's mid-2025 estimate of 25,656 sits 7.5 percent above its April 2020 base.

That doubling between 1990 and 2000 means much of the housing is newer than in older river towns such as Elgin itself. Check your own house's age, roof and mechanicals with a local agent, because those details drive price more than any village-wide average.

  • District 303 spans about 57 square miles of the Fox River Valley.

Two freight rail lines also pass through, one running toward Rockford and one toward Sioux City. If your house sits close to a crossing, expect buyers to raise noise during a showing.

Which repairs need a village permit in South Elgin?

Most building work requires a permit from Community Development at Village Hall, 10 N. Water Street. The office answers at (847) 741-3894 and keeps weekday hours from 8:30 a.m. until 5:00 p.m.

  • Staff review of small projects takes 5 to 10 business days; projects sent to an outside consultant take three weeks.
  • A permit lasts six months, with a further six months available for an extension fee.
  • Call by 4:00 p.m. to book an inspection for the following day.
  • The village exempts painting, wallpaper, tile, carpet, tree trimming and broken window repair.
  • Construction noise is limited to the hours between 7 a.m. and 9 p.m.
  • A radon control system needs its own permit, and renovation of any building from before 1978 falls under the federal lead-based paint repair rule the village page links to.

The village enforces the 2024 International Building Code and International Residential Code with local amendments, alongside the 2023 National Electrical Code. A contractor who pulls permits for you will know which edition applies.

The village's own permit FAQ says an informed realtor or lawyer may tell a client to hold off on a purchase until permits and inspections are on file. The same page says it is unlawful to sell, transfer, mortgage or lease a structure served with a compliance order. A finished basement or deck built without paperwork is worth a call before you list. Who assesses a South Elgin home, and how do appeals work?

Township assessors set the starting values, Elgin Township or St. Charles Township for South Elgin parcels, and the county equalizes them. Kane's assessment office describes the base as 33.33 percent of fair cash value on January 1, drawn from three earlier years of sales.

Start any dispute with your assessor. When that fails, the Kane County Board of Review takes complaints for 30 days after the township roll is published in a local newspaper. Recognized grounds are wrong property data, a value above one third of market value, and a figure out of line with comparable houses. The state appeal board has held that the size of the bill or of a yearly jump does not qualify.

  • General Homestead: Kane's page prints $8,000 as the cut to equalized assessed value on an owner's main residence.
  • Senior Citizen: the same $8,000 figure, available once the owner turns 65 by the last day of the assessment year.
  • Forms: call 630-208-3818 or use the online portal.

The Kane treasurer's home page says payment season for 2025 taxes ended Friday, October 23, 2026, and that anyone whose taxes were sold redeems them through the County Clerk's tax extension office at 630-232-5964. Your title company will tell you how taxes are divided at the table.

What does a South Elgin closing record and tax?

The deed goes to the Kane County Recorder, normally filed by the title agent or attorney. Section 31-15 of the Property Tax Code (35 ILCS 200/31-15) puts the state's levy on a sale at 50 cents per $500 of value. The recorder collects it through revenue stamps, and the filing reaches the Department of Revenue through MyDec.

Call the Recorder for the county's share and the recording fee. Call the village to learn whether any local stamp or final water reading applies. A title company can usually settle both questions in one phone call, and the numbers will appear on your settlement statement.

Look for your plat of survey in your purchase papers. The village notes that surveys are generally part of the closing set, and permit staff request one with many applications.

Must I fix my South Elgin house before it sells?

Illinois does not make a seller repair a house first. Open permits and unresolved compliance orders can still stall a closing, and an as-is buyer will price the defects in while a listing buyer may ask you to fix them.

Elgin Township or St. Charles Township, depending on the parcel. The village permit page names both, and the Kane County assessment office can confirm yours from the parcel number.

Can a South Elgin house with a code violation be sold?

Only with care. The village says it is unlawful to sell or transfer a structure that has been served with a compliance order, so call Community Development at (847) 741-3894 to learn how the order can be cleared or passed on to a buyer.

How much is the Illinois transfer stamp on a sale here?

Fifty cents per $500 of value goes to the state, paid through the recorder. County and village charges are separate, so have the recorder and your title company list every line before closing.

Where does Belvidere sit, and what is its housing history?

Belvidere is the Boone County seat in far northern Illinois, about 12 miles east of Rockford and roughly 75 miles northwest of downtown Chicago. The Kishwaukee River runs through it, and the city is known as the City of Murals for the public art in its North State Street and South State Street historic districts, both federally listed historic districts. It as an industrial community surrounded by farms.

The first European American settlers came in 1835 and named the spot Elysian Fields; the city later took the name of Belvidere, Virginia. A railroad built south of the river in 1851 pulled the business district across the water, which is why downtown sits on the south side today. Downtown grew up along that rail line, so a house near State Street may be well over a century old, and buyers of older homes tend to ask about electrical service, roofs and basements.

Severe weather is part of local history. A tornado on April 21, 1967 killed 24 people and demolished over 100 homes, and an EF1 tornado hit the city on March 31, 2023. Keep roof invoices, storm-damage repair records and any insurance claim paperwork, since buyers and insurers ask for them.

How large is Belvidere's owner market?

The Census Bureau counted 25,339 residents in April 2020 and estimates 25,462 for July 1, 2025, a 0.5 percent gain. That steady count, rather than a boom or a slump, means prices follow condition and interest rates more than population swings.

With owners holding 70.9 percent of housing, most Belvidere sales are family homes rather than investor stock.

How do jobs and the Stellantis plant affect Belvidere home sales?

The Belvidere Assembly Plant, built in the mid-1960s, has long been the city's best-known employer. It built the Dodge Neon until 2005 and later the Jeep Cherokee, and Stellantis idled it in February 2023. Under the 2023 UAW settlement the company agreed to reopen it, so plant news moves buyer confidence in a way few other single sites do. A local agent can tell you how the latest announcements are affecting showings on your street.

  • Other manufacturers: Dean Foods and General Mills operate plants along the Kishwaukee River, and General Mills has announced a large distribution center in a newly annexed southwest area.
  • Education and training: Rock Valley College opened an Advanced Technology Center in northwest Belvidere on March 30, 2022.
  • Logistics: Walmart announced a cold storage facility project in June 2023.
  • Commute: Rockford's RMTD runs Route 24 bus service linking Belvidere and Rockford.

Sellers who need to move quickly often compare a listing timeline with a direct cash purchase, where there is no mortgage approval to wait on.

Which Belvidere school districts and amenities will buyers ask about?

Belvidere Community Unit School District 100 serves the city. Its two high schools are Belvidere High School and Belvidere North High School, its middle schools are South and Central, and its elementary schools include Lincoln, Perry, Meehan, Caledonia and Seth Whitman. Washington Academy is the district's STEM school, and the Everest Alternative Program is also listed. Buyers with children will want to confirm which attendance zone the street falls in.

Downtown draws buyers with the Boone County Museum of History, the Carnegie-built Ida Public Library (opened in 1913) and festivals such as Heritage Days. If your house is walkable to State Street, say so in the listing or offer conversation.

What does Belvidere's Building Department require for permits and repairs?

The City of Belvidere Building Department permits and inspects construction and enforces the zoning and property maintenance codes. It sits at 401 Whitney Boulevard, Suite 300, takes calls at 815-547-7177 and keeps counter hours of 8 a.m. until 5 p.m. on weekdays. Call before starting a pre-sale project, because the city says some work needs a permit and online applications cover many permit types.

  • The city adopted the 2021 International codes (building, residential, fire, mechanical, fuel gas, existing building and energy) by Ordinance 703H on November 19, 2024, effective for permit applications after January 1, 2025.
  • State law has required carbon monoxide alarms in existing and new residences since January 1, 2007, installed within 15 feet of each bedroom.
  • Projects the city lists as commonly needing permits include siding, windows and doors, remodeling, additions, central air, plumbing, finished basements, and driveways, approaches, sidewalks and patios.
  • Landmarked buildings face added construction rules through the Historic Preservation Commission.
  • Work in the public right-of-way, such as curb cuts, sidewalks, or water and sewer line repairs, needs a Public Works permit at 401 Whitney Boulevard, Suite 200.

Ask the Building Department for the permit history on your address before you list. An unfinished permit can surprise a buyer's inspector, while a cash buyer will usually take the house as-is and handle it afterward.

How are deeds recorded in Boone County after a Belvidere sale?

Boone County's recording page lists a standard document at $65.00, a non-standard document at $67.00 and an exempt standard document at $47.00 in a schedule effective August 1, 2018. The same page notes the statewide Rental Housing Support Fee increase that took effect July 1, 2023, so ask the office for the total before you send a check. The office takes cash and checks, wants a return envelope with postage, and does not give legal advice.

Since September 11, 2023, the county accepts transfer declarations only through the state's MyDec service, with the status set to closing completed before documents are submitted. A deed also needs a Plat Act Affidavit when it uses a metes and bounds description, designates roadway easements, or divides about five acres or less. The page lists Simplifile, CSC and EPN as e-recording providers, and a title company usually files for you.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Belvidere houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How does Boone County assess, appeal and bill property tax?

Township assessors value every parcel as it stood on January 1, aiming for one-third of market value, and the Supervisor of Assessments equalizes townships to 33.33 percent. Taxpayers can file a complaint with the Board of Review within 30 days after publication of assessment changes or by September 10, whichever is later, on the county's forms with a market-value opinion and evidence. Acceptable evidence includes a closing statement from a recent purchase, at least three comparable sales within a year of the assessment date, a recent appraisal, or income and expense statements for investment property. A decision can be appealed to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board in Springfield within 30 days.

Bills come from the Boone County Treasurer the year after the assessment year, in two equal installments that the county describes as targeted for June and September. Treasurer contact: 1212 Logan Avenue, Suite 104, 815-544-2666. Boone County's exemptions page lists the general homestead exemption (an increase over 1977 value up to $6,000 of equalized value), a $5,000 senior exemption, a $2,000 disabled persons reduction, the senior freeze, and veterans' exemptions. If you are selling, confirm with the Treasurer which installment is paid and how the closing agent will prorate the rest.

Frequently asked questions

Is a tornado damage history a problem when selling in Belvidere?

It can be, mainly if repairs were incomplete or undocumented. The city was hit by an F4 tornado on April 21, 1967 and an EF1 on March 31, 2023, so buyers and inspectors often ask for roof and structural repair records. Gather permits and invoices, or consider an as-is sale if records are thin.

Is a transfer declaration required for a Boone County sale?

Yes. Boone County has accepted declarations only through the Illinois Department of Revenue's MyDec service since September 11, 2023, and the status must say closing completed before recording. Your title company or attorney normally completes it with you.

How much does recording a deed cost in Boone County?

The county's base schedule, effective August 1, 2018, lists $65.00 for a standard document, $67.00 for non-standard and $47.00 for government-exempt documents. The page also notes a Rental Housing Support Fee increase effective July 1, 2023, so confirm the current total with the recorder.

When can I appeal a Belvidere property assessment?

Within 30 days after assessment changes are published, or by September 10, whichever is later. File a Board of Review complaint with your estimate of January 1 market value and supporting evidence such as three comparable sales or a recent appraisal.

Does Belvidere require a city inspection before closing?

Ask the Building Department at 815-547-7177 about open permits or code violations on your address before you list. Those items can affect a buyer's lender or inspector, and the department is the city's compliance office for the property maintenance and zoning codes.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a West Chicago, IL sale

Selling in West Chicago?
We buy West Chicago houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

How does a West Chicago home sale differ from other suburbs?

A West Chicago sale has one local step that most Illinois suburbs lack: the city must approve the structure before any deed is recorded. The city paperwork is identical for a listed sale, a private deal or a buyer paying cash for a property in any condition. Plan for it early, because the inspection is valid for six months and the city asks for scheduling at least two months before closing.

The city sits on the western edge of DuPage County, about 32 miles from downtown Chicago, with Illinois Route 59 running north and south and Routes 38 and 64 running east and west. Buyers who commute use the Metra station on Main Street or drive to I-88 and I-355. Commute options belong in any description of the house, because buyers ask about them first.

What does West Chicago's inspector look for before a sale?

The Community Development Department inspects the structure for basic maintenance and life safety, and no Deed Certification Number is issued without an approved inspection unless an exemption applies. A visit takes about 30 minutes and happens Monday through Friday between 9 a.m. and 3 p.m. Vacant lots are inspected too.

  • Smoke detectors must be present and working.
  • Ground fault interrupters must be installed where the checklist calls for them.
  • Stair railings must meet the minimum standard.
  • The structure must show adequate property maintenance, and vacant parcels are checked for tall grass, weeds and garbage.

The fee is a $100.00 base charge plus $0.12 per square foot, using the square footage the township supplies to the city. A vacant parcel adds a flat $20.00. If the house fails, the seller can fix the items and request a re-inspection at no added charge, or sell as-is and leave the repairs to the buyer.

What steps must a West Chicago seller finish before the deed records?

The city lays the steps out in order, and skipping one stalls the recording. The table summarizes them from the city's Property Transactions page.

Seller steps on the City of West Chicago Property Transactions page
OrderStepDetail
1City inspection$100.00 base plus $0.12 per square foot; valid six months
2Final water and sewer readingCall Finance at least 2 working days before closing
3Clear city balancesInspection fees, water bills, parking tickets, ordinance violations, liens, waste services
4Deed Certification NumberForm signed by a seller or agent, presented at 475 Main Street

The number must be attached to the deed when the title is recorded. Payment at City Hall can be made by cash, check, or debit or credit card.

Certain transfers skip the inspection fee but still need a certification number. They include new construction, deeds that secure or release a debt, corrective deeds with no added consideration, and a sale where the occupant does not change. A final water reading is still required for those exempt deeds, and the city takes up to five business days to decide an exemption.

What happens if a West Chicago house is sold as-is?

When a seller declines to repair failed items, the buyer signs a Letter of Intent Agreement and posts a $1,600.00 bond with the Community Development Department. The buyer then has 90 days to finish repairs and pass an inspection, and one free 90-day extension is available if requested in person before the deadline. After an approved inspection the city refunds $1,500.00 within two to three weeks, because it keeps a $100.00 administrative fee.

This rule shapes cash offers on rough houses. A buyer who plans renovations can still close, but the bond and the 90-day clock are part of the buyer's cost, so ask any purchaser how they handle the city's requirements before you sign.

How do West Chicago's housing numbers look?

West Chicago has a young, family-heavy housing stock. The Census Bureau counts 7,459 households with 3.35 people each, with owners living in 70.9% of the homes (2020 to 2024 figures). Typical West Chicago values sit at $336,800, rent at $1,469 a month, and household income at $99,927. The July 2025 population estimate is 25,296, down 1.3% from the 2020 base.

  • Median monthly owner costs run $2,428 with a mortgage and $1,035 without one.
  • The Census Bureau finds 92.2% of residents stayed at one address over the prior year, a sign of low turnover.
  • The city covers 15.38 square miles of land, a density of 1,665.8 residents for each of them at the 2020 count.

Who handles West Chicago property tax at closing?

West Chicago is in DuPage County, which bills property tax in arrears: the 2025 bills were mailed April 29, 2026, with installments due June 1 and September 1, 2026, and both dates have passed. The county treasurer's page lists the general homestead exemption and the senior exemption at $8,000 each, so check your bill for both. If a mortgage servicer pays your tax, a yellow box on the bill says so and you should not pay twice.

The title company splits the unpaid tax between seller and buyer on the settlement statement, and the state taxes the transfer itself at a half dollar per $500 of declared value. Ask the DuPage County recorder what the county adds. Illinois also requires a seller of one to four units to deliver a finished disclosure report ahead of contract signing (765 ILCS 77/20).

What should a landlord know before selling a West Chicago rental?

West Chicago requires a Rental Property License for residential landlords and annual rental inspections tied to the International Property Maintenance Code standard. Anyone selling a rental should confirm that your license and inspection record are current, because open city items surface at the same Community Development counter that handles the sale inspection. A sale where the occupant or tenant does not change can qualify for the inspection fee exemption, so bring the signed deed to the Director of Community Development and ask for a ruling before closing.

What is West Chicago like for sellers and buyers?

The place began as a railroad junction. The Galena and Chicago Union reached the site in 1849 and the Aurora Branch crossed it in 1850, which made it the first railroad junction west of Chicago. It was platted as Junction in 1855, incorporated as the Village of Turner in 1873 and renamed West Chicago in 1896. The 2020 census counted 25,614 residents.

Local employers include Jel Sert and Ball Horticultural Company, and the city lists West Chicago Elementary School District 33 and Community High School District 94 among its larger employers. DuPage Airport sits inside the city limits, and the West Chicago Prairie Forest Preserve and the Illinois Prairie Path give buyers trail access. The park district manages more than 390 acres across 13 sites, led by 125-acre Reed-Keppler Park.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a city inspection to sell my house in West Chicago?

Yes, except for the exempt transfer types the city lists. Without an approved inspection the city issues no Deed Certification Number, and the visit costs $100.00 plus $0.12 per square foot. It stays valid for six months, so schedule it about two months before closing.

Can I sell a West Chicago house that fails the inspection?

Yes. You can repair the items and get a free re-inspection, or sell as-is. With an as-is sale the buyer posts a $1,600.00 bond and has 90 days to finish repairs and pass.

Who schedules the final water reading in West Chicago?

The seller does. Contact the city's Finance Department at least 2 working days before closing, pay the unbilled water and sewer use, and clear any other city balances before the certification number is issued.

Does West Chicago charge a local transfer tax?

The Property Transactions page describes inspection fees and a Deed Certification Number but no local transfer tax rate. The state's share is a half dollar on every $500 declared, and the DuPage County recorder can tell you what the county adds.

When are DuPage County property tax bills due?

Illinois bills a year behind, and the 2025 bills carried installment dates of June 1 and September 1, 2026. Both have passed. Your closing statement splits the unpaid portion between seller and buyer.

What does the Alton housing market look like?

Alton is a Mississippi River city in Madison County, about 18 miles north of St. Louis, with a low-priced housing market. Owners value their homes at a median $103,700 in the Census five-year survey ending 2024, and 59.9% of homes are occupied by their owners, so a good part of the market is rental.

Census staff counted 25,676 residents in 2020 and estimated 25,013 for July 1, 2025, a 2.6% drop from their base. Most of Alton rises steeply from the waterfront onto bluffs, which gives many streets river views and leaves low-lying blocks exposed to river floods. The city was laid out as a river trading town in January 1818 and later grew around grain, glass, steel and box board.

  • Typical monthly gross rent: $1,015
  • Median household income: $54,568
  • Share of residents in poverty: 21.0%
  • Households: 10,714, averaging 2.30 people
  • Mean commute: 22.7 minutes

How do Alton's bluffs, floods and old streets affect a house sale?

They affect inspections, insurance and buyer expectations more than any other local factor. The city's history notes that the lower levels of Alton flood, that high-water marks are painted on the grain silos near the riverfront, and that the flood of 1993 was the worst of the last century. The city's own website advertises an open house on planned flood mitigation, so ask the city about any project near your block.

Much of the older housing is Victorian Queen Anne, with brick commercial buildings downtown and an unusually high number of brick-paved streets left over from the area's brick factories. Buyers near the river will ask about the flood zone, so gather any elevation certificate or flood insurance history before you list.

Which Alton landmarks and districts draw buyers?

The riverfront, the historic core and the bluff-top residential streets each attract a different buyer. The seventh Lincoln-Douglas debate took place in downtown Alton on October 15, 1858, and the Lyman Trumbull House is a national historic monument. The city has a Historic Preservation Commission, an Appearance Review Commission and a Building Board of Appeals that work alongside the planning staff.

  • The Meeting of the Great Rivers National Scenic Byway and the Great River Road follow the riverfront and the bikeway north of town.
  • Lock and Dam 26 is the newest and busiest lock complex on the main channel of the Mississippi, and the National Great Rivers Museum runs tours of it.
  • The city site lists 19 parks, a marina and a fire department ISO rating of 2.
  • Visitors come for antique shopping, the Argosy Casino and bald eagle watching in winter.

The planning department also administers the Riverfront TIF District and the Hunterstown TIF District and coordinates with Madison County on the Riverbend Enterprise Zone. A property inside one of those boundaries may qualify for redevelopment incentives, so ask the Planning and Development office at 618.463.3500 whether your parcel is inside one.

Which schools and transit options serve Alton?

Alton Community Unit School District 11 serves the bulk of the city, while a small eastern section sits in Bethalto Consolidated Unit School District 8. Alton High School and Alton Middle School are the public secondary schools, and Alton Middle School enrolls roughly 1,500 students and is billed as the largest middle school in the state. Marquette Catholic High School is the private option, and the former Shurtleff College campus is now home to the Southern Illinois University School of Dental Medicine.

Alton station carries Amtrak's Lincoln Service north to Chicago Union Station and south to St. Louis. Madison County Transit buses run in the city with hubs downtown and at the Amtrak station.

What does Alton Code Enforcement require when a house changes occupants?

Alton's Code Enforcement Department performs universal residential occupancy inspections, so a change of occupant can trigger a visit even when ownership stays the same. The department also issues building, demolition, electrical, plumbing, signage, occupancy and agent authorization permits and reviews plans for renovations.

  • Since February 1, 2015, the city has refused to schedule an occupancy inspection until the form names every person moving into the dwelling.
  • For adults the form needs a full name, date of birth and driver's license or state ID number. For children it needs a full name and date of birth.
  • The department cites weeds, junk, trash, derelict vehicles and exterior or interior property maintenance violations, and it sends unresolved citations to court.
  • The city also inspects fire-damaged structures and handles demolition proceedings.

Before you list, call the Code Enforcement Office at 618.463.3500 and ask whether the property has open citations or an unclosed permit. A buyer of the house in any condition inherits those issues, so settling them first keeps the closing date steady.

How does Madison County bill property tax on an Alton house?

Madison County collects in four installments. Bills for the 2025 tax year went out the week of June 9, 2026, and mobile home tax came due August 31.

2026 installment dates published by the Madison County Treasurer
InstallmentDue date in 2026
FirstJuly 9
SecondSeptember 9
ThirdOctober 9
FourthDecember 9

Source: Madison County Treasurer, Frequently Asked Questions.

  • A 1.5% penalty attaches to a late installment every 30 days, and taxes still unpaid go into the annual tax sale.
  • After a tax sale an owner can redeem for two to three years through the County Clerk, paying the entire amount owed.
  • About 220 taxing districts levy against Madison County property, and the assessed value is one third of fair market value.
  • The FAQ lists a $6,000 general homestead exemption, a $5,000 senior homestead exemption, $5,000 returning veterans and $2,000 disabled persons exemptions.
  • The treasurer's FAQ says Madison County does not apply the Property Tax Extension Limitation Law that caps increases in other counties.

Call the Treasurer's Office at (618) 692-6260 for a duplicate bill. State law makes the tax due even when the bill never arrives.

How can an Alton owner challenge an assessment?

A written complaint goes to the Madison County Board of Review, and it is due 30 days after the assessments are published. Section 16-55(d) of the Property Tax Code sets that deadline, and the county treasurer's FAQ repeats it. Talk first with the township or county assessor, since the Chief County Assessment Office at (618) 692-6270 can explain how the value was set.

You will need evidence that the property is overassessed, such as recent sales of similar Alton houses, an appraisal or documented condition problems. The Board of Review can be reached at (618) 692-6210. An appeal changes the assessed value only, because the tax rate comes from the local taxing districts.

What does the Madison County Recorder need to record an Alton deed?

The Recorder will not accept a deed without an Illinois Department of Revenue transfer declaration (PTAX) or a statement of exemption. The state collects 50 cents on each $500 of taxable consideration under Section 31-10 of the Property Tax Code, and Madison County adds 25 cents on each $500.

  • Each deed carries the grantee's name and address for tax billing, with a Plat Act affidavit attached.
  • A permanent parcel number is required on documents that affect a transfer, by county board resolution.
  • The preparer's name and address must appear on the instrument itself.
  • When paying by check, the recording fee and the transfer tax are paid separately.

The recorder's list of documents includes executor's, administrator's, guardian's and trustee's deeds, so a house sold through an estate is recorded with the same declaration and parcel number requirements.

Which selling routes fit an Alton house?

Alton owners can hire an agent, go it alone, or sell outright to a buyer who takes whatever shape the house is in. A listing works best on a clean, move-in ready house in a good school boundary. A private sale suits an owner who already has a buyer lined up. The third route suits a vacant, inherited or damaged house, because the buyer accepts what is there and the closing date can be set around the occupancy inspection and the flood or code questions described above.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

How many property tax installments does Madison County have?

Four. For 2025 taxes payable in 2026 they were due July 9, September 9, October 9 and December 9, with mobile home tax due August 31. The Treasurer's Office can give you the schedule on the next bill.

What is the penalty for a late Madison County installment?

A 1.5% penalty is added the day after the deadline and again every 30 days. Delinquency notices go out about a month before the tax sale, and unpaid taxes are sold to a tax buyer.

Does Alton require an occupancy inspection when I sell?

Alton conducts universal residential occupancy inspections, and its policy requires information on every person who will live in the dwelling. Ask Code Enforcement at 618.463.3500 whether your sale or the next tenant triggers one.

How much is the Illinois transfer tax on an Alton sale?

The state rate is 50 cents on each $500 of declared value, and Madison County adds 25 cents on each $500. The Recorder collects both at recording.

When must an Alton assessment complaint be filed?

The filing period is 30 days from publication of the assessments, and the complaint goes to the Madison County Board of Review. Call (618) 692-6210 to confirm how the board takes filings.
